**Why.** The two failures are fixtures that the merged law changes made
stale. Neither is a defect in the posted G-code or in the refusal. No
assert is relaxed and no refusal is made wider.

**Considered and dropped.**
- *Exempt a stock-source chamfer from the wall law.* It would make the
  old fixture pass. It would also post again a cone that rides a line
  that is no edge. Dropped.
- *A zero-degree tilt.* It would pass, but the test would not exercise a
  turned operation frame any more. Dropped.
- *Compare `ra` and `rb` with a tolerance in `arc_chords`.* A circle would
  then keep the old chord count. But it changes motion code under the
  safety floor in a crate that #2483 does not touch, and the new chords
  are not wrong: they are only one more. Dropped from this PR; filed as
  #2520 (P7).
- *Write the whole golden again from the Windows run.* It brings many
  last-digit changes that are inside the compare tolerance and are not
  part of the cause. Dropped.

**Follow-ups.**
- `arc_chords` decides by an exact float compare (`ra != rb`), so the
  chord count of a circular arc depends on float noise in its two radii.
  Filed as #2520.
- The wall-law refusal says "would ride into the part" also when the
  source is the stock and no part is near. The text could name the stock.
  Wording only (P7), filed as #2521.

**Cost to change later.** Low. The golden is generated output. The test
constant `MID` is local to the one test.

## #2496 - A hole wider than its drill is named, and the post is not held

- **Decided:** a Drill op names each Z hole wider than its Drill-kind tool by more than `DRILL_SIZE_TOL` (0.1 mm on the diameter). The names show in two places:
  - Detect holes keeps the hole and names it in `DetectedHoles::undersize` (MCP `undersize`, the GUI status line).
  - Generate adds one `Warning::DrillUndersize` for each such hole, at its first cutting move (MCP finding kind `drill_undersize`).
  - **Why:** the drill makes its own diameter, so such a hole comes out undersize. No other law saw it: the containment law judges a cut into the part, never material left in a hole.
- **Decided:** the warning is advisory, like `Scallop`, `ProbeSearch` and `SinkerFinishOrder`. It does not hold the post.
  - **Why:** a pilot drill is a valid plan (the maintainer's triage on the issue: "a named warning that the user can accept is better than a silent skip"). The part size is wrong but nothing gouges or collides, so the user decides.
  - **Dropped:** skipping the hole at Detect holes, as Bore does (#1556). That makes a pilot drill impossible from Detect holes.
  - **Dropped:** a refusal at generate. The same reason.
- **Decided:** the law reads only a Drill-kind tool, in a cycle that drills to size: Auto, Drill, Peck and Ream. It reads only the mill's Z holes.
  - **Why:** a spot dimple, a tap (its hole is the tap drill's, by design) and a bore cycle (sized by the slide) make a hole of another size. Other tool kinds in a Drill op (a chamfer mill, a boring bar) are not drills.
  - **Not changed:** the turret's radial holes. The issue is a mill case; a radial follow-up can use the same `undersize_holes`.
- **Decided:** `DRILL_SIZE_TOL` is 0.1 mm on the diameter, with a float slack of 1e-6 mm.
  - **Why:** a twist drill cuts up to about a tenth over its size. The project's own matched fixtures model a hole that much over its drill: `drilling_axial` has a 4 mm drill in a 4.1 mm hole, and calls it "a matched axial drill".
  - **Dropped:** 0.05 mm (the first try). It named the 4.1 mm hole of that matched fixture, and the quick gate failed.
- **Not changed:** a hole narrower than the drill. That is a cut into the wall, and the solid law holds the post with a `Gouge` (pinned by `a_hole_narrower_than_the_drill_is_held_as_a_gouge_not_named_undersize`). The hole-wall excuse is capped at the facet sagitta, so it does not hide that cut.
- **Note:** the GUI's `CommandKind::DetectedHoles` field `skipped` is renamed `notes`. It carries the skipped and the undersize sentences, which the one status line shows.

## #2505 - The tool kind rules name each kind, with no catch-all

- **Decided:** `Tool::kind_rule` in `crates/tools/src/tool_sanity.rs` has no `_ => None` arm. Its last arm names each kind that has no rule, or whose guarded rules held. A new `ToolKind` does not compile until this match names it.
  - **Why:** with the catch-all, a new kind passed the check with no kind rule, and no test saw it.
- **Decided:** the test list `KINDS` is guarded by `kind_slot`, an exhaustive match in the test file. A new kind does not compile until it gets a slot. Then `the_sweep_list_holds_each_kind_once` fails until `KINDS` holds it.
  - **Dropped:** a `ToolKind::ALL` constant in `crates/tools/src/tools.rs`. That file has 691 lines, over the 400-line limit. A hand-written constant also does not grow by itself when a kind is added.
- **Not changed:** the oracle `old_is_sane` keeps its `_ => true`. It is the old law, verbatim, and the sweep compares against it. The verdicts for the 18 kinds do not change.

## #2512 - Operation notes documentation and module boundaries

**Chosen:** Document the optional per-operation `notes` array returned by
MCP `generate` and `verify`, including its string values, omission when
empty and informational meaning. Extend `unreached.rs`'s module comment
to describe both the narrow-band check and the corner check, including
the stock-outline intersection and approximation-noise filter.

**Why:** These public descriptions lag the behavior added by #2503.
Explaining existing output needs no change to toolpaths or posting.
Leaving the descriptions unchanged was rejected because an agent could
miss uncut material even when generation and verification succeed.
Later wording changes cost a documentation edit and its contract checks.

**Chosen:** Retain `crates/app/src/operation/generate.rs` and
`crates/app/src/script/api.rs` in their current modules for this issue.
Both remain over the approximately 400-line limit; this decision records
the remaining structural debt rather than claiming that either was split.

**Why:** #2512 explicitly accepts a recorded decision for each owed item.
Splitting the generation dispatcher and its verification tail requires
careful handling of shared geometry, frame and verification state.
The script API has a clearer prospective seam between document/tool IO
and generation, verification and reporting, but extracting that seam is
separate behavior-preserving work. Broad extraction was considered and
dropped from this small documentation correction because it would widen
the code and validation scope without changing the documented output.
Changing this decision later costs scoped module extraction, import and
visibility updates, and the existing generation/script regression tests.

**Chosen:** Keep the stock-outline selection in
`generate.rs::run_job_arms`; continue passing its borrowed result to
`keep_law::narrow_noted`.

**Why:** The dispatcher owns the cached stock region, the optional local
frame and the temporary projected outline. It can reuse the cached
outline when no frame transform is needed and retain the temporary
outline for the duration of the note check otherwise. `keep_law` owns
the decision to attach band and corner notes, not generation-frame
preparation. Moving selection into `keep_law.rs` was considered and
dropped because it would expand that helper's context or require owned
geometry where a borrow currently suffices. Changing this later costs
an explicit input/lifetime interface and regression checks for stock
and model sources with and without a local frame.

## #2516 - Tab, Shift+Tab and Enter move between the value fields of the Properties pane

- **Found:** egui's own Tab already moved the focus, but in draw order over each focusable widget: from a value field it went to a group header (no visible focus mark), a combo or the action bar's buttons. Thus the focus seemed to leave the form. Enter committed the value and dropped the focus (egui's default).
- **Decided:** a value-field ring for the Properties pane (`crates/ui/src/egui_app/layout/field_ring.rs`).
  - The form seam's number helpers in `fields.rs` register each value field, with the group it sits in (`group_open` marks the group).
  - From a registered field, Tab moves to the next field and Shift+Tab to the previous one. The ring wraps at the two ends.
  - Enter commits the value to the draft (egui's DragValue, as before) and moves to the next field of the same group. After the group's last field the focus drops, as before.
  - From a combo, a checkbox or a button, egui's own order stays.
  - **Why:** the issue asks for the next value field, and the form seam is the one place that knows which widgets are value fields.
  - **Dropped:** making headers, combos and buttons not focusable. That breaks keyboard access to them.
  - **Dropped:** changing each page. The helpers cover the pages that use the form seam; a page that adds a raw `DragValue` is outside the ring (see #1122).
- **Decided:** the ring records the target at the end of the pane, asks for a repaint, and focuses the field when the next frame of the pane begins, before any widget draws.
  - **Why:** the field then GAINS the focus, so egui's DragValue selects its text, and a typed number replaces the old one, as after a click. egui also applies its own Shift+Tab at the start of the next frame (`id_next_frame`); the ring's request comes after it.
  - **Dropped:** a request at the end of the frame (the first try). On the next frame the field was not "gained", so its text was not selected and typing appended to the old number. Shift+Tab was also lost to `id_next_frame`.
- **Changed tests:** the `thread_hand_tests` helpers `edit_number` and `type_dip` click a field only when it is not focused. After Enter the next field already has the focus with its text selected; a click on a focused field only places the cursor.
- **Not changed:** the value reaches the document only through the page's command (Apply, `EditOperationParams`). Focus is ephemeral UI state and needs no command.

## #2523 - Keep example NC programs at LF

**Decision:** Use `examples/**/*.nc text eol=lf` for all example programs.
Replace the separate rule for the first 4-axis part.
Test a fresh Git checkout with `core.autocrlf=true` in an isolated repository.
The test copies the real attributes and all tracked example NC programs.

**Why:** The post writes LF bytes. The example tests compare those bytes
with the shipped programs. Git must preserve LF on Windows as well as Linux.
The glob covers programs directly in `examples/` and inside the catalog.
All four programs already have LF in the Git index, so no renormalization is needed.
The 4-axis tests read the already pinned program. The site tests read only
that program and use text reads.

**Dropped:** Separate rules for each program need updates for new examples.
A repository-wide `*.nc` rule or global line-ending rule changes files
outside this issue. Changing the byte comparisons would hide checkout errors.

**Cost to change later:** Edit one attribute rule and its checkout test.
No posted program or golden changes.

## #2533 - Restore the Drill test fixture

**Chosen:** Set `break_through_from` to `camcraft_app::drilling::BreakThroughFrom::Tip`
in the height advice fixture. Keep both machine transition tests. Add a test
that checks the mill default when the document has no machine.

**Why:** The fixture predates the new field. `settle_drill_break_through`
assigns `Tip` to legacy Drill operations from projects before v68. This
explicit value preserves the fixture's meaning and restores the test build.
The change does not change production behavior.

**Dropped:** `FullDiameter` is the default for new operations. It does not
preserve the legacy reference used by this fixture.

**Cost to change later:** Change one initializer if the fixture needs a
different reference.

## #1950 - the release gate skips three known-fail heavy tests by name (cut v0.24.0)

**Decided.** The release tier skips three `#[ignore]`d heavy tests that pin the
open, blocked issue #1950. The list is `xtask/src/known_fail.rs`:

- motion lib `machining2d::pocket_hsm::ring_tests::the_stock_ring_level_reaches_the_air_planner_with_the_stock`
- motion lib `machining2d::pocket_hsm::ring_tests::the_stock_ring_level_plans_adaptive_with_no_budget_note`
- app `pocket3d_hsm::the_users_whole_model_bore_roughs_adaptive_on_each_level`

The heavy lane of each target runs with `--exact --skip <test>`. The release
plan prints `SKIPPED (known fail, #1950): <test>` for each. Each test also gets
its own step that runs it alone. That step is ok only when libtest reports
that exact test as FAILED by its #1950 assert: the `panicked at` line names the
test's file, and the message holds the pinned text of that assert. A pass, a
renamed test, a compile error, a crash of the test binary, or a failure for
another reason (a planner panic, a gouge or collision warning, another assert)
is a FAIL. Before the steps
run, `gh issue view -R NeoTech/Camcraft` reads the state of each pinned issue,
with a 30 s limit. A closed issue fails the gate. The cut job has no
`GH_TOKEN`, so `gh` may not be able to read the issue on the cut runner. Then
the gate prints a "could not read" note, and the known-fail steps are the
guard.

**Why.** The cut gate of v0.24.0 (run 44362577581) was red on only these three
tests. They were added red on purpose in the #1950 work (16ffe937f, dc2e76926,
2026-11-15) and marked "expected red" in 716c9f08b and 83580bb2a. No merge of
this cycle made them fail, and v0.23.0 did not have them. The output is safe:
the planner refuses Adaptive with a note and cuts each level with Offset rings.
There is no lost pass, no missing level and no gouge. The fix of the planner is
open research that waits for a maintainer decision, so it cannot be in the cut.
The release tier runs every `--ignored` test, and before this change it had no
way to keep a pinned red test out.

**Dropped.**
- Re-record the expectation (assert the Offset-rings fallback): this hides the
  target of #1950. Refused by the coordinator's order.
- Delete the tests or remove their `#[ignore]`: this loses the pin.
- A `cfg` or feature gate on the tests: silent in the gate log, and nothing
  fails when the tests start to pass.
- Hold the cut until #1950 is solved: the issue is blocked on a maintainer
  decision, and its output is safe.

**Cost to change.** When #1950 is solved, the three known-fail steps go red.
Delete the three entries in `KNOWN_FAIL`. The mechanism stays for the next
blocked pin. Each new entry needs an open issue and a decision entry.

## v0.25.0 - decisions gathered at the cut

## #917 - kernel and geometry parity for the solidcore STEP path (PR B0)

PR B0 holds the items of #917 that we can pin under the app. PR B (the
switch of the app to solidcore) is stacked on it.

### The coordinate snap (`camcraft_kernel::mesh_weld`)

- **Decided.** Before the exact-position weld of the machining mesh, each
  coordinate goes through one rule:
  - The grid is 1e-3 mm (`SNAP_GRID_MM`). The window is 1e-9 mm
    (`SNAP_WINDOW_MM`).
  - `k = round(c / 1e-3)`, `g = k / 1000` (one IEEE 754 division).
  - If `|c - g| <= 1e-9`, the coordinate becomes `g + 0.0`. Otherwise it
    stays bit for bit. A coordinate that is not finite, or with
    `|k| > 9e15`, stays.
  - `+0.0` replaces `-0.0`. Equal inputs always give equal outputs.
- **Degenerate facets.** A triangle whose corners snap or weld onto a
  repeated vertex has no area. The weld drops it. The side count after
  the weld (`sides`) then refuses the mesh with `NotWatertight` if the
  drop opened a hole. No facet is moved past the window to close a gap.
- **Why.** The evaluator gives 20.000000000000004 for a face at Z 20. The
  app's flat-level and floor logic compares levels exactly, so a level
  read off the mesh by one ulp gives a wrong floor. The window is far under
  any machining tolerance (the smallest tolerance is a millionth of the
  body). A vertex moves at most one window in each axis, sqrt(3) x 1e-9
  = 1.73e-9 mm (`SNAP_MOVE_MM`), so the measured deviation stays true to
  1.73e-9 mm. The mesher adds `SNAP_MOVE_MM` to the measured deviation
  before it compares it with the tolerance, so the judged figure holds
  for the snapped mesh too (review of #2843).
- **Dropped.** A snap to the 1e-6 grid (it would move true model values
  such as 12.5000004). A relative window (a large part would move more).
  A snap after the weld (two near copies of one vertex then weld
  differently).
- **Pinned by** `the_snap_takes_the_last_bit_noise_off_a_grid_value`,
  `a_coordinate_outside_the_window_is_never_moved` (12.5 +/- 1e-6 stays)
  and `the_bore_mesh_stands_on_its_exact_levels`.
- **Test location.** The coordinator asked for the snap pins in
  `crates/geometry/tests`. They are in `crates/kernel/tests` because the
  snap is in the kernel's machining mesh, and `geometry::step` is not on
  `main`. A geometry test would need a new dependency edge
  (geometry -> kernel), which the law does not permit without a decision.
- **Cost to change.** One function and two constants.

### An inward solid is turned outward (`machining_mesh`)

- **Decided.** A watertight, consistently wound mesh of ONE shell (one
  group of triangles joined side to side, `mesh_weld::shells`) with a
  finite negative volume has all its faces pointed inward. The mesh swaps the
  second and third corner of each triangle, negates the volume and adds
  the note "the solid's faces all pointed inward (volume -X mm^3); the
  mesh is turned outward". A zero or NaN volume is still the `Volume`
  refusal. A mesh of two or more shells (a solid with a void) with a
  negative volume is also the `Volume` refusal: the sign of the sum does
  not tell which shell is turned, and a turn of all shells would make the
  void solid (review of #2843).
- **Why.** Main's truck path turned such a solid outward too
  (`step_outward.rs`). A closed shell with all senses turned over is the
  same solid.
- **Dropped.** A refusal (a legal file would be refused). Turning only
  part of the faces (a mixed winding is already refused by `sides`).
- **Pinned by** `an_inward_solid_is_turned_outward_and_said` and
  `a_solid_with_a_void_and_its_outer_shell_inward_is_refused`.

### A breaking edge or swept spline is refused by name (`step_curve_guard`)

- **Decided.** Before the topology read, the reader scans each B-spline
  curve that an `EDGE_CURVE` (through `SURFACE_CURVE`, `SEAM_CURVE`,
  `INTERSECTION_CURVE`) or a swept surface
  (`SURFACE_OF_LINEAR_EXTRUSION`, `SURFACE_OF_REVOLUTION`) uses. It refuses
  a weight that is not positive. It refuses an interior knot whose
  multiplicity is above the degree when the control polygon jumps there
  by more than 1e-9 x max(1, |coordinate|). The message names the role
  ("edge #N" or "swept surface #N"), the curve, the knot, the
  multiplicity, the degree and the jump, and says that the curve needs a
  subdivision.
- **Why.** Such a curve is two curves in one entity (ISO 10303-42 permits
  a multiplicity of degree + 1 only at the ends). solidcore evaluates it
  as one continuous curve and the mesh then has a gap or a wrong edge. A
  repeated knot with no jump is continuous and still imports.
- **Dropped.** A split of the curve at the knot (it changes the model's
  topology, which is the exporter's job).
- **Pinned by** the four tests in `crates/kernel/tests/step_curve_guard.rs`.

### Adaptive refinement of the deviation bound (`mesh_deviation`)

- **Decided.**
  - `measure_within` refines a sub-triangle until its bound is in the
    tolerance, down to depth 12, with a budget of 2^21 new samples for
    one plan (3 for each split). Past either cap the bound found so far
    is the judged one. `measure` keeps depth 3.
  - The bound of each sub-triangle also takes the minimum with
    `dmax + longest side`. The distance to a surface is 1-Lipschitz, and
    no point of a flat triangle is farther from a corner than its longest
    side, so this is a true upper bound.
  - The bound is one-sided. It bounds the distance from each point of
    the mesh to the surface. It does not bound the distance from each
    point of the surface to the mesh. A surface that folds back between
    two samples could stand off the mesh by more than the tolerance with
    no refusal. The algorithm is not changed for this (review of #2843).
- **Why.** The fillet fixture has a pole. A sliver at the pole spans the
  full u range in parameters, so the parametric Hessian bound did not
  shrink with a split. The bound was about 12 times the true deviation and
  a good mesh was refused. The Lipschitz bound shrinks with each split.
- **Dropped.** A depth cap only (it cannot stop a plan with many bad
  triangles from taking a long time). A larger fixed depth for `measure`
  (the bench timings would change).
- **Pinned by** `the_fillet_fixture_meshes_at_the_app_chord`.

#### Changed pins (`crates/kernel/tests/machining_mesh.rs`)

The tighter bound proves plans that the old bound could not prove. Each
fixture that we measured now meshes at its first plan:

| Fixture | Tolerance (mm) | Judged bound (mm) | Replan |
|---|---|---|---|
| Solidcraft sample | 0.005 | 0.0049999913 | no (was yes) |
| Solidcraft sample | 0.1 | 0.0999999405 | no (was yes) |
| fillet_corner.step | 0.005 | 0.0049998025 | no (was refused) |

- `solidcraft_sample_meshes_within_the_app_chord`:
  - old: the notes contain "replanned";
  - new: the notes do not contain "replanned" (the first plan is proven).
- `solidcraft_sample_still_refuses_an_out_of_tolerance_mesh`:
  - old: `coarse_01.largest() > 0.1` (the coarse 0.1 mm plan measured over
    0.1 mm);
  - new: `coarse_01.parametric > 0.1 && coarse_01.largest() <= 0.1` (the
    parametric reading still over-reads; the certified bound proves the
    plan).
  - Kept: the coarse plan exceeds 0.005 mm; the 0.1 mm request passes with
    a parametric reading over 0.1 mm; the spline bump on box.step is still
    refused with `Deviation` at face 0.
- The replan branch is still run by the bump case (replan, then refusal).
  No tracked fixture now passes only after a replan.

### Solid ranges in the mesh (`camcraft_geometry::geometry::mesh_solids`)

- **Decided.** `Mesh` has a `solids` field: one facet range per closed
  solid, empty for one soup. `Mesh::from_solids` refuses ranges that do
  not tile the facets in order. `slice::slice_of(facets, ranges, z)` slices
  each solid on its own and unites the sections when the whole soup meets
  the plane non-manifold. A solid with a volume that is not positive keeps
  the soup's refusal.
- **Why.** A STEP file with solids that share a wall line (the AP214
  sample) gives one soup in which the shared edges are used four times.
  The union fallback (`closed_solids`) must refuse it, because it cannot
  tell the solids apart. The importer knows the solids, so it keeps them.
- **Dropped.** Radial pairing of the facets around a non-manifold edge
  (a guess where the importer has the truth). One part for each solid in
  the app (it changes the model tree that the user sees).
- **Cost.** The literal `Mesh { facets }` no longer compiles; eight app
  tests use `Mesh::from_facets`. A transform that builds a new mesh from
  facets drops the ranges, which gives the old soup behaviour.
- **Pinned by** the five tests in `crates/geometry/tests/mesh_solids.rs`.
  The app reads the ranges in PR B.

## #917 - The kernel makes the pcurves that a STEP file does not give

**What was decided.**
- The solidcore pin moves to the fork's commit
  `2016386442dfee3b2a0c3a1bfdd4017c5254dac8` (#2781), by the procedure of
  `916-solidcore-step-bench.md`. The record at that commit has a `Blend`
  surface. The mesh bound and the mesh deviation give no closed form for
  it (`None`), as for a spline, so the measured deviation decides.
- The kernel crate implements the solidcore `Trims` seam
  (`solidcore_ops::pcurve::Trims`) in `crates/kernel/src/solidcore_trims.rs`
  (`KernelTrims`). `read_step` now calls
  `solidcore_step::topology::read_solids_with(&exchange, &KernelTrims)`
  instead of `read_solids`.
- A face that has an edge without a closed-form pcurve (a free-form edge on
  a spline face, for example a twisted B-spline flank) goes to the solidcore
  kernel alone, as an open one-face sheet. The uses without a pcurve go in
  bare (`solidcore_convert::brep::to_kernel_with_bare_uses`). The kernel
  makes their UV trims as it makes each trim it needs, and
  `solidcore_convert::brep::to_record` gives them back.
- The route is the maintainer's Solidcraft `SmlibTrims`, reused with his
  permission and moved onto the public API at the pinned solidcore commit.
- The trims run on the same kernel state as the import (`SolidcoreKernel::k`),
  not on a fresh kernel. Its tolerances, opt-in fixes and cancel token then
  hold for the trims too.
- Nothing is taken unchecked. Each of these is refused by name ("kernel
  pcurves: ..."), and the reader then refuses the solid:
  - an edge that lies more than 0.01 mm off its surface
    (`MAX_EDGE_GAP_MM`), whatever tolerance the file gives the edge. A
    smaller gap raises the edge and vertex tolerances to
    `SURFACE_GAP_MARGIN` times the gap, as the reader does;
  - an edge interval that the kernel moved past the edge's reach (the
    larger of its vertex and edge tolerances);
  - a made pcurve whose lift onto the surface misses its 3D edge by more
    than the held edge tolerance, but never more than `MAX_EDGE_GAP_MM`
    (33 samples, ends included);
  - a face, edge or vertex tolerance that is not a finite number of zero or
    more, and a lift sample whose distance is not finite (`f64::max` drops a
    NaN, so each is checked before it is used).
  The reader checks the whole record again after this
  (`record_check::agreement`). The interval and lift checks are in
  `crates/kernel/src/solidcore_trims/checks.rs` (the 400-line rule).
- New dependency edge: `camcraft-kernel -> solidcore-ops`, at the same
  pinned commit as the other solidcore crates. It is a crate of the solidcore
  workspace and is already in `Cargo.lock` through `solidcore-step`. No new
  third-party crate. No new edge between our own crates.
- The bench (`crates/kernel/tests/step_agreement.rs`) pins the new
  verdicts. `crates/kernel/tests/step_twisted_flank.rs` pins #2780 at the
  kernel: `twisted_flank.step` reads closed at 8000 mm3; the variant with a
  vertex off its curves is refused by name (observed: the surface would
  move 0.89 mm, over the reach of 0.51 mm), and so is
  `bspline_discontinuous.step` (the gap cap below).
- The two twisted-flank fixtures do not reach `KernelTrims`: the reader
  makes their pcurves itself (a probe found no call). `fillet_corner.step`,
  `bar_cross_holes.step` and `fig8.step` reach it, and
  `crates/kernel/tests/step_closed_form.rs` pins that route against closed
  forms. In `step_twisted_flank.rs`, only `bspline_discontinuous.step`
  reaches it (the gap cap).
- An inch file reaches it too: `fillet_corner_in_inches_reads_at_its_closed_form_volume_in_mm`
  edits the length unit of `fillet_corner.step` to the inch in memory and
  reads 25.4^3 times the closed form, in mm. The gap cap and the lift
  tolerance are in mm after the unit change.
- The two `Milling-test*.step` bench rows move from "disagree: bounding box"
  to "agree" (Refs #939). The port's box at 2016386 stops at the flat at
  Y = 19.719, as the file's vertices and both meshes do. This PR does not
  close #939; its owner confirms the fix there.
- The bench helper `step_util::solidcore_mesh` reads with `KernelTrims` too,
  so the sc-tess mesh is judged on the same record as the import.

**Why.** At the pinned commit the reader refuses a face whose free-form
edges have no pcurve ("pcurves failed on ..."). Real files have such faces:
a user STEP file with a twisted B-spline flank was refused. The kernel
already makes trims for its own booleans and blends, so the same code makes
these. The maintainer chose this route (option 2) over the alternatives
below.

**Considered and dropped.**
- Keep truck as a fallback for the faces that solidcore refuses. Dropped:
  two readers give two sets of answers, and the maintainer asked to remove
  truck.
- Our own pcurve fit (project 3D samples onto the surface, fit a 2D
  B-spline). Dropped: it is a second trim maker beside the kernel's, with
  its own tolerances to keep in step.
- Wait for the reader upstream to make the pcurves. Dropped: there is no
  date, and the user file stays refused until then.
- A fresh kernel for each face. Dropped: it loses the opt-in fixes and the
  cancel token of the import.

**Cost to change later.** Low. The seam is one trait. If the reader later
makes the pcurves itself, `read_step` calls `read_solids` again and
`solidcore_trims.rs` is deleted; the bench pins show any change of verdict.

### The lift tolerance (held edge tolerance, at most 0.01 mm)

**Chosen.** `lifts_onto` checks a made pcurve against
`min(held, MAX_EDGE_GAP_MM)`. `held` is the edge's tolerance from the file,
or as `cover_gaps` raised it. A loose file tolerance (or a raised one, which
can reach `SURFACE_GAP_MARGIN` times 0.01 mm) does not pass a pcurve that
misses its edge by more than the cap on an edge's gap.

**Measured** (a temporary probe, removed before the commit):

| Fixture | Held tolerance (mm) | Largest lift gap (mm) |
|---|---|---|
| fillet_corner.step | 1e-6 | at most 2.9e-7 |
| bar_cross_holes.step | 2e-5 | 1.2e-5 |
| bspline_discontinuous.step | 1e-6 | refused at the gap cap first |

On each fixture the held tolerance is under 0.01 mm, so the rule changes no
verdict. fig8, fillet_corner, bar_cross_holes and twisted_flank read at the
same volumes, and the two refused fixtures stay refused.

**Dropped.** The held tolerance alone: it follows the file, and a file can
give any tolerance.

### The edge-gap cap (0.01 mm)

**Chosen.** `MAX_EDGE_GAP_MM` = 0.01 mm. An edge whose measured gap to its
face's surface is over the cap is refused: "kernel pcurves: edge N lies G mm
off the face's surface, over the cap of 0.01 mm". The reader adds the solid
and the face (`#16 at read: pcurves failed on 1 of 6 faces; first: face
#53: ...`).

**Why.** With the reach of 1 mm, `bspline_discontinuous.step` (#1697) read
as a closed solid of 1.125 mm3: its edges stand 0.25 mm off a 1 mm part, and
the record raised their tolerances to 0.375 mm to cover that. On main it was
refused by name, so the 1 mm reach loosened a verdict. The maintainer's
Solidcraft keeps the same 1 mm limit (`MAX_TOLERANCE` = 1.0), so it would
take the file too. The cap is set from the largest gap that `KernelTrims`
measured on the fixtures that read:

| Fixture | Largest gap (mm) |
|---|---|
| fig8.step | 3.5e-12 |
| fillet_corner.step | 8.2e-13 |
| bar_cross_holes.step | 1.2e-6 |
| twisted_flank.step | no bare edge measured |
| bspline_discontinuous.step | 0.25 (refused) |

0.01 mm is about 8000 times the largest good gap and 25 times under the
0.25 mm step. It is not more than the sim's verdict tolerance (twice the
0.005 mm chord, #689), so an edge that is kept cannot move a verdict.

**Dropped.**
- The reader's 1 mm reach alone: it keeps the 0.25 mm step as a solid.
- A cap on the raised tolerance (`SURFACE_GAP_MARGIN` times the gap): the
  same test with a margin in it; the gap is the measured fact.
- A second guard on the reader's notes ("tolerance raised to ..."): the
  0.375 mm note came from `cover_gaps` itself, so the cap removes its cause.
  Not added, to keep one rule in one place.

### Bench verdicts against truck (fillet_corner, bar_cross_holes)

**Chosen.** The rows of `fillet_corner.step` and `bar_cross_holes.step` are
"disagree: volume, area" | "watertight, within tolerance". `fig8.step` is
"agree" | "watertight, within tolerance".

| Fixture | Main | Now |
|---|---|---|
| fig8 | solidcore refuses: #14 ... / no exact solid | agree / watertight |
| fillet_corner | solidcore refuses: #1289 ... / no exact solid | disagree: volume, area / watertight |
| bar_cross_holes | solidcore refuses: #655 ... / no exact solid | disagree: volume, area / watertight |
| bspline_discontinuous | both refuse (#16) / no exact solid | the same |

**Why.** Truck reads both files as open meshes (121 and 1090 open edges), so
its volume is short (20651.68 against 26816.49 mm3; 45816.21 against
78225.68 mm3). That is a defect of the truck path, which the app switch
(#917, PR B) removes. To pin the exact volumes apart from truck,
`crates/kernel/tests/step_closed_form.rs` checks each against:
- a closed form from the fixture's own dimensions, relative 1e-5:
  - fillet_corner: a 30 mm cube less three R 3.125 edge rounds and a
    spherical corner, 27000 - 3 (1 - pi/4) r^2 (30 - r) - r^3 (1 - pi/6) =
    26816.4939 mm3 (read 26816.49);
  - bar_cross_holes: a R 25 x 40 bar less two blind radial R 2.5 holes with
    flat bottoms at the file's z = 16.9707 and -16.9679, the hole volume
    integrated over the hole's disc = 78225.6805 mm3 (read 78225.68);
- solidcore's own closed sc-tess mesh, within the bench tolerance (1e-3);
- the bounding box.

**Dropped.** "agree" with a looser tolerance: it would hide truck's open
mesh. Dropping the rows: the bench must name each fixture.

### Port verdicts that the pin move changed (solidcore 55d0e76 -> 2016386)

The narrow batch gate found three kernel pins that the pin move changed.
KernelTrims is not the cause: none of these tests reads STEP.

- **Rim chamfer (`blend`).** The default path now gives the cone (upstream
  WR-421, solidcore#420). Chosen: the "not yet" test becomes
  `rim_chamfer_default_path_matches_the_cone`, as the test asked. It heals
  the result (`heal` hands out only a closed solid) and measures it against
  the cone's closed form, in volume and box. Dropped: a deleted test, and
  an unchanged "not yet" test with a loose bound.
- **Box at a NaN origin (`corrupt_input`).** The port now refuses it
  (`Err`); 55d0e76 built a non-solid box. Chosen: pin `Err`, with a comment
  that names the rev. The refusal is the stricter verdict. The other 14
  rows do not change.
- **Zone tolerance edits (`import_corpus`).** The writer now prints the
  zone tolerance as `1e-5`, not `0.0000100000000000`. The corpus edit was a
  literal `replacen`, so the zero, negative and NaN rows read the intact
  box. Only the NaN row failed, because the other two rows pin "Ok". The
  reader does not accept a NaN tolerance: `read_smb` refuses a non-finite
  one by name (it did before this change), but the edit did not reach it.
  Chosen:
  - the edit finds the header line by its label (`zone_tolerance`);
  - the corpus test asserts that each edit changed the file;
  - the new test `non_finite_zone_tolerance_is_refused_by_name` asserts the
    refusal text of `read_smb` and `import_smb` for NaN, inf and -inf.

  All pinned rows stay as they were, with the "replaced by 1e-4" notes of
  the zero and negative rows. Dropped: a second refusal in the importer.
  `read_smb` already refuses before the port parses, and `import_smb` calls
  it first. Also dropped: a refusal of a zero or negative tolerance. The
  importer replaces those values and reports the change in a pinned note;
  that is the earlier decision for the INTACT rows.

## #917 - The app reads STEP models through solidcore (part 1 of 3)

**What was decided.**
- The model import of a STEP file (`Format::Step`) goes through
  `camcraft_geometry::step::parse`. That module calls the kernel seam
  (`solidcore_step_import::import_step_model`, then `machining_mesh` for
  each solid). `camcraft-app` does not depend on `camcraft-kernel`. No new
  edge between our crates: geometry already depends on the kernel for
  Solidcraft (#1456). The time bound and the mesh-to-facets glue that the
  two kernel imports share moved to `camcraft_geometry::kernel_import`.
- The truck mesh path of the app is removed (the `step_*` helper modules of
  `crates/app/src/geometry/import/` that only the truck reader used), with
  the truck dependencies of `crates/app/Cargo.toml`.
- The public STEP entry for text in memory stays
  `camcraft_app::geometry::import::parse_model(data, Format::Step)` and
  `parse_model_graded`, with `import::step::parse_noted(data, budget)` under
  them.
- The browser build (wasm32) does not link solidcore. It refuses a STEP file
  by name: "STEP models open in the desktop app only, not in the browser
  build".
- A model over the facet budget is meshed again at a coarser chord: at most
  6 more tries, the chord times the facet ratio, clamped to x2..x16. The kept
  chord goes to `Graded::coarse_mm` as before (#864, #1054).
- **Sheets.** A sheet (a shell of a `SHELL_BASED_SURFACE_MODEL`, open by the
  file's own word) is meshed with its open boundary
  (`machining_mesh_open::sheet_mesh`) and labelled "sheet #N"; its notes
  read "STEP sheet #N: ...". A solid whose faces the mesher leaves out gives
  a partial mesh (`partial_mesh`). It lands only as an incomplete model
  with each left-out face named (the #1610 hole line, `step::hole`). It
  never lands as a whole model, and the graded loaders refuse it.
- **No STEP text reaches the partial path at the pinned solidcore commit.**
  Probes on `box.step` and the bent `fillet_corner`:

  | Probe | Result |
  |---|---|
  | one face removed | refused at read: "the outer shell is not closed" |
  | plane moved 0.5 mm or turned 90 degrees | "pcurves failed ... an edge lies 0.5 mm off the face's surface" |
  | plane tilted | reads; the mesh is refused: "face 2 stands 2.873e-1 mm off its surface" |
  | the same face twice | "face #53 is used twice" |
  | bent `fillet_corner` weights | refused at read, by face and value (face #1228, 1E300) |

  So the partial mesh is pinned at the kernel by a record edit
  (`crates/kernel/tests/machining_mesh_open.rs`), and the app pins of the
  incomplete model use a synthetic hole.
- **Closed solids ride the facets (`SolidRanges`).** The STEP import lands
  one facet range for each closed solid (`Mesh::from_solids`,
  `app::mesh_solids`). The slicer and the winding check read the solids
  from the ranges, not from a weld of the soup. The ranges are valid only at
  the model revision and facet count that they landed with. Import, update
  and undo land them. Any other landing of facets (`model::set_facets`,
  Align) steps the revision, and the soup read applies again. `MoveModel`
  sets only the transform, so the ranges stay. A file with a sheet or a
  partial mesh gets no ranges: such a mesh is not a set of solids.
- **Project file: `solids`, no version step.** The model entity has an
  optional `solids: [[start, end], ...]` (serde default, not written when
  empty). An older reader drops the key and reads the facets as one soup,
  which is what it did before. So the format version does not step. Ranges
  that do not tile the facets (out of bounds, overlap, gap, short, out of
  order, empty, one range) are dropped at load with a logged note, never
  trusted.
- **Shared-edge rule (`shared_edge::solids_touch`).** Two outward solids
  that touch or overlap along a wall use one mesh edge in 2k facets. Such an
  edge is accepted only when all of these are true:
  - the use count is even and balanced, with at least 4 uses;
  - each body (linked over plain edges only) uses the edge once each way;
  - no facet apex lies on the edge line;
  - each body has a facet at the same angle (1e-6 rad) as a facet of
    another body (a wall of one lies on a wall of the other).

  The slicer fallback (`slice_bodies::closed_solids`) and the winding check
  (`pick::winding`) use the same function. A soup that is truly
  non-manifold (one shell that meets itself, a fin, blocks that meet only
  along an edge line) is still refused by name. A model without such an
  edge gives the same result as before.
- **Face winding notes.** solidcore orients each face with its shell and
  leaves no trace. `step_face_winding` finds the faces in the file whose
  loops run against their neighbours and names them, as the earlier
  importer did: "shell #7: 1 face(s) wound against their neighbours were
  flipped: face #32 (3 of 6)".
- **Inward solids: one note.** The closed solids that are wound inward are
  turned outward. The import gives one note for all of them (#1617
  wording): "{k} closed solid(s) wound inward (negative volume) were turned
  outward: {n} facet(s) reversed".
- **Syntax locator.** A syntax refusal keeps the #912 location. Since #917
  the locator (`step_diag`) runs on every file before the kernel reads it,
  so it now skips a resource reference `<...>` (ISO 10303-21 ed. 3): a `/*`
  or a `'` in it opens nothing.
- `Graded::open` and the project field `mesh_open` stay.

**Why.** The maintainer asked to remove stepio and finish the switch to
solidcore. One reader for each format means one set of refusals and one
mesh law (watertight, outward, deviation measured). The solid ranges keep
what the reader knows (which facets close which solid) instead of a guess
from a weld of coincident facets.

**Changed pins** (old -> new, cause; the `#[test]` count of each file is
kept):
- `import_step_closed_shell.rs` (3 tests) and `import_step_open_shell.rs`
  test 1: "closed shell #1288 (10 faces) meshes open" / an incomplete model
  with its hole named -> a refusal at read, "first #1289 at read: face
  #1228: weight: 1... out of range". Cause: solidcore refuses the bent
  weight before any mesh (probe table above). The #1610 tests 2-4 do not
  change.
- `import_step_guard.rs`, `import_step_guard_default_cap.rs`: truck's
  evaluation cap ("within 100000 evaluations", "did not converge",
  "stopped after 3 faces or edges") -> the kernel's reasons: "off the
  face's surface" for the jumping face, "used twice" for the repeated face.
  The #1568 pin now uses a facet budget, and the volume bound is
  `1.2 * chord` at the kept chord (1.0194 at a 0.01 chord). Cause: the
  evaluation cap is gone with truck.
  Per assert (old reading -> new reading; cause; why not weaker):
  - `import_step_guard_default_cap.rs`: "face #53 (B-spline surface, face
    6 of 6 in shell #17)" and "did not converge" -> "first #16 at read:
    pcurves failed on 1 of 6 faces; first: face #53", "edge 0 lies 0.2500
    mm off the face's surface" and "import an STL". Cause: the kernel names
    the solid (`MANIFOLD_SOLID_BREP` #16), not the shell (#17), and it does
    not print the surface kind. Not weaker: the face, its solid and the face
    count are still asserted (restored on the final head), and the reason
    is now a measured gap (0.25 mm over the 0.01 mm cap), not a time-out.
    The surface kind ("B-spline surface") has no text in the new refusal.
  - `import_step_guard.rs`, `a_dome_over_its_facet_budget_keeps_a_coarser_mesh_at_its_own_chord`:
    volume bound `2e-3` -> `1.2 * chord` for the kept, coarser mesh; the
    `2e-3` bound stays on the full mesh at the cap. Cause: the old fallback
    kept a mesh of chord ~0.002 mm; the new fallback keeps a mesh at the
    budget's chord (0.01 mm reads 1.0194 against 1.0222). Not weaker for
    safety: the kept mesh carries its chord in `coarse_mm`, so the program
    verdict tightens by the excess or refuses (#864, `model_fidelity.rs`);
    the bound follows that chord (curved area under 1.2 mm2, each facet at
    most `chord` off its surface).
  - `import_step_guard.rs`, `a_shell_of_many_runaway_faces_is_refused_after_a_few_trips`:
    "stopped after 3 faces or edges" -> "first #16 at read: face #53 is
    used twice" (restored to the full text on the final head) and a time
    bound under 30 s. Cause: the old pass-wide trip budget stopped a mesh
    pass after 3 failed faces; the kernel refuses the repeated face when it
    reads the shell, so no face is meshed at all. Not weaker: the law (a
    hostile shell ends at once, by name) holds at zero meshed faces, and the
    time bound pins "at once".
  - `import_step_closed_shell.rs` (3 tests): "closed shell #1288 (10 faces)
    meshes open", "boundary edges lie more than", "got no mesh from the
    kernel" (the dropped face named) and "in shell #1288 could not be
    tessellated" / "returned no mesh for it" -> the one refusal at read,
    "first #1289 at read: face #1228: weight: 1... out of range". Probed on
    the final head: none of the old texts is in the new refusal, so none
    can be restored. Cause: solidcore refuses the bent weight before any
    mesh. Not weaker: the old asserts named a face that was dropped from a
    mesh; now no mesh exists, and the refusal names the same face (#1228)
    and its value. The dropped-face path itself is pinned at the kernel
    (`machining_mesh_open.rs`).
  - `import_step_open_shell.rs` test 1: the STEP-level incomplete-hole
    wording ("closed shell #1288 (10 faces) meshes open", "got no mesh
    from the kernel", `coarse_mm == UNKNOWN_MM`, the "Incomplete:" line,
    MCP `incomplete: true`, "the model would import with walls missing")
    is no longer asserted from a STEP file anywhere. Cause: no STEP text
    reaches the partial path at the pinned commit (probe table). Not
    weaker: each of those laws is still asserted in the same file, on a
    synthetic hole that lands through the same command
