## #1198 - Viewport bar snapping and typed values (slice d)

**What was decided.**
- **Expand the bottom overlay bar upward only when Move or Rotate mode is
  active.** When neither handle mode is on, the bar remains the 12-button
  strip (`bar_rect`, 368 x 38 px), keeping the default shell layout and pixel
  snapshots unchanged. When Move or Rotate is on, the same rounded grey
  background extends upward by one compact control strip (`panel_rect`,
  368 x 66 px) hosting the axis selector (`X`, `Y`, `Z`), the typed distance
  or angle field (`TextEdit` + `Set` / Enter), and the snap step parameter.
  `viewcube::Hud::contains` covers the full expanded bar so clicks and drags
  on those widgets never start viewport orbit or picking, and
  `viewport_layout::furniture_with_bar` lifts the legend and empty-document
  line above the expanded height.
- **Hold Shift to snap; defaults are 1.0 mm (Move) and 90.0 degrees
  (Rotate).** `BodyDrag` and `TurnDrag` track the unsnapped raw drag
  (`raw_delta`, `raw_angle`) separately from the active previewed/released
  value (`delta`, `angle`) so pressing or releasing Shift mid-drag toggles
  snapping smoothly without accumulation drift. Both snap parameters are
  positive bounded fields in the bar (`0.001..=10_000.0` mm through the active
  unit lens, `0.1..=360.0` degrees), and `DEFAULT_ROTATE_SNAP_DEG = 90.0`
  matches the 90-degree requirement in #1198 while remaining editable in the
  bar for finer angles such as 15 or 45 degrees.
- **Typed entry applies through the existing drag commands.** Typing a
  distance or angle in the bar and pressing Enter or clicking `Set` converts
  from the active display unit (`units::from_display`) or degrees to radians,
  refuses non-finite / missing-selection inputs by name, skips zero-length
  deltas with no history step, and queues `CommandKind::MoveModelBy` or
  `CommandKind::TurnModelBy` — so undo, staleness, following stock and
  aligned-setup frames work identically to dragging a handle.

**Why.**
- Keeping the control strip hidden while Move and Rotate are off avoids
  unrequested bar clutter in normal navigation and avoids changing the
  default shell width (`viewcube::min_width`) or default pixel goldens.
- Using `Shift` for handle snapping avoids colliding with `Ctrl`/`Cmd`
  shortcuts and `Alt` window-manager drags on Linux.
- Reusing `MoveModelBy` / `TurnModelBy` preserves one command path (`MoveModel`)
  and requires no new app command or MCP tool.

**Considered and dropped.**
- **Always showing snap and value widgets in the main bar:** dropped because
  the inputs are mode-specific (mm/in distance vs degree angle) and widening
  the base bar would crowd narrow panes and shift every resting viewport
  golden.
- **Persisting snap steps in per-user `prefs.json`:** dropped to match the
  other viewport-bar toggles (`move_handles`, `rotate_handles`, `pick_through`),
  which are session view state in `crates/ui` and require no app preference
  format changes.
- **Using `DragValue` instead of `TextEdit` for the typed move/turn input:**
  dropped because `DragValue` fires `changed()` on intermediate keystrokes
  and silently discards invalid text, whereas `TextEdit` + `Set` / `Enter`
  commits exactly one command on submit and refuses non-finite text by name.

**Cost to change later.**
Low and local to `crates/ui/src/egui_app/viewport_bar_controls.rs`,
`crates/ui/src/move_drag.rs` and `crates/ui/src/turn_drag.rs`. Changing the
default snap steps, adding prefs persistence, or moving the controls onto a
combined move+rotate gizmo (#2624) touches only those UI fields and helpers.

# 1339 - Vouch for a mesh of unknown fidelity

Issue: #1339 (a follow-up of #1056).

## What was chosen

- A new undoable command, `VouchModelFidelity { model, by }`. It clears the
  "fidelity unknown" mark (`model_fidelity::UNKNOWN_MM`) of one model and of
  the stocks copied straight from it. Undo puts each mark back.
- The command applies to the unknown sentinel only. It refuses by name:
  - a model with a recorded coarse chord (#864);
  - an incomplete model (#1610, a mesh with a hole);
  - a model that is not marked;
  - a name that is not a model;
  - an empty name of the person who vouches.
- The record of who vouched is a new component, `FidelityVouched { by, rev }`.
  `rev` is the geometry revision of the model at the time of the vouch.
- The record speaks only while the model has that revision and no fidelity
  flag (`model_vouch::by_of`). An import, an update or a repair lands other
  facets, and the record is then silent. No other command changes for this.
- The history names who vouched. `VouchModelFidelity::run` executes the
  command as one labelled undo group (`History::top_label`). It also logs
  the vouch at `info` level.
- The project file keeps the record in the optional key `fidelity_vouched`
  of the model row. The loader refuses the key on a row that is not a
  model, beside a fidelity flag, or with an empty name.
- The MCP tool is `vouch_model_fidelity { model, by }`. `get_job` shows
  `fidelity_vouched` on the model. Scripts use the tool through
  `cam.call("vouch_model_fidelity", ...)`, which is the script seam for
  each undoable MCP tool (#2393).
- The model page shows a name field and the button "Vouch for this mesh"
  below the "Fidelity unknown" line. A vouched model shows who vouched.

## Why

- A recorded chord is a measurement. A hole is a fact about the mesh. The
  word of a person does not replace either, so the command refuses them.
- The gate refuses each operation on an unknown mesh, and the laws read
  that mesh untightened at generation. The toolpaths that exist are thus
  the toolpaths of an exact mesh. The command regenerates nothing.
- The revision in the record keeps a stale vouch silent with no edit to
  `UpdateModel`, `RepairModel` or `ImportModel`. Open PR #2024 changes
  those files, so this also prevents a conflict.

## What was dropped

- No project version step. An old reader that drops `fidelity_vouched`
  loads the same unmarked model and loses only the name, as with
  `mesh_open`. The gate result is the same.
- No change to `UNKNOWN_NOTE`. The refusal text still says to re-import the
  model. Many tests pin that text. The model page and the MCP tool
  description tell the user about the vouch.
- No vouch for a stock copy whose source model is deleted. The command
  takes a model name. Such a stock still needs a new stock definition.
- No vouch through a chain of copies. Only a stock copied straight from the
  model, with the unknown mark of its own, is cleared. A copy with a
  recorded chord keeps it.
- No identity check of `by`. The application has no user accounts. The
  name is plain text that the person types.
- No dedicated script verb. `cam.call` is the seam.

## #1389 - Explain comments for the remaining post dialects

**Decided:** Enable Explain on eight more posts through the shared helper.
Sinumerik uses semicolon comments. grblHAL, TinyG, Carvera, PathPilot
plasma and lathe, and generic ISO wire and sinker EDM use parentheses.
Each writer appends a comment only when the complete line fits within
80 characters. Existing executable text stays unchanged.

**Why:** Each control has its own word meanings. Sinumerik describes
G700 and G710 as length and feed unit choices. It describes G505 and
G506 as work offsets 5 and 6. It leaves G58 and G59 unexplained.
PathPilot plasma describes its probe, torch and plasma parameter words.
PathPilot lathe describes its extended offsets and retains the existing
tool station and offset decoder.

Machine-supplied EDM commands stay unexplained. The wire post marks
these calls to `block()` so the helper skips them. This includes a
motion block that carries a machine-supplied UV code. The sinker post
already writes its machine commands through `emit()`. A machine can
assign meanings to these words that differ from the shared mill table.

Heidenhain and Sodick retain their named refusal when Explain is on.
Heidenhain's public ISO manual describes semicolon comments after the
last word. It does not confirm placement beside the `*` terminator
that this post exports. Sodick uses T91 and T90 to thread and cut the
wire. The shared decoder would describe them as tool numbers. These
posts need confirmed syntax or a suitable decoder before they can
declare `explains`.

**Considered and dropped:** Do not enable every post with the shared
mill table. That would give some EDM commands incorrect descriptions.
Do not guess where Heidenhain accepts a comment beside `*`. Do not
shorten executable text to make room for an explanation. Omit the
explanation when the complete line would exceed the chosen limit.
Keep the shared engine unchanged because the existing helper supports
the eight enabled posts.

**Cost to change later:** Heidenhain needs a confirmed exported block
example and tests for its terminator and tool-axis words. Sodick needs
a decoder for its EDM T words and tests for each supported meaning.
A different line limit needs updated boundary tests for the affected
post. Machine-specific EDM explanations need an explicit meaning
contract instead of an inference from the code letters.

Public behavior references:

- [Siemens 840D Fundamentals](https://cache.industry.siemens.com/dl/files/241/109763241/att_971137/v1/840Dsl_fundamentals_progr_man_1218_en-US.pdf), section 3.2.4, page 44: semicolon comments.
- [Heidenhain TNC 640 ISO programming](https://content.heidenhain.de/doku/tnc_guide/pdf_files/TNC640/34059x-07/diniso/892909-25.pdf), section 4.1, pages 172-173: comments after the last word.
- The existing post provenance comments identify the sources for the
  supported control words. This change uses those behavior descriptions.

## #1444 - Slot Undercut: T-slot, keyseat, dovetail and lollipop passes that never move in Z under material

**What was decided**

1. **Four cutter kinds, no new tool fields.** `TSlot`, `Keyseat`, `Dovetail`
   and `Lollipop` join `ToolKind` (file words `t_slot`, `keyseat`,
   `dovetail`, `lollipop`; additive, no `PROJECT_VERSION` step). They read
   the existing fields: `diameter` is the head, `flute_len` the head's
   height, `shank_d` / `shank_len` the neck, `tip_angle` the dovetail's
   flank angle off the bottom face. One reading for every consumer:
   `camcraft_tools::undercut::Undercut` (head shape, neck radius, contact
   point).
2. **One operation kind, `Slot Undercut`** (`OpParams::SlotUndercut`, tag
   44, appended). The centre line is typed: `a`, `b` and a DXF-style
   `bulge` (0 = straight, else a circular arc). The undercut `width` is
   measured at the cutter's widest point, so the pass offset comes from
   the profile's contact radius, not from the tip.
3. **The Z law is a construction law and a verified law.** The generator
   changes Z at one XY station only (`run_in` behind `a` on the entry
   tangent) and checks that on the built path. The verifier has a new
   mode (`Mode::Undercut`) and law (g): any move that changes Z while
   material stands in or over the head's disc is `Warning::UndercutLift`
   (blocking); a neck or holder band with material above its bottom is a
   `ShankHit`. Both are re-read against the stock the program ahead left
   (`acquit_undercut_by_prior`), so a neck slot or an entry pocket that an
   earlier operation cut is air. With no such cut the conviction stands.
4. **An undercut clears no column.** In `Mode::Undercut` the verifier's
   rest model takes no cut from the path, and the column stock engines
   (program verdict, carried stock, rest grids) remove nothing for an
   undercut operation. A column holds one top per (x, y): lowering it to
   the head would remove the roof and report a false gouge, and would let
   a lift through the roof pass as a retract in its own kerf.
5. **The true profile where a solid can hold it.** The solid law judges
   head and neck against the part mesh with the real head: `Prof::Dove`
   (frustum) and `Prof::Ball` (whole ball) beside the existing disc. The
   field stock (`Stock::simulate_undercut`) removes the head and the neck
   as two convex solids (their union is the non-convex cutter), with a new
   exact frustum solid (`SdfTool::Dovetail`). The stock view uses it.
6. **Refusal instead of support where nothing is verified:** a flipped WCS
   and a rotated work offset refuse the kind; an aligned setup and a WCS
   yaw do not list it (refused by their own doors); no 3+2 tilt.
7. **A cylinder against a 'Do not touch' item** (merge of main, #2055).
   Main's avoid law grows each atom by the clearance
   (`swept::rho_expanded`). For `Prof::Dove` and `Prof::Ball` it reads the
   circumscribed cylinder: the head's largest radius over the atom's
   height. `avoid_poly` stretches an atom over a Z range, and a profile
   that is not non-decreasing would then report too small a radius above
   its bottom. The cylinder holds the head at each stretch, so the law
   can refuse a legal move near a protected item by at most the head's
   taper, and never passes a violation. The stretched atom has no `cap`
   allowance: a protected item is never cut. *Dropped:* the exact grown
   frustum and ball, which are correct only for an atom that is not
   stretched and need a second code path for the keep-out.
   Pinned by `crates/sim/tests/verify_avoid_undercut.rs`.

**Why**

- The issue's safety statement is about Z moves under material. A plain
  contour's laws read a vertical retract as "rides its own kerf", which is
  false under a roof. The law had to say so in the verifier, not only in
  the generator, because a path can be edited, pasted or produced by a
  later generator.
- Reusing `shank_d` as the neck keeps every existing reader of the tool
  record correct: `Tool::profile`, the drawn-cutter law and the verifier's
  shank band already describe "a cylinder head on a narrower shank". Only
  the dovetail and the ball needed new profile code.
- A union of convex solids keeps the field engine's convex sweep law
  (golden section on a convex distance) true for each piece. A general
  non-convex revolved profile would need a bracketed search (issue 896's
  research, slice 2) and was not needed for these four heads.

**Considered and dropped**

- *A generic `FormMill` kind with a drawn outline* (issue 896, slice 1).
  It needs the drawn outline to survive `cutter_fit::refit`, a digest of
  the flute outline and a non-convex sweep. That is issue 896's work. The
  four kinds here are parametric and need none of it. Issue 896 stays open
  for corner rounding, back chamfer and slitting saws.
- *A new `SimOp` field for the undercut.* `SimOp` has about 90 literal
  construction sites. The undercut rides `Planned::undercut` in the app
  and `Stock::simulate_undercut` in the sim crate instead.
- *New neck fields on `Tool`.* Not needed (see above); the file format and
  every tool dialog stay as they are.
- *Multiple depth levels.* One level per operation: the head cuts the
  whole undercut height when the cutter matches the slot. A taller
  undercut takes a second operation with another Bottom Z.
- *Round far ends.* The far end links offsets with a straight lateral
  feed. The cutter centre never leaves the band within the shift of the
  centre line, so the undercut is never wider than asked; a blind end is
  left square by up to the shift.
- *Picked geometry.* The centre line is typed (as the Slot's is). A pick
  law for undercut faces is follow-up work.
- *Cutting the neck with the column engine.* It would be correct only
  where the neck slot is narrower than the neck (a collision the law
  already refuses), so it adds nothing.

**Literature search (review follow-up, 2026-11-19)**

The original implementation preceded this search. This follow-up checks its
choices against published material; it does not change that history. The
search used the web search tool because no Perplexity tool was available.
Queries covered T-slot preparation and side entry, dovetail and lollipop
contact geometry, distance-field CSG, and tri-dexel machining simulation.
Only public Autodesk behaviour documentation, a machining handbook, and
published research support the findings below. No camlib implementation,
HSMWorks source, binary, output trace, or bundled asset was inspected.

Checked sources and the choices they support:

1. Walter, [Technical Compendium — Milling, 2024, section D2,
   page D 140, “Strategies for preparing a T-slot”](https://cdn.walter-tools.com/files/sitecollectiondocuments/downloads/global/manuals/en-gb/technical-compendium-milling-2024-en.pdf).
   The indexed section describes a prepared opening that extends below
   the shoulder to leave the cutter shank clear. This supports checking
   the neck against the opening as well as the head against the slot.
   Our additional allowance for each radial pass follows from the neck's
   lateral displacement. The handbook gives machining preparation
   advice, not a proof of collision freedom for an arbitrary entry.
2. Autodesk, [Sketch profile selection](https://help.autodesk.com/cloudhelp/ENU/Fusion-CAM/files/MFG-GEOMETRY-SELECTION-SKETCH-PROFILE.htm),
   and [Is it possible to create a keyway undercut with a Slot operation
   in Fusion?](https://www.autodesk.com/support/technical/article/caas/sfdcarticles/sfdcarticles/Is-it-possible-to-create-a-keyway-undercut-with-a-Slot-operation-in-Fusion.html)
   (2025-11-04). The first describes tapered walls cut with a dovetail
   cutter and clearance at both path ends. The second describes a gouge
   with an ordinary slot path and returning to the entry position.
   These support an explicit entry and exit clearance check. Our chosen
   construction is more restrictive: descend at one outside station,
   enter and leave laterally at depth, then retract at that station.
   This construction and the separate stock check are our design.
3. Autodesk, [Generate a Blend toolpath](https://help.autodesk.com/cloudhelp/ENU/Fusion-CAM/files/MFG-MULTI-AXIS-BLEND-STEPS.htm),
   and [Lollipop cutter fails to completely deburr undercut hole using
   'Flow' toolpath strategy in Fusion 360](https://help.autodesk.com/view/fusion360/ENU/?caas=caas/sfdcarticles/sfdcarticles/Lollipop-cutter-fails-to-completely-deburr-undercut-hole-using-Flow-toolpath-strategy-in-Fusion-360.html)
   (2023-10-30). The first distinguishes surface-based undercut spacing
   from tip-based spacing. The second identifies the ball diameter as a
   limit on access to tight corners. These support using the actual
   profile instead of treating the cutter as a point at its tip.
   Our contact coordinates follow from elementary geometry: a cylindrical
   disc and a narrowing frustum reach their largest radius at the bottom;
   a sphere reaches it at the equator. These coordinates are our
   derivation, not formulas copied from the documentation.
4. Frisken, Perry, Rockwood and Jones, [Adaptively Sampled Distance
   Fields: A General Representation of Shape for Computer Graphics](https://www.merl.com/publications/docs/TR2000-15.pdf),
   SIGGRAPH 2000, pp. 249–254, sections 3 and 4.1. Section 4.1 gives
   Boolean carving of object and tool fields. Section 3 discusses
   sampling resolution and reconstruction error. This supports removing
   swept head and neck solids from a volumetric field that can retain a
   roof. It does not require a one-height stock model or establish our
   sweep search's accuracy.
5. Frisken and Perry, [Designing with Distance Fields](https://www.merl.com/publications/docs/TR2006-054.pdf),
   2006, section 2.2 and Table 1; sections 4.1–4.3. The paper states the
   sign convention for min/max CSG and warns that a combined field need
   not remain a Euclidean distance field. It also describes aliasing and
   resolution limits. Our inference is to sweep each convex head/neck
   piece separately and combine the removed sets, rather than apply a
   convex search to the complete non-convex cutter. This paper supports
   the set representation, not the convex-search convergence claim.
6. Ren, Zhu and Lee, [Feature Conservation and Conversion of Tri-dexel
   Volumetric Models to Polyhedral Surface Models for Product
   Prototyping](https://www.cad-journal.net/files/vol_5/CAD_5%286%29_2008_932-941.pdf),
   Computer-Aided Design & Applications 5(6), 2008, pp. 932–941,
   DOI 10.3722/cadaps.2008.932-941, sections 1 and 6. The paper describes
   tri-dexel Boolean modelling and the work needed to preserve features
   and produce a consistent surface. Tri-dexel is a valid alternative
   for this class of stock representation. We retain the existing field
   engine to avoid adding another representation and reconstruction
   path. A single top height cannot represent air below a roof.

Limits of this search and the retained design:

- These sources support the selected shapes and representation. They do
  not certify our implementation, feeds, engagement, or collision tests.
  The original handbook and convex-search references in module comments
  remain historical provenance; this search does not claim to have
  checked every page of those references.
- A prepared neck opening does not prove that the head can descend into
  it. The outside station still needs the stock check before any Z move.
  Returning along the entry path alone does not prove that path is clear.
- The field is sampled and circular moves are approximated. Small roofs
  and sharp features can depend on cell size and chord tolerance. CSG
  set operations do not provide a global exact-distance guarantee.
- Four ideal parametric heads do not describe arbitrary form cutters,
  edge radii, or every flute/neck transition. Tilted tools and general
  non-convex sweep searches remain outside this operation's scope.
- No source found here supplies the exact straight/circular pass layout
  or proves its safety. That layout is our own construction, checked by
  the generator tests and the independent verification and profile laws.

**Cost to change later**

- The kind words and the op's keys are in saved files from the first
  release that ships them: renaming one is a format step.
- `Mode::Undercut` and `Warning::UndercutLift` (`undercut_lift` over MCP)
  are part of the verify contract and of cached findings.
- Moving to a generic drawn form cutter (issue 896) can keep these four
  kinds as presets: `Undercut::of` is the one place that reads them.

### The lollipop head in the fixture laws (review of `b95c27b2`)

**Chosen:** the fixture laws (c2)/(d2) read
`camcraft_tools::undercut::fixture_geom`. It is `Tool::geom` with the
head band raised to the head's top (the ball's pole at `2r` for a
lollipop). The shank band shrinks by the same amount, so the neck top
and the holder stay at their real heights. The post gate
(`fixture_struck::op_hits`) and the generation steel laws (link routing
and the workholding warnings) use it. The holder stack is still built
from the real `Tool::geom`.

**Why:** a lollipop's `flute_len` is the neck start, below the pole.
The plain stack swept the ball only up to the neck start and the neck
above it, so steel beside the upper hemisphere passed. The band is a
cylinder of the ball's radius, so it encloses the ball and can only
over-report.

**Dropped:** a change of `Tool::geom` itself. Every stack law reads it,
and `Cutter::judged` matches the undercut head to `flute_len`; a change
there moves the gouge and stock laws too. The fixture laws alone had
the gap.

## #1445 - Fine boring (G76): the shift is in the cycle choice and in the chain; only a post that declares the cycle writes it

**What was decided.**

1. Fine boring is a new cycle choice on the drilling operation,
   `CycleChoice::FineBore { shift_x_um, shift_y_um }`, and a new CL cycle
   kind, `CycleKind::FineBore`. The shift is a required part of the choice.
   There is no default shift.
2. The chain makes the shift. A hole's group is: feed in, a lateral rapid
   at the bottom (the shift), a rapid out at the shifted XY to R, a rapid
   back onto the hole axis at R. The `Cycle` and `CycleRec` records get no
   new field.
3. The post engine reads the shift from the chain and gives it to the
   script as `ShiftX` / `ShiftY`. It refuses the cycle by name for a script
   that does not declare `fineBoring = true`, and for a chain with no shift
   move.
4. Only the Haas post declares `fineBoring`. It writes
   `G76 X Y Z R I J P F`, one whole block for each hole, and never `Q`.
   Each of the other 17 shipped posts refuses the cycle by name.
5. A machine file can state `spindle.orientation: true|false`.
   `false` refuses a fine bore by name, with any post. An unstated value
   is "not limited", as for `spindle.rigid_tapping`.
6. The shift must be smaller than `(tool dia. - shank dia.) / 2`. The
   generator refuses a larger shift by name. The command refuses a zero
   shift, a shift above 5 mm on one axis, and a shift not smaller than a
   hole radius.
7. The verifier reads the three stopped-spindle rapids with the stopped
   bar. Law (d) and the solid law do not read the cutting-edge zone on
   these moves. The solid law still reads the shank and the holder at the
   shifted position.
8. The reach law holds a fine bore to the shank fit in the hole, not to
   the flute length. The hole is there already, as for a bore and a ream.

**Why.**

- #1479 asks for an explicit shift: "A guessed default could drag the tip
  across the finished bore, so no default is posted." A choice that cannot
  exist without its shift makes that a type rule. The integer micrometres
  keep `CycleChoice` `Copy` and `Eq`, and they are the lattice the chain
  uses.
- A shift held in the chain cannot disagree with the posted shift. The
  WCS flip, the WCS yaw and the axis mirror already transform the moves and
  the cycle centre together, so the posted `I` and `J` are correct in each
  frame with no new code. A new field on `Cycle` or `CycleRec` would need a
  transform in each of those places, and it would change about 50 struct
  literals in tests.
- The chain as plain moves is not safe on a control: the shift would move
  a turning tool into the finished wall. So the refusal is in the engine,
  for each post that does not declare the cycle. A future post is refused
  until it declares the flag. The author of a post does not have to
  remember the cycle.
- The Haas `G76` takes `I` and `J` as the shift along X and Y (Haas Mill
  Operator's Manual, G76 Fine Boring Canned Cycle). The `Q` form takes its
  direction from Setting 27, which a program cannot state. So the post
  never writes `Q`.
- The verifier models a tool as the cylinder that its turning edge sweeps.
  That cylinder, shifted by `s`, overlaps the bore wall by `s`, and the
  verifier refused each fine bore. With the spindle stopped, the bar
  reaches `bar radius + s` from the hole axis and the tip reaches
  `tool radius - s`. Both are inside the cylinder that the feed in cut
  while `s < tool radius - bar radius`. The feed in was read over that
  same cylinder. The shank and the holder are above the edge zone and are
  not inside that cylinder, so they keep their reading.

**Considered and dropped.**

- A `shift` field on `Cycle` and `CycleRec`, with a `SHIFT` word in the
  `.cl` and `.cnc` texts. Dropped for the reasons above.
- A separate `fine_bore_shift` field on `OpParams::Drill`. It permits a
  fine bore with no shift, and it changes about 70 test files that build a
  drill operation.
- `G76` with `Q` on the Fanuc, Mazak and Doosan posts. The direction of
  `Q` is a control parameter (Fanuc parameter No. 5101). A program cannot
  state it, so the posted shift could go into the wall. These posts refuse.
- Heidenhain `CYCL DEF 202`, Sinumerik `CYCLE86`, Mach4 `G76`. Each needs
  words that the operation does not have (a spindle angle, a disengaging
  direction code), or a word layout that this work did not read from the
  maker's manual. These posts refuse. The follow-up issue names them.
- An expanded chain with `M19`. The orientation word and its angle are
  different on each machine. #1479 asks for a refusal.
- A refusal when `spindle.orientation` is not stated. No shipped machine
  file states it, so each machine would refuse. The unstated-limit law
  already governs `rigid_tapping`; this capability uses the same law. The
  post is the second door.
- A removal of each `RapidInStock` warning of the three rapids. That hides
  a holder that the shift moves into a clamp or a wall. Only the edge zone
  is acquitted.

**What it trusts.** The tip points against the shift at the oriented stop.
This is the user's statement. No geometry in the program can check it. The
bar diameter is the tool's shank diameter. The shift is along the X and Y
of the hole list (the model frame); the post writes it in the frame of the
setup.

**Not done here.**

- No literature search ran. The session had no web access (the fetch was
  refused). The sources are the cycle formats as the worker knows them; no
  page was read in this session. A reviewer must check the Haas `G76`
  block against the Haas manual before a real cut.
- The Machines sheet has no row for `spindle.orientation`. No shipped
  machine file states it.
- Nothing ran on a real control.

**Cost to change later.** A shift field on the records can be added
without a file-format break: the `fine_bore` choice in the project file
already holds `shift_x` and `shift_y` in millimetres. A new post adds the
flag and its own word; no other code changes.

## #1480 - Back bore (G89) carries the dwell and feeds out at the plunge feed

**What was decided.** The drill generator (`camcraft_motion::drilling::drill`)
now writes the user's dwell into the `Cycle` record of a Back bore hole. It
also feeds the tool out at the plunge feed, the same feed as the way in.
Before, the dwell was forced to 0 and the feed out used the cutting feed.

**Why.**
- G89 is "feed in, dwell, feed out" (RS-274/NGC, NIST IR 6556; LinuxCNC
  G-code reference). The cycle exists for its dwell, and the user could not
  get one.
- A canned G89 (and the G85 that several posts write for a Back bore with no
  dwell) has one F word. The post takes that F from the first cutting move
  of the hole's chain, which is the plunge. So the control always fed out at
  the plunge feed. The chain said the cutting feed. The verifier, the
  simulation time and the `.cl` dump then disagreed with the machine. The
  Ream cycle (G85, #1445) already uses the one-feed chain; Back bore now
  uses the same law.
- Each post reads the dwell in seconds from the stream and writes its own
  P unit, or refuses by name. Fanuc, Mazak, Doosan, Haas and Sinumerik write
  whole milliseconds; grblHAL, Tormach, LinuxCNC and Mach4 write seconds;
  Heidenhain writes an explicit dwell block. The lathe posts and the posts
  with no canned cycle refuse the Back bore.
  `crates/post/tests/dwell_cycles_modal_p.rs`, `haas_dwell_cycles.rs`,
  `mach4_post.rs`, `heidenhain_cycles.rs` and `sinumerik_g89_dwell.rs` pin
  these words (#2350, #2360).
- Sinumerik G89 now writes `P0` for zero dwell. This clears a previous
  positive dwell instead of leaving its modal P active. The Siemens
  [ISO dialects Function Manual, 07/2021](https://cache.industry.siemens.com/dl/files/254/109801254/att_1077768/v1/ONE_840Dsl_828D_iso_dialects_fct_man_0721_en-US.pdf),
  table 6-1, printed page 95, gives the G89 dwell unit in milliseconds.
  Section 6.3.1 describes modal cycle parameters. The tests
  `sinumerik_g89_dwell_posts_p_in_milliseconds` and
  `sinumerik_g89_zero_dwell_clears_previous_p` pin the unit and its reset.

**Considered and dropped.**
- Keep the feed out at the cutting feed, and make each post write a second F
  word. A canned cycle has no second F word. A post would have to expand the
  cycle into G1 moves, which changes every Back bore program.
- A separate "retract feed" parameter for bore cycles. This is a new
  parameter and a new command field. It is not necessary for this issue.
- A new G89 golden for each post in this PR. Direct assertions pin each
  P word. The Sinumerik tests also pin the transition from positive dwell
  to zero.

**Cost to change later.** Small. The feed out is one line in
`crates/motion/src/drilling/cycle.rs`, pinned by
`back_bore_feeds_in_and_out_at_the_plunge_feed`. A Back bore program with no
dwell keeps the same F. Its Sinumerik G89 block now includes `P0` to clear
a previous dwell. The `.cl` chain of a Back bore changes its feed-out feed.
On the Heidenhain post,
which writes the Back bore as an explicit chain, the retract line now has
the plunge feed.

## #1481 - The ream on the lathe posts is pinned by tests and goldens; no post changed

**What was decided.** A new test binary, `crates/post/tests/ream_lathe.rs`,
posts an axial ream on the spindle centreline through each shipped lathe
post, on the shipped machine file of that post (`lathe.mch`,
`tormach-15l-slant-pro.mch`). It adds one golden for each lathe post in
`crates/post/tests/golden/ream/`. No post script and no source file
changed.

- `fanuc-lathe` writes one `G85` (never a different cycle), seated on R on
  the centreline, with the expanded chain suppressed and `G80` before the
  exit rapid.
- `tormach-lathe` has no canned cycle. It posts the expanded chain: feed
  in, feed out at the same F, no rapid in the reamed hole.
- A dwell stays with the ream: `G85 P` on `fanuc-lathe`, `G4` at the floor
  on `tormach-lathe`.
- A ream off the spindle axis is refused by name on the two posts.
- `every_lathe_post_is_covered` fails when a `*lathe*.cps` post ships
  without a row in the test.

**Why.** The two posts already post the ream correctly on `upstream/main`
`e048b103c`. The issue asks for the pins, and "Done means" asks for a
golden for each lathe post. On unchanged code only the golden test was
red (the golden files did not exist); the behaviour tests were green.
Three mutations of the post scripts prove that the tests catch a wrong
mapping (see the PR body).

**Considered and dropped.**

- Rows for the lathe posts in `ream_cycle.rs`. Dropped: that test posts on
  `3axis-vmc.mch` with holes off the spindle axis, which a 2-axis lathe
  refuses. The lathe needs its own stream and its own machine files.
- A change to `fanuc-lathe.cps` that suppresses the chain of a refused
  off-axis cycle (it posts today as plain `G01` moves, as `tormach-lathe`
  does not). Dropped: the program has a warning and is never released, and
  the change is not part of this issue.
- A reading of the retract feed of `G85` on a Fanuc T-series control. The
  post states "feed in, feed out at F". This PR pins our mapping only. It
  was not compared with a control manual or a machine.

**Cost to change later.** Low. A change to a lathe post's ream output
moves one golden; regenerate it with
`WRITE_GOLDEN=1 cargo test -p camcraft-post --test ream_lathe` and read
the diff.

## #1521 - Plasma cut data on the torch: slice 1 (the recipe record)

**What was decided.** A plasma torch's cutting row can carry a recipe
(`CuttingRow::plasma`, type `tools::plasma_cut::PlasmaCutData`). The recipe
is keyed by the row's material and the recipe's plate thickness. It states
the kerf and, each optional, the cut height, pierce height, pierce delay,
transfer height, puddle jump (percent of pierce height and dwell), amperage,
arc voltage, the pierce capacity (`max_pierce_thickness`) and an edge-start
mark. The record follows the shape that #1881 gave the waterjet recipe: one
optional field on the row, one file key (`plasma`) on the row's DTO, and
the existing `AddTool` / `ChangeTool` / `ImportTools` commands carry it.

This PR is slice 1 of the five slices that the issue lists, and only the
tool-side part of it. The PR says `Refs #1521`, not `Fixes #1521`. The
issue stays open for the other slices.

**Why.**

- The issue is an umbrella (`effort:max`). The effort check comment on the
  issue recommends one piece of work for each slice. Slice 1 is the base
  that the other slices read.
- A recipe is never picked by its material alone. `row_for`,
  `row_in_tool` and the `Unknown` row logic ignore recipe rows
  (`CuttingRow::is_recipe`). The feed of a 3 mm recipe must not seed an
  operation on 12 mm plate. Selection is `plasma_row_for(material,
  thickness)`, with an exact thickness and no nearest-thickness
  substitution.
- A blank value means "the controller's own table", the same meaning as a
  blank on the plasma operation. There is no default for a height or a
  time.
- A recipe whose plate is thicker than its stated pierce capacity is
  refused, unless the recipe states an edge start. The refusal is at the
  tool door (`refusal_for_kind`), so the command, the project file and the
  tool library all refuse it by name.
- Zero is legal for a height and a time, as on the plasma operation
  (`PlasmaParams::validate`). Thickness, kerf, amperage, arc voltage, the
  capacity and the puddle-jump percent must be above zero.
- A puddle jump without a pierce height is refused: it is a percentage of
  that height.
- The tool editor does not draw a torch recipe in the speed-and-feed
  table, and a plain row for the same material can stand beside it. The
  recipe stays in the draft and survives Apply.

**Considered and dropped.**

- The full "Done means" of the issue in one PR. It is four more slices
  across motion, post, sim and two new machine kinds.
- An editor for the recipes on the tool page. PR #2663 changes that page's
  layout at this time. Until the editor exists, a recipe enters through the
  project file, the tool library and the MCP tool definition
  (`cutting_data[].plasma`).
- "The operation picks a row" and the override commands. They change what
  the operation generates and posts, so they belong with slice 2 and its
  goldens.
- Gas type and gas pressure. A gas name is text and `CuttingRow` is
  `Copy`; the field needs its own design (a fixed gas list, or a row that
  is not `Copy`).
- Multi-stage pierce (0 to 4 stages). Plasma uses one stage. The stage
  list arrives with the laser slice.
- Order rules between the heights (transfer below pierce, cut below
  pierce). Maker charts differ, and the issue does not state such a rule.
- A project file version step. No build reads a recipe for generation
  yet, and three open PRs already move `PROJECT_VERSION`. #1881 added the
  `waterjet` key in the same way. An older build drops the `plasma` key
  and reads the row as a plain material row of the torch.

**Cost to change later.** Slice 2 must take the project version step when
a recipe first changes generated or posted output: from then on an old
reader must refuse the file. A new recipe field is one optional key. A
move to a stage list replaces `pierce_height` / `pierce_delay` and needs a
read migration for files written by this slice.

## #1547 - Ignore unused stored Stepover in load strategies

**Decided:** Apply `!strategy.steps_by_load()` to the positive Stepover check in `Pocket3DParams::validate`.
The diameter check already uses this condition.
Adaptive and Offset rings accept finite stored zero and negative Stepover values.
Their generated moves stay identical to those for a valid Stepover of 3 mm.
Keep the finite parameter check and the optimal load limits.
Zigzag, Waterline and Auto still require a positive Stepover within the tool diameter.

**Why:** Adaptive and Offset rings space passes by optimal load.
They do not read Stepover, and their Passes page hides that field.
An unused stored value must not prevent generation or name a field the user cannot see.
This change needs no new dependency or toolpath algorithm.

**Considered and dropped:** Resetting the stored value would change project data without a machining need.
Asking the user to switch strategies would expose the field but retain an unnecessary refusal.
The tests reuse small fixtures and one depth pass to keep generation below 60 seconds.
The existing zero Stepover refusal assertion now tests Zigzag.
The new generation test covers acceptance under both load strategies.

**Cost to change later:** A strategy that starts to read Stepover must update its validation and its Passes page together.
The generation and refusal tests must then cover that new rule.

## #1591 - 3D Adaptive: Method choice with a Trochoidal method per level

**What was decided**

- `OpParams::Pocket3D` has a `method` field (`AdaptiveMethod`: Spiral or
  Trochoidal). It is read only under the Adaptive strategy. The default
  is Spiral.
- Under Trochoidal, each level of the plain ladder is planned by the 2D
  lane planner (`plan_all_lanes`, `plan_cleanup`) on the cutter-centre
  area that the ladder already has. The new module
  `machining2d::adaptive_troch_level` plans, posts and checks one level.
  `machining3d::troch` holds the run state and the new entry point
  `pocket3d_trochoidal`.
- A level that the method refuses is cut by the Spiral plan. A note says
  why and names the Z of the level. The level is built on a copy of the
  path, so a refusal posts nothing of the trochoidal attempt.
- The material top is proved, not assumed. A trochoidal level can leave
  stock, so a later bore or plunge starts above the deepest trochoidal
  level whose cleared area holds its disc. If no level holds it, the
  bore starts above the stock top. A proved bore starts on the proved
  plane, as the ladder's own descents do. Thus the helices of two levels
  share no depth and cannot cross.
- In a trochoidal run, each level enters as a first level does. This
  includes a fallback (Spiral) level below a fallback level. No level
  reads the plane above as cleared. The cost is a longer descent in air
  on a run where many levels fall back.
- Each posted level is checked against its level area and against the
  crossing law. The crossing check reads the level's own moves and all
  moves before it.
- The rest pass, the offset shells and the rotary wrap keep the plan
  that they had. Their existing notes say so.
- The method is passed as an argument of the internal `ladder`, not as a
  field of `Pocket3DParams`.
- The project file writes `method` as a word for each 3D Pocket, as 2D
  Adaptive does. A file without the word reads as `spiral`. No format
  version was added.
- The stamp gets one more byte only under Adaptive with Trochoidal.
- Under Trochoidal the footprint does not use the Adaptive air band
  (#1950). The loops are not planned from the air.

**Why**

- The level area of the ladder is the level law: footprint less the
  part above the plane, eroded by the tool radius and the stock to
  leave. Loops inside it are inside the level area and beside the
  model. The posted level is checked again, move by move.
- The 3D descents (`descent.rs`) read the plane above as the material
  top. That is true after a Spiral or ring level. It is not true after
  a trochoidal level that left stock. A rapid to that plane could hit
  stock. Thus a trochoidal run proves the top or uses the stock top.
- After a trochoidal level the tool is at the end of that level, not on
  the plane of an older fallback level. A keep-down level link would
  feed from there through stock that the loops left. The "Do not touch"
  keep-out of #2149 also reads the plane above as the top of the band
  that a descent crosses. With no plane above, the keep-out covers the
  full height, which a bore from the stock top needs.
- A level area of a 3D part is often narrow near a wall. A refusal of
  the whole operation for one such level makes the method hard to use.
  The issue permits a fallback by name.
- A `method` field in `Pocket3DParams` changes 74 struct literals in 28
  test files. An argument of `ladder` changes 7 internal call sites.
- A Spiral operation has the same stamp as before. Existing 3D
  Adaptive operations do not go Stale.
- The MCP params patch refuses a key that does not come back from the
  typed round trip. An unwritten default made `"method": "spiral"` an
  unknown field. Thus the word is always written.
- 2D Adaptive added its `method` word without a format version (#1509).
  This change follows that precedent.

**What was considered and dropped**

- Refuse the operation when one level cannot be cut by loops. Dropped:
  see above.
- Offset rings as the fallback of a refused level. Dropped: the Spiral
  plan is the other value of the same choice, and it already falls back
  to rings by name.
- Record a fallback level as fully cleared, so that the next bore starts
  lower. Dropped: the HSM plan can leave stock inside its own budget.
  The cost is a longer bore helix in air below a fallback level.
- The four trochoidal controls of 2D Adaptive (#1588: engagement limit,
  return, return feed, loop width) on the 3D page. Dropped from this
  change: the issue asks for the Method choice only. The 3D method uses
  the defaults (90 deg, automatic return).
- A trochoidal rest pass or trochoidal offset shells. Dropped: the rest
  targets are sim crumbs and the shells lift vertices off the plane.
  The lane planner proves its loops on a plane.
- Write `method` only when it is `trochoidal`, to keep the bytes of a
  Spiral operation. Dropped: MCP could then not set the method back to
  Spiral (see above).
- A project format version for the new word. Dropped: an older build
  ignores the unknown word and cuts the Spiral plan, which is a legal
  program for the same operation.

**What it costs to change later**

- A `method` field in `Pocket3DParams` instead of the argument: a
  mechanical edit of the struct literals.
- Trochoidal controls on the 3D page: `troch::Run::level` passes
  `AdaptiveTrochParams::default()` at one place.
- A format version for the word: one constant and one migration note.

### Latest review corrections

**What was decided**

- Save protection data with project format 73. Add the forward migration
  from format 72, default absent protection, and preserve linked model
  source data.
- Select the convex welded bore wall in the UI cost fixture. Require two
  closed horizontal rims with matching XY bounds and different heights.
  Require the nonzero XY turns to have the same sign.
- Separate the protection command and generation tests from the project
  persistence tests. Keep shared fixtures in a support module. Keep each
  file below 400 lines.

**Why**

- The existing format 72 reader supports linked model sources but ignores
  unknown area fields. It can discard protection data. Format 73 makes
  that reader refuse the file before it can generate an unprotected path.
- Upstream STEP refinements changed the face strip counts. Horizontal
  rims alone can select the concave outer figure-eight wall, whose refined
  points fail preview triangulation. The convex rim identifies the bore
  wall needed by the filled area preview checks. The assertions remain
  unchanged.
- The separate files follow the command and persistence domains and keep
  the source files within the repository size limit.

**What was considered and dropped**

- Keep format 72 or compare only with a format 71 reader. Dropped: neither
  proves refusal by the existing format 72 reader.
- Keep the strip-count selector or select the largest wall with matching
  horizontal rims. Dropped: both can select the concave outer wall and
  fail preview triangulation.
- Remove the filled preview assertions. Dropped: the assertions check the
  required preview.
- Keep all protection tests in one file. Dropped: the file exceeds the
  source size limit and combines separate test domains.

**What it costs to change later**

- A later project format change needs another forward migration and a
  check of the older reader boundary.
- A different fixture needs the same wall geometry and filled preview
  assertions. Shared fixture changes must still cover both test domains.

## #1619 - Tormach lathe G76: the grid J makes R1's ladder cut the record's passes

**Decided.** `g76Grid` in `assets/posts/tormach-lathe.cps` no longer takes
J (first depth) to the grid with a plain `floor`. LinuxCNC's G76 with R1
("constant depth", public LinuxCNC G-code reference) cuts J, 2J, ... with
the last pass clamped at K, so ceil(K/J) passes. The record lays
n = ceil(height / first depth) equal rungs, so J must satisfy
(n-1)J < K <= nJ. J is the shallower grid rounding when that holds;
when the shallower J would add a pass, it is the one grid step up, never
a full grid step heavier than the record's first cut. When no grid J
meets both, the record is refused by name ("no first depth J on the
control's grid makes R1's equal ladder cut the record's n passes").

**Why.** The inch golden posted J0.0314 K0.0944: ceil(0.0944 / 0.0314) = 4
passes where the record laid and the verdict judged 3. J0.0315 is
0.000004 in (0.1 um) over the record's 0.8 mm on the diameter and cuts
0.0315, 0.0630, 0.0944: three passes, the root still rounded outward.
A scan of realistic records (first depth 0.05-0.5 mm, height 0.3-2 mm,
four minor diameters, the stream's half-micron lattice) found the old
rule mis-stating 2.7% of inch records and the new rule refusing none in
either unit; mm words are unchanged (2 x first depth already sits on the
0.001 mm grid).

**Considered and dropped.**
- Shrinking K (root further outward) to fit the floored J: the thread
  would be cut short of its minor by up to n grid steps, a thread not to
  depth.
- Refusing whenever the floored J miscounts: it refused the plain M12x2
  inch fixture, a common thread, for a 0.1 um difference.

**Cost to change later.** One function in the post script and the inch
G76 golden's J word.

**Simulator verification.** `crates/app/tests/golden/nc/tormach-lathe/thread_g76_inch.nc`
(`G0 X0.4764`, `G0 Z0.5512`, `G76 P0.07874 Z0.315 I-0.004 J0.0315 K0.0944 R1 Q0 H0`)
was run by mkinney on PathPilot Hub 8L SIM (PathPilot v2.14.4, 2026-11-18
12:42 PDT; G54 Z offset shifted `-4.5040` -> `-4.6040` for the simulator's
Z travel). Observed X (DIA) and Z DRO readings from a 10 fps screen
recording:
- Pass 1 bottom: X (DIA) `0.4409` (depth `0.0315`, Z `0.5512 -> 0.3150`)
- Pass 2 bottom: X (DIA) `0.4094` (depth `0.0630`, Z `0.5512 -> 0.3150`)
- Pass 3 bottom: X (DIA) `0.3780` (depth `0.0944`, Z `0.5512 -> 0.3150`)
- Three cutting passes, no spring pass (`H0`), returned to `X 0.4764 Z 0.9449`,
  ran to `M30` (last line 19, cycle time `00:00:06`) with no alarm.

# Decisions - issue #1696

## #1696 - the Report door: a prefilled GitHub issue and a clipboard screenshot

**What was decided.** A Report door on the status strip opens a small
window. It takes a short title, and its two buttons ("Report a bug",
"Request a feature") open the browser on a prefilled new-issue URL:
`https://github.com/NeoTech/Camcraft/issues/new?title=...&body=...&labels=...`
(no `template` parameter: the prefill query applies to the blank issue,
and the repository enables blank issues in
`.github/ISSUE_TEMPLATE/config.yml`). The body embeds the Debug info
report (#157) - same fields, one source. A "Copy screenshot" button puts
a PNG of the whole application window on the clipboard (see the
full-window follow-up below); the user pastes it into the issue box and
GitHub uploads it. The repository also gained `blank-issue.md` and a
`config.yml` that enables blank issues.

**Why.** The maintainer asked (issue #1696) for one button that prepares
a bug or feature report with a screenshot and the relevant data
attached. GitHub's prefill query is the only documented way to fill a
new issue from an app, and it works only on a blank template. egui's
`Context::open_url` and `Context::copy_image` exist in the pinned
egui 0.36.2 and are already plumbed by the shell's platform-output
handler, so no new dependency is needed.

**Considered and dropped.**
- Opening the existing issue FORMS (`bug.yml`, `feature.yml`) prefilled:
  GitHub ignores the query on issue forms (community discussion
  orgs/community#15477). The blank template plus the `labels` query
  reproduces their `bug` / `enhancement` labels.
- Attaching the PNG file from the app: a browser cannot receive a file
  from another program. The clipboard paste is the shortest path, and
  GitHub uploads a pasted picture on its own.
- The GPU `snapshot_rgba()` path for the picture: the viewport's own
  readback needs a device and is unused by the app. The CPU raster
  (`camcraft_app::raster`, the MCP `render_stock` path) works headless
  and deterministic.
- Writing the report body through a new command: the window writes only
  view state (an open flag, a title string), the same class as the
  Debug info window's state, so "Everything Is a Command" does not
  apply.

**Cost to change later.** The URL and the label names are constants in
`report.rs`; a fork pointing at its own repo changes one constant. If
GitHub later lets a URL prefill an issue form, the app code needs no
change: the same query works on that form.

## #1696 follow-up - the screenshot's ground grid (GUI test finding,
superseded by the full-window design below)

**What was decided.** The maintainer's first GUI test found the CPU-raster
shot's background grid wrong: dark scratch lines over the part. The fix
gave the raster shot its own floor grid. That whole path was then
superseded (next section): the shot is now the real window, so the grid
problem cannot occur. The raster additions it needed (`Canvas::ground_line`,
`Camera::scale`, the `interact` visibility widenings) were reverted;
nothing else used them.

## #1696 follow-up - a full-window shot from the real renderer (GUI test
finding)

**What was decided.** The maintainer's second GUI test said the shot must
be the whole application window, not just the 3D model area. The door now
asks the shell for a window picture the way egui intends: the report path
pushes `egui::ViewportCommand::Screenshot` with a private token. The frame
loop (`shell_window/capture.rs`) sees the command in the root viewport's
output and, in the same frame after the normal egui pass, draws the same
tessellated shapes a second time into a private texture
(`RENDER_ATTACHMENT | COPY_SRC`, the surface config's size and format)
in its own render pass. It then copies the texture to a mapped buffer and
answers egui with `egui::Event::Screenshot`, which the door reads: on a
matching token it copies the picture to the clipboard with
`Context::copy_image` and says so in the status line. SolidCraft
(tangency-labs/solidcraft) was read as mechanism reference only -
their public API use, no code, no look (their brand licence).

**Why.** egui's own screenshot responder lives in eframe; our shell
drives winit and `egui_wgpu::Renderer` itself, so nobody else answers the
command. A second pass in the same frame is the only way to catch the
window as the user just saw it: the report dialog the user pressed is
still up, and its shapes are already tessellated. Reading back the
surface texture itself is not possible: wgpu does not make the swap-chain
texture a copy source. `egui_wgpu`'s own `capture` feature was dropped
without trying: its readback rejects the `Bgra8UnormSrgb` surface format
ours uses, and enabling the feature edits Cargo.toml for one call we must
rewrite anyway. A CPU raster cannot show panels, the ribbon or the dialog -
that was exactly the complaint.

**Sub-decisions taken with it.**
- Token law: `egui::UserData::eq` compares `Arc::ptr_eq`, and Rust
  allocates nothing for a zero-sized payload, so every `UserData::new(())`
  shares one pointer and all tokens compare equal. The shot token is a
  `OnceLock` `UserData` over a non-zero string; the unit test
  `the_shot_token_matches_only_itself` pins both halves of the law.
- Delivery: egui 0.36.2 has no `Context::send_event`, so the map callback
  posts over an `mpsc` channel and the frame loop drains it into
  `raw_input.events` before `ctx.run_ui`. The loop keeps
  `request_redraw` alive while a readback is in flight, so the answer
  lands without user input.
- Format: the swizzle table maps RGBA (0,1,2,3) and BGRA (2,1,0,3);
  the raw read-back of an sRGB format is already sRGB-encoded, so no
  gamma step runs. Any other surface format refuses with a logged status
  line - a wrong-byte-order picture would mis-report colours silently.
- Test law: the kittest harness (wgpu/snapshot features) answers
  screenshot requests itself with the requester's own token. The
  foreign-token test therefore makes no request at all: only the injected
  foreign answer could trigger a copy there.

## #1700 - A stock copied from an incomplete model keeps naming its hole

**Decided:** a `FromModel` stock copy carries its source's hole
(`schema::MeshOpen`) itself, beside the fidelity-unknown sentinel it
already carried (#1056, #1610). Every path that lands the sentinel on a
copy lands the hole with it: `SetStock` and its undo, a setup clone
(`CreateSetup` with a datum), an undone `DeleteSetup`, `UpdateModel`'s
refresh of the copies and its undo, and the project loader. The refusal
(`model_fidelity::op_problem`) reads the hole off the entity that carries
the sentinel, so a copy's refusal still names its source and that hole
once the source is deleted. `mesh_open::hole_behind` is
`model_fidelity::chord_behind`'s twin, and `mesh_open::note_for` gives the
words for a hole already in hand.

**Why:** the copy's refusal read the hole from the source model by name
(`mesh_open::unknown_note`). With the source deleted that lookup found
nothing, and the refusal fell back to "saved before CamCraft recorded
mesh fidelity (project v58 or older)", which is the wrong reason for that
mesh. The post still refused it; only the words were wrong. The copy
already held the sentinel for exactly this case (#1056: "keeps it when
the model is deleted or renamed"), so the hole now rides the same way.

**File format:** the saver already wrote `mesh_open` for any entity that
has one. The loader now also accepts it on a `FromModel` stock marked
`fidelity_unknown`, and a hole without the mark stays corrupt. Commit
`35b3422cf` (#1610) shipped in `v0.21.0` through `v0.24.0`, where
`validate.rs` refuses `mesh_open` on any entity that is not a model
marked `fidelity_unknown` as corrupt. A project file written with a hole
on a `FromModel` stock row therefore does not open in `v0.21.0` to
`v0.24.0`, making this an incompatible project-file change (marked with
`fix(fidelity)!:` and a `BREAKING CHANGE:` footer).

**Review follow-up (PR #2024):**
- **Released `v0.21.0`–`v0.24.0` files:** those builds wrote
  `fidelity_unknown: true` on the stock copy and `mesh_open` only on the
  source model. `model_fidelity::adopt_copies` now heals such a copy on
  load from its live source (so deleting the source later keeps the hole
  and re-saving repairs the file), and `model_fidelity::coarse_source`
  falls back to the source's hole if an unhealed copy has none. Pinned
  by `a_v021_to_v024_copy_without_its_own_hole_keeps_naming_its_sources_hole`
  in `crates/app/tests/stock_copy_hole.rs`.
- **Project version:** kept unbumped on this branch (`67`, unchanged
  from its `upstream/main` merge base) rather than bumping `67` to `68`
  (which would conflict with `upstream/main`'s `v68`–`v71` ladder) or
  pulling `upstream/main` and bumping past `v71`. `upstream/main` is
  already at `v71` (above `v0.21.0`–`v0.24.0`'s `v61`–`v69`), so merged
  saves already trigger `UnsupportedVersion` in those releases, while any
  pre-#1700 `v67`–`v71` build fails closed as corrupt rather than dropping
  the hole. Cost to change later: one `PROJECT_VERSION` bump and
  no-op migration rung if a version refusal is wanted against unreleased
  pre-#1700 `v71` builds.

**Considered and dropped:**
- Keeping a tombstone of the deleted source's hole (by name) in the
  world, which would have given a second source of truth.
- Looking up a copy of the deleted source by name at refusal time. That
  has more than one possible answer when two setups each copy the model,
  and it is wrong after a rename.

**Cost to change later:** the hole is one optional component on the copy,
written beside the sentinel at the six sites listed above. Pinned by
`crates/app/tests/stock_copy_hole.rs`.

## #1708 - the finish3d gap link: a straight line across gap openings

**What was decided.** A `gap_link` parameter on the Finish3D parameters,
a dropdown with two options:

- `Jump` (default): the existing retract/clearance hop, byte for byte as
  every older file wrote it.
- `Straight`: one straight Feed link from the end of one run to the start
  of the next, at the two end points' own tip height - no rise, no
  traverse, no plunge.

The law for `Straight` (new file `crates/motion/src/finishing3d/gaplink.rs`):
both run ends stand at tangent centers by the march's own construction, so
the line is fixed and nothing is chosen for it. The exact segment-triangle
sweep of the move at the budget `r - TOUCH_EPS` answers the whole question:
a grazing contact at the rim passes (tangency is the law's own currency),
a real bite refuses. A refused link takes the `Jump` hop. `ramp`'s
certified diagonal still takes the break first where it can be struck.

The same commit fixes the raster serpentine for a line broken by openings:
a back line now reverses WHOLE (`pieces.reverse()` plus each piece's points).
Reversing only the points kept the pieces in grid order, so the chain ran
one piece backwards and then jumped back across the whole field to the next
piece's far end. Under the plain hop that mis-pairing hid inside a high
rapid; a straight link authors the same line at the cut, where it shows.

**Naming and the stored word.** The maintainer's verdict after a GUI
try-out (chat, 2026-11-14): keep only `Jump` and `Straight` in this PR.
An intermediate build had offered three options (`Lift`, `Bridge` - the
lowest facet-certified traverse height - and `Straight`); `Bridge` is
dropped, and the default option's word is `Jump`, not `Lift`. The project
digest takes tag `0x4D` plus a variant byte only when the choice is not
`Jump`, so every op that hops as before keeps the stamp it had. The file
words are `jump` and `straight`, written always, like `ramp` - new words
in an existing grammar, no version step-up.

**Why.** On the maintainer's part (a 171 mm STEP model with many holes)
every hole broke the raster line and each break lifted to the retract
plane. The moves looked wrong in the GUI and the air hops cost cycle time.
A straight rim-to-rim link at cut height is the smoothest answer; the
sweep verdict keeps the Prime Directive - only a certified non-cutting
line is authored, anything else falls back to the hop.

**Considered and dropped.**

- `Bridge` (lowest certified traverse) in the shipped dropdown: the
  maintainer asked for the two-option surface only; the code for it was
  not carried over. A later issue can re-add it under its own law.
- Auto-lowest-hop with no parameter: the maintainer chose the explicit
  dropdown; the default must write the old bytes.
- Land-model lid work (an earlier experiment to close openings for the
  march): dropped, it did not work reliably.
- Splines or curves for the link path: the named future direction
  ("later we can add splines and curves for how to connect them"); a
  future link type under the same certify-or-hop law.

**Cost to change later.** Low to add link types: the ladder in
`emit_runs` is one branch per type, each certify-or-fall.

## #1807 - Keep Circular ramp transitions at depth

**Decided:** For an explicit Circular Ramp entry, limit the effective
`approach.plunge_height` to 0.1 mm. Keep a lower configured value. Use
`entry_top(material_top)` to place this gap above the remaining material.
The hole top alone does not establish the remaining stock height.

Replace the default Clearance level link with the existing certified
KeepDown link when the effective transition is also Ramp and
`approach.ramp_to_depth` is false. Keep an explicit Retract link and the
links for other transition types. Keep the ring order, the lifts between
rings, the final retract, the entry refusals, and the ramp angle law.

**Why:** A closed ring ends at its next ramp start. The existing link
proof can certify the connection on the floor just cut. This removes
the unnecessary clearance trip without adding a new safety proof. A
small initial gap reduces the ramp travel through air. The remaining
material height keeps the rapid above stock carried over the hole top.

**Dropped:** Keep the clearance trip and feed its final descent segment.
That option retains the extra travel. Change the shared ladder code.
That option would change operations outside Circular. Use the hole top
as the stock top. That option can put a rapid into uncut stock.

**Cost to change later:** Change the local Circular parameter adaptation
and update its motion pins, application safety test, and Ramp golden.

## #1847 - Thread infeed tools for MCP

**What was decided:** Add `get_thread_infeed` and `set_thread_infeed` over the existing `EditOperationParams` command. Return every plan field, including defaults. Accept partial updates. Refuse unknown fields. Use the project DTO to decode values. Let the existing command validate the machining parameters.

**Why:** Project JSON omits the default plan and default flags. The generic editor checks whether a patch survives project serialization. That check refuses some resets to default values. Explicit read values let an MCP caller inspect and restore the complete plan. The command preserves validation and undo behavior.

**Considered and dropped:** A broad change to the generic editor would affect unrelated operation types. Direct ECS writes would bypass command validation and undo. A new command or dependency would duplicate existing support. Separate machining validators would repeat domain rules.

**Cost to change later:** A new plan field requires an update to the tool schema, explicit JSON view and tests. A shared explicit representation could replace this view if more callers need it.

## #1862 - A DXF profile on the stock of a setup, and the virtual model reference

The maintainer's words (issue 1862, 2026-11-15): "A DXF should be possible to
"place" on a stock and used as references for cutting - not be treated like a
model - thus for processes like wireedm, plasma, laser, etc etc.. we can just
make a sheet, cube, cylinder. place the DXF - and select operations accordingly.
The Adding DXF Profile, should thus live on "Stock page" and have a "virtual"
model reference, just so the operations pages gets happy about a model being
loaded.."

### What a profile is in the ECS

- **A `Sketch` component on a named entity** (`crates/app/src/schema.rs`),
  beside `Name` and `Location`. It holds `setup: Option<String>` (the
  declared-vs-effective law of `Operation::setup`) and `data:
  Arc<SketchData>`. The entity never has `Facets`, and `model::is_model` is
  false for it, so the part readers (`model::model_entities`) and each 3D
  solid tool do not see it.
- **`SketchData` is in `camcraft-geometry`** (`sketch_data`), not in `app`:
  it works only on domain values. It holds the primitives in millimetres, the
  layer names, the source units (the file's `$INSUNITS` and the unit applied),
  the join tolerance, the chains of issue 1861 and the import summary. Its
  fields are private and the two constructors make the chains, so the stored
  chains are always the chains of the stored primitives.
- **The `Location` of a profile is relative to the stock**, as the scope
  change says: the frame is the top face of the stock of the setup, at the
  stock origin, turned with the stock (`sketch::face_frame`). The stock origin
  is the origin of the stock entity (for a box and a cylinder: the centre in
  XY). The top is the box height, the cylinder height, or the highest facet Z
  of a stock made from a model. A profile has Z 0 and a turn about the face
  normal only. Because the placement is relative, a moved or resized stock
  carries the profile, and nothing must follow it by a second command. The
  stock is setup furniture, so a setup's part alignment does not move the
  profile.
- **Deleting the entity frees the drawing.** The component is a Rust-owned
  type; the last `Arc` holder drops the data
  (`deleting_the_entity_frees_its_drawing`).

### The commands

- **`ImportDxf::new(world, setup, path, options)`** reads, checks and chains
  the file at construction. `setup` is the new argument (`None`: the active
  setup). A setup without a stock is refused ("make a stock first"). A file
  with no unit and no unit from the caller is the typed
  `CommandError::DxfUnitsMissing`; it has the drawing extents, so the UI of
  issue 1863 can show them in each unit before it asks. A unit from the caller
  wins over the unit of the file (the argument is an override).
- **`MoveSketch` moves a profile; `MoveModel` refuses one by name.** The issue
  body said `MoveModel`. That was written before the scope change. `MoveModel`
  writes a world placement and carries the stock; a profile has a face
  placement (X, Y, angle) and rides the stock. Two verbs on one object would
  split the undo story (the "pages own their verbs" law of `MoveModel`), so
  the profile has its own command and the placement cannot leave the face.
  Dropped: a `MoveModel` that accepts a profile and silently drops Z and tilt.
- **A name from the file stem is made unique** (`plate`, `plate (2)`), so one
  drawing can be placed more than one time on a sheet. A stated name that is
  in use is refused.
- **`DeleteSetup` refuses a setup with a placed profile** (as it refuses one
  with operations). Dropped: deleting the profiles with the setup, which loses
  work without a word.
- The Z of the drawing (`Document::elevation`) is not used: the profile lies
  on the stock face.

### What the virtual model reference is

- **It is derived, not stored**: `sketch_model::of(world, setup)` is `Some`
  when the setup has one or more placed profiles and the document has no part
  (a model that is not a fixture). No component and no file key holds it, so
  it cannot disagree with the document. Dropped: a tag component or a
  placeholder model entity. A placeholder entity must be kept in step by each
  command that adds or removes a model or a profile, and a facet-less "model"
  in `model_entities` is the zero-triangle mesh that the issue forbids.
- **It has no facets.** It names profiles only.
- **An operation refers to a profile as `SrcRef::Entity(<profile name>)`.**

### Which checks read it

| Check | Reads | Result on a virtual reference |
|---|---|---|
| The source door of each operation command (`gates::valid_src`, `sketch_gate`: create, paste, retarget, retype, move to a setup) | `sketch_model::source_problem` | A profile is a source for the 2D milling, plasma and wire EDM sections, in its own setup. Each other kind refuses: "needs a solid model - '<name>' is a DXF profile, a virtual model reference with no solid". |
| The same door, 3D milling and multi-axis sections, each source | `sketch_model::of` | Refused: "a <kind> operation needs a solid model - the setup has only its stock and the DXF profile ..." |
| The model-height diagnostic (`operation::missing_source`, Top/Bottom of Model) | `sketch_model::of` | The text names the virtual reference and says to use a stock or fixed height. It is not "no model loaded". The height has no value: a reference with no solid has no top and no bottom. |
| The generation door (`operation::collect_job`) | `sketch_model::generation_problem` | Refused by name with what the operation is checked against (the stock and the chains). |
| `get_job` (MCP) | `sketch_model::of`, `checked_against` | Each setup has `model_reference` (`solid`, `virtual` with its profiles, or null); an operation on a profile has `checks_against`. |
| The operation pages (issue 1863) | `sketch_model::model_loaded` | True for a part or a virtual reference. |

Checks that need a solid part keep their refusal: part alignment and locate
("import a model first"), fit stock to models, the WCS box points of a model,
mesh repair, fixture tags, stock from a model.

### Why nothing passes silently

This PR does not make a toolpath from profile chains: that is issue 1864
(chain picks, side and direction per chain, stock and crossing checks without
a mesh). Until then generation of an operation on a profile is refused by name,
so no gouge, collision or verify check can pass because the model is virtual.
The operation has no toolpath, and the post gate refuses it.

### What the project file stores

- A profile is an entity row with `kind: "sketch"`. Its `translation` and
  `rotation` are the face placement. Its `sketch` key has: `setup`, `insunits`
  (the code the file stated, 0 for none), `unit` (the `$INSUNITS` code of the
  unit applied), `join_tolerance`, `layers`, `primitives` (mm, radians; each
  names its layer by index), and the import counts (`entities`, `vertices`,
  `skipped`).
- **The chains are not stored.** They are made again from the primitives at
  load, by the same `chain()` call as at import. Dropped: storing the chains.
  A stored chain can disagree with its primitives after a hand edit, and the
  chain identities of issue 1861 do not depend on the order of the input.
- **The virtual model reference is not stored.**
- Each profile is read and chained before any world write. A profile off its
  face, with an unknown unit code or with primitives that do not chain refuses
  the file by name.
- **`PROJECT_VERSION` 70 -> 71.** Main uses v67 to v70 for the WCS flip
  (#1720), the drill break-through mode (#2441), the 2D Adaptive move
  (#1517) and the holder reference (#2016). Profiles use the next version,
  v71. A v70 file steps up unchanged; the trunnion data, stated RTCP mode,
  tilt basis, earlier cutting-data rows and breakthrough values remain
  intact. An older reader refuses a v71 file before it can discard a
  profile. Dropped: sharing a version with main, which
  lets an older reader discard data it cannot represent.

### What it costs to change later

- A stored reference or stored chains need a new project version and a
  migration.
- If Top/Bottom of Model must have a value on a virtual reference (for
  example the stock top and the stock bottom), `operation::resolve_height`
  gets one arm; operations saved before that keep the refusal until then.
- A profile on a different stock face (a side, the bottom) needs a face
  choice on `Sketch` and in the file.

### PR #2134 review fixes

- **Reserve the stock source word without regard to letter case.** Explicit
  profile names such as `stock` and `STOCK` are refused. The same file stems
  use the existing `profile` fallback and unique-name handling. The MCP
  source reader treats these words as stock, so accepting them as profile
  names could silently select different geometry. Dropped: accepting
  ambiguous aliases or changing the source-reference format for this fix.
  An unambiguous source-reference format later needs coordinated changes to
  the source reader and its callers.
- **Validate summary counts in both `SketchData` constructors.** Entity and
  vertex counts must fit the default DXF import limits. The skipped counts
  are added with checked arithmetic, and their total must fit the entity
  limit. This check runs before the empty-drawing refusal. The validated
  total is retained for `profile_view`, so it never adds untrusted counts.
  Invalid stored summaries become the existing project error naming the
  profile before any world write. Dropped: unchecked addition, a panic, or
  saturating addition that hides invalid saved data. Changing these limits
  later requires changing the constructor validation and its pins; no new
  project field or version is needed for the derived total.

### PR #2134 merge refresh

- Keep both `rest_dto` and `sketch_dto` in the project module. They store
  separate data. Dropped: taking either module list alone, which loses the
  other feature's file types.
- The first refresh kept project version 63 because main still wrote
  version 62 after #1817. Its rest parameters were additive optional keys.
  That decision is superseded by the next refresh below.

### PR #2134 breakthrough format refresh

- This choice is superseded by the cutting-data and tilt-basis refreshes
  below. Merge main's v63 breakthrough format and give profiles v64. Keep both
  project modules and all breakthrough fields. The v63-to-v64 migration
  preserves the document data. The v62 migration remains in the chain.
  Dropped: retaining version 63 for profiles, because two formats with one
  version let an older reader remove a stated breakthrough on save.
- Pin a v63 breakthrough file through load, save as v64, and load again.
  Pin the profile and rest payloads in the v64 round trip. These checks
  protect the stored travel limit and the profile data together.


### PR #2134 cutting-data format refresh

- This choice is superseded by the tilt-basis refresh below.
  The breakthrough refresh's choice of v64 for profiles is superseded:
  main now uses v64 for #2015's cutting-data rows and stock material.
  Merge that format intact and give the profile row v65. Keep main's
  v63-to-v64 migration and add the v64-to-v65 step; neither needs a data
  rewrite. Dropped: sharing v64, because an older build could open and
  save away data belonging to the other format.
- Keep both profile and stock-material state in `DeleteEntity`, and both
  DXF unit-code APIs. They serve separate callers and can coexist.
  Dropped: taking either conflict side alone, which removes the other
  feature's state restoration or unit API.
- Keep the v63 breakthrough pin and update the profile and combined
  persistence pins to write v65. The earlier migration must continue to

- Additional refresh pins: `a_v64_cutting_row_steps_up_without_losing_its_limits`,
  `delete_undo_keeps_both_stock_material_and_profile_drawing`, and
  `all_drawing_units_keep_both_persistence_code_apis`. They cover the v64

- This choice is superseded by the trunnion-format refresh below. Merge

- Pin a v65 tilt with legacy basis 0 and with basis 1 through load, save as

## #1864 - 2D Contour on DXF sketches: layer/chain picking, per-chain overrides, and sketch verify

Maintainer request from #1452 ("We should be able to load DXF file to do profile cuts on."), continuing #1862 and #1863.

### What was decided and why

- **Extend `FeatureSel` with `SketchChain(ChainId)` and `SketchLayer(String)` (`crates/app/src/operation/types/sel.rs`).**
  `FeatureSel` drops `Copy` and derives `Clone` so `SketchLayer` can carry the layer name directly across UI state, commands, MCP IDs (`sketch_chain:<hex>` / `sketch_layer:<name>`), and `PROJECT_VERSION = 74` (`crates/app/src/project/file.rs`).
  - *Dropped*: interning DXF layer names into numeric IDs or resolving layers into fixed chain lists at pick time. Expanding a layer pick dynamically during resolution (`crates/app/src/operation/contour_sketch_pick.rs`) keeps layer picks accurate when a DXF sketch is reloaded.
- **Additive per-chain overrides on `OpParams::Contour` (`ChainOverride` in `crates/app/src/operation/types/params.rs` and `crates/app/src/operation/types/sel.rs`).**
  Each override keys on `(entity, chain: ChainId)` with optional `side: Option<ChainSide>` and `reverse: bool` (`#[serde(default, skip_serializing_if = "Vec::is_empty")]`). `PROJECT_VERSION` steps from `73` to `74` (main took v73 for #2055) so older builds refuse files carrying sketch picks or per-chain overrides instead of silently dropping them, while v73 files load unchanged.
  - *Dropped*: attaching `side`/`reverse` onto `GeoSel` itself (which would break layer picks and prevent plain selection equality) or minting a separate sketch-only operation variant. Storing `chain_overrides` on `OpParams::Contour` reuses the standard `EditOperationParams` undo/redo and `GenStamp` staleness checks, while `SetOperationGeometry::with_chain_overrides` lets MCP callers update picks and overrides in one undo step.
