- **Natural nesting when uniform, ordered per-chain generation when overridden (`crates/app/src/operation/contour_sketch.rs`).**
  Whole sketches (`SrcRef::Entity`) and layer/chain picks with unmodified `Auto` sides and uniform `climb` check `can_group_natural` and cut as one nested `Region` (holes Inside, outers Outside). When per-chain `side` or `reverse` overrides diverge, closed chains generate in hole-before-outer order so inner bores clear while the part still holds them. Preserved closed polylines and sampled arcs keep true CL `ArcMove` geometry so `posting` emits `G2`/`G3`.
- **Explicit open-chain safety (`validate_plan` in `crates/app/src/operation/contour_sketch.rs`).**
  Open DXF chains cut along the centerline only. Operation-level `Side::Inside`/`Side::Outside`, any per-chain `ChainSide` override on an open chain, and control/wear compensation (`G41`/`G42`) refuse by name, naming the sketch chain; `reverse: true` remains allowed to flip centerline direction.
  - *Dropped*: guessing an inside/outside side from winding or open endpoints, which causes silent undercuts or wrong compensation.
- **Meshless generation and verification (`crates/app/src/sketch_model.rs`, `crates/app/src/operation/material.rs`, `crates/app/src/operation/job.rs`).**
  `sketch_model::generation_problem` admits `OpParams::Contour`, and `material::named_material` returns the placed sketch stock-top height with empty facets for `Sketch` entities (`part_solid = false`). Unresolved `TopOfModel`/`BottomOfModel` heights still refuse via `sketch_model::NO_SOLID_HEIGHT`. Stock removal (`stock_sim::simulate_document`), crossing, stock-rapid, and fixture collision checks run against setup stock and fixtures without requiring a 3D solid mesh.
- **Ray-to-curve picking and UI workflow (`crates/app/src/pick/sketch_pick.rs`, `crates/ui/src/edge_pick.rs`, `crates/ui/src/egui_app/geo_page.rs`, `crates/ui/src/egui_app/mill2d_page.rs`).**
  `pick_feature` projects sketch primitives at their setup pose, finds the closest curve within pick radius, and respects front solid occlusion unless `PickQuery::through` is set. `edge_pick` appends Shift-clicked `SketchChain` picks instead of running 3D loop extension, `geo_page` adds per-layer toggle buttons, `mill2d_page`/`fields.rs` edits `Per-chain overrides`, and `pick_highlight`/`interact` render hovered and selected sketch chains in world space.

### What it costs to change later

- A future sketch operation kind (such as `2D Pocket` on DXF profiles) can reuse `SketchContourPlan` resolution in `contour_sketch_pick.rs` and `named_material` stock-top handling while adding its own clearing generator and `sketch_model::generation_problem` arm.
- Adding per-chain lead or tab overrides on top of `ChainOverride` requires adding defaulted fields to `ChainOverrideDto` and another `PROJECT_VERSION` bump.

## #1868 - Slot and Trochoidal Slot on DXF sketch chains

**What was decided**

- A Slot and a Trochoidal Slot read one picked chain of a DXF profile.
  They keep their two points and their width (`a`, `b`, `width`). The
  project file does not change, and no version bump is necessary.
- The pick seeds the numbers in the pick's own command
  (`CreateOperation`, `SetOperationGeometry`). One undo takes back the pick
  and the seed. This is the law that #1504 made for model picks.
  - One closed line-arc slot outline seeds `a`, `b` and `width`.
  - One open straight chain is the centerline. It seeds `a` and `b`. The
    typed `width` stays.
- Generation judges the stored slot against the picked chain, as the world
  is at that time. A slot that left its outline, or whose ends are not the
  ends of its centerline, is refused by name. A moved or re-imported
  profile cannot cut in the old position.
- A closed chain is a slot outline only when the fitted straight slot
  covers 99.5 % or more of the area of the chain. A rectangle, a circle, an
  L or a keyhole is refused by name.
- A selection with more than one chain is refused by name. The whole
  profile as the source is refused by name.
- The refusal of a Slot that is narrower than the tool now gives the two
  numbers.

**Why**

- The room law of `machining2d::SlotBound` (#1504) is reviewed and pinned.
  A sketch outline is a face room, and the existing fit and confine laws
  apply without a second algorithm. A centerline is one new room kind
  (`Room::Line`) with a small law of its own.
- Seeded numbers stay visible and editable on the operation page. The
  generator, the machine area, the WCS rotation and the verification read
  `a`, `b` and `width` in many places. A second source of slot geometry in
  the job would need a change in each of them, in safety code.
- The stock simulation and the verification use the setup stock
  (`part_solid = false`), as #1864 made for the 2D Contour.
- The area test refuses an outline that only contains a slot. The model
  face law of #1504 accepts a rectangular floor as a room, because a floor
  face is the room of a slot. A drawn outline is the slot itself, so the
  rule is stricter.

**Considered and dropped**

- Bent and arc centerlines (an open chain of lines and arcs). The plain
  Slot generator cuts a straight channel only. The Trochoidal Slot
  generator takes a point chain, but its machine area, its fit law and its
  parameters have two points. A curved channel needs a new parameter form
  and a new machine area. Such a chain is refused by name. This needs an
  issue of its own.
- Closed chains as centerlines (a circular groove). A closed chain is read
  as an outline only. One chain cannot be the two things without a new
  parameter, and a wrong guess cuts in the wrong place.
- More than one chain in one operation (a layer of slots). The operation
  holds one `a`, `b` and `width`. Each slot is one operation for now.
- New `SrcRef` or `OpParams` fields for the sketch. The existing
  `SrcRef::Selection` with `FeatureSel::SketchChain` / `SketchLayer` of
  #1864 holds all that is necessary.
- An analytic read of the outline (two lines and two half circles from the
  chain segments). The area test accepts the same outlines, and it also
  accepts an outline whose arcs a CAD system wrote as short lines.

**Cost to change later**

- Curved centerlines add a parameter form. That is a project file change
  with a version bump.
- The 99.5 % limit is one constant (`OUTLINE_COVER` in
  `operation/slot_sketch.rs`).
- The messages of a judged sketch outline say "the picked face" (the text
  of the face room). A separate room name is a small change in
  `slot_room.rs`, which is near the 400-line limit.

## Review corrections

**What was decided**

- Group natural contour chains only within one profile entity. Parent
  checks use both the entity and the chain ID.
- Key sketch highlights by the placed world pose. Keep `None` in the key
  when the sketch has no stock.

**Why**

- Independent profiles can nest in world space while both resolve to an
  outside cut. A combined region can turn the inner profile into a hole
  and reverse its cut side. Separate generation keeps the resolved sides.
- A chain ID belongs to one profile. An equal ID in another profile is
  not its parent.
- A profile rides its stock. The highlight position changes when the
  stock moves or its height changes. Without stock, the profile has no
  placement and draws no highlight.

**Considered and dropped**

- Grouping chains from separate profiles by chain ID alone. This loses
  entity identity and can change the resolved cut sides.
- Using a sketch's local `Location` as the highlight key. That value
  does not change when the stock moves, changes height, or is removed.

## #1873 - Core cadmpeg runner, version check and temp-dir sandbox

### 1. No `cadmpeg formats --json` probe; the exit status of `check` and `convert` is the capability test

**What was decided.** The runner does not call `cadmpeg formats`. It runs
`--version`, then `check --json <input>`, then
`convert <input> -o <out> --to step --reject-lossy=export`. A build that
cannot read the input format or cannot write STEP fails one of these with
a nonzero exit status, and the import is refused with cadmpeg's own last
error line.

**Why.** The issue asks for a `cadmpeg formats --json` probe. cadmpeg
0.6.12 has no such option: `formats` takes no arguments and prints a text
table (the first worker on this issue found this; the CLI definition at
tag commit `9d7592c64` confirms it). cadmpeg's own source says that the
table is for a terminal reader and is not for a caller to parse. The
probe was only an early diagnostic. Safety does not depend on it: `check`
and `convert` give the verdict, and the STEP importer's guards run on the
result.

**Dropped.**
- Parsing the text table of `cadmpeg formats`. Its layout is not a
  contract, so a new cadmpeg could silently break the import.
- A JSON schema of our own that only the stub answers. It proves nothing
  about cadmpeg.
- Waiting for an upstream JSON contract (the first worker's
  recommendation). It blocks #1875, #1876 and #1877 on a third party. The
  probe can be added later without a change to the pipeline.

**Cost to change.** One more step in `cadmpeg::to_step` before `check`.

### 2. The check verdict is the exit status, and the JSON report is read as a second guard

**What was decided.** A nonzero exit status of `check` refuses. With exit
status 0, the runner still reads the JSON on standard output. It refuses
when a `findings` list at any depth has an entry with severity `error` or
`blocking`, and when the output is not JSON.

**Why.** cadmpeg's README states that `check` exits 1 on `error` and
`blocking` findings, so the exit status is the documented contract. The
report layout is versioned by cadmpeg and can move; the scan by key name
does not depend on the path of the list. A report that the runner cannot
read cannot clear a part (Prime Directive).

**Dropped.** A typed model of the report. Its schema is not ours and no
real report was available in this environment (cadmpeg is not installed).

### 3. The child writes to files in the private folder, not to pipes

**What was decided.** Standard output and standard error of the child go
to two files in the private folder. One loop looks at the child, the
clock and the file sizes every 15 ms. A child that passes the time limit,
prints more than 16 MiB, or grows the STEP file past the size limit is
stopped. The folder is removed by a `Drop` guard.

**Why.** With pipes, a reader thread blocks for as long as any process
holds the pipe open, also after the child is stopped. With files there is
no reader thread, and "bounded buffers" is a size that the loop reads. No
new crate is needed.

**Dropped.** Stopping the whole process group of the child. That needs
`libc` (`kill` on a negative pid) or `unsafe`; the issue forbids new
dependencies. Only the direct child is stopped. cadmpeg is one process.

### 4. Refusals use `CommandError::Needs`; an unusable binary uses `CommandError::Invalid`

**What was decided.** A missing program, an old version, a wrong stated
path, a failed `check`, a failed `convert`, a time-out and an oversized
output are `Needs`: plain text that the user can act on. A program whose
`--version` text states no version is `Invalid`. An unqualified native
extension keeps `CommandError::UnsupportedType` with the extension, as
IGES had.

**Why.** `Needs` shows the text with no "invalid parameters:" prefix
(#1105). `UnsupportedType` keeps the existing IGES tests and UI status
text unchanged.

### 5. The qualified table is empty, and the stated path is used alone

**What was decided.** `import::native::QUALIFIED` is empty, so no import
reaches the runner in a shipped build until #1875 adds a format. All
extensions that cadmpeg lists as inputs (`.prt` included) are refused by
name. When `cadmpeg_path` is set and is not a program file, the import
refuses; it does not fall back to `PATH`.

**Why.** The issue says to keep the table empty. A silent fallback would
run a different program than the one the user named.

**Also.** `ImportModel::within` reads the preferences file for the
stated path (`Settings::from_prefs`) because the command constructor has
no settings argument; #1876 owns the UI field. Until then the UI keeps a
hand-written `cadmpegPath` when it saves the preferences.

**Not done here.** The `wasm32` refusal text and the UI wording belong to
#1876. In this PR the runner module is compiled only off `wasm32`, and a
qualified extension on `wasm32` or in `ImportModel::from_bytes` refuses by
name.

## #1888 - Deburr: picked edges, excluded edges, minimum edge angle, hole filter

**What was decided**

1. **Picked chains narrow the ride; they do not bound a region.** A Deburr
   whose source is a selection with edge chains breaks only the exposed
   edges on those chains. `OpParams::Deburr` stays in the `selection_drives_region`
   list of mesh-driven kinds. The picks are read by a new module,
   `operation/deburr_picks.rs`, the way Multi-Axis Contour reads its drive
   chains. A source that is a whole model, the stock, or a selection with
   no edge chain keeps the automatic detection.
2. **A pick selects among exposed edges only.** A picked chain that lies on
   a concave or flat meeting is not ridden. The path has a note for it. If
   no pick names an exposed edge, generation refuses by name.
3. **A pick is not filtered.** The minimum edge angle and the hole filter
   judge the automatic edge set only. An excluded chain is removed in both
   modes.
4. **A face, patch or vertex pick in the source keeps its old meaning.**
   It names the model that the ride reads and does not narrow the ride
   (`setup_align_deburr.rs` pins this reading, #2284). `exclude_edges`
   holds chains only; `is_sane` refuses a face, a patch or a vertex there.
   An excluded chain that is no longer in the model is refused by name.
5. **New operations get 40 degrees; old files get 0.** The seed sets
   `min_edge_angle_deg` to 40.0. A project file without the key reads 0.0
   (every crease), which is the ride the file stored. Each new key is absent
   from the file at its rest value, so an old file saves unchanged. The
   operation stamp digests a filter only off its rest value. An automatic
   or face-only operation keeps its legacy stamp and cached path. A
   chain-selected operation gets a selection-law version in its stamp and
   must regenerate once. The previous generator ignored those chains.
6. **The hole filter matches the bore's own cylinder.** A recognized hole
   (`drilling::recognize`, `recognize_cross`) whose diameter is in the range
   removes each exposed edge with both ends on its cylinder, within 0.05 mm,
   inside the wall's span. The seed range is 0 to 10 mm, with the filter off.
7. **The picked and the excluded chains share the job's `drive_chains`
   slot.** The source's chains come first; the pick count of the source
   says where the list splits. The WCS yaw then turns both lists with the
   facets, with no new slot.
8. **The UI moves picks into the exclusion list.** The Deburr page has the
   button "Exclude the picked edges". It adds the edge picks of the
   Selection block to the draft's `exclude_edges`. Apply writes them with
   the other parameters, as one `EditOperationParams` command.

9. **Exclusion models are cache dependencies.** The stamp includes each
   referenced model's geometry and placement in the setup frame. A missing
   model makes the stamp unresolved and the cached operation stale.

**Why**

- The issue text says to remove Deburr from the `!selection_drives_region`
  guard. That guard sends the picks to `selection_region`, which makes a 2D
  area from them and refuses an open run. A picked edge is a path, not an
  area. The Multi-Axis Contour pattern gives the behaviour that the issue
  asks for ("`SrcRef::Selection` drives manual edge chains").
- A vertical cone over a concave corner cuts the two faces. A pick must
  not make that path (Prime Directive).
- A silent change of the edges that an old project breaks is a change of
  posted G-code. The 0.0 default for old files prevents it.
- Generation reads the geometry and placement of exclusion models. A
  changed or missing reference must invalidate a cached path before posting.
- Before this change, a Deburr with a selection source ignored the picks
  and rode every edge of the picked models. That was a silent wrong answer
  for a user who picked one edge.
- The first version of this change refused a face pick by name. The quick
  gate showed that `turned_selected_deburr_cuts_like_the_baked_part` uses
  a face pick to select the model. A refusal would break stored projects
  that do the same, so the face pick keeps its meaning.

**Considered and dropped**

- Invalidating every Deburr cache or changing the global stamp version:
  unnecessary regeneration for automatic and face-only operations.
- Removing Deburr from the guard as written: refused open chains and gave
  no path.
- 40.0 for a file without the key: changes the path of each stored Deburr
  on a mesh with shallow creases.
- Applying the minimum angle and the hole filter to picked chains: a pick
  is an explicit instruction.
- A separate job slot and a new `WcsYaw::enter` parameter for the excluded
  chains: more plumbing for the same result.
- A new command for the exclusion list: the list is an operation
  parameter, and `EditOperationParams` already makes it undoable. MCP sets
  it through `edit_operation`.
- A pick mode in the viewport that writes to the exclusion list directly:
  larger UI work; the button uses the existing Selection picks.

**Limits**

- A stepped hole (counterbore, chamfered mouth) is recognized by its narrow
  bore. The wider ring's rim is not on that cylinder and stays in the ride.
- A rim of an open mesh has no bend, so the minimum angle does not remove
  it.
- A behaviour change: a Deburr whose stored source has edge chains now
  breaks only those edges. Before, it rode every edge of the picked models.
- A face pick does not select the edges of that face. That is possible
  later work.

**Cost to change later**

- The 0.0 file default is a file contract. A change needs a migration.
- The shared `drive_chains` slot is local to `job.rs`, `generate.rs` and
  `deburr_picks.rs`. A separate slot is a small refactor.

## #1889 - Deburr: a policy for edges out of the cone's reach

**What was decided**

- `finishing3d::UnreachableEdges` has two values: `SkipWithNote` (the
  default) and `Refuse`. It is a field of `DeburrParams` and of
  `OpParams::Deburr` (`unreachable`).
- An edge is out of reach when it is inside the programmed window and
  climbs steeper than the cone's flank (#303). This is the one reach test
  that the kernel has.
- `SkipWithNote` keeps the behaviour of each earlier Deburr: the edge is
  left, and the note `deburr: N edges climb steeper than the cone's flank
  and were skipped` gives the count. No golden moves.
- `Refuse` returns `GenError::Invalid` before a path is built. The text
  gives the count, names the setting, and names `Skip with note` as the
  way out. It comes before the `Empty` answer.
- The project word is `"unreachable": "skip_with_note" | "refuse"`. It has
  `serde(default)`, so an earlier file reads as `skip_with_note`. No
  `PROJECT_VERSION` step.
- The word is always written, the default too.
- The digest writes one byte (`0x52`) only for `Refuse`. The stamp of each
  earlier Deburr does not change.
- UI: a combo `Unreachable edges` on the Geometry tab of the Deburr page.
- MCP: no new tool. `add_operation` and `edit_operation` take the field in
  the params patch, and `list_operation_types` and `get_job` show it.

**Why**

- The issue asks for the two modes, with skip as the default.
- A `Refuse` that comes after `Empty` would hide the reach failure when
  each candidate edge is steep.
- The word is always written because the MCP patch check
  (`mcp/edit.rs`, `lost`) refuses a key that does not come back from the
  typed round-trip. With the default left out of the file, the patch
  `{"unreachable": "skip_with_note"}` was refused as an unknown field.
  The pin `mcp_selects_the_two_modes_and_lists_the_field` found this.

**Considered and dropped**

- To count an edge that the window clips as unreachable. Dropped: the
  window is the machinist's own selection. With it, `Refuse` would refuse
  each closed part, because the bottom rim is always under the window.
- To count the winding and non-manifold skips as unreachable. Dropped:
  they are mesh defects, not reach. Their notes stay as they were.
- To move the flute-length check of `generate.rs` under the policy.
  Dropped: it is true for each edge of the ride, so it always refuses.
- To leave the default word out of the file (`skip_serializing_if`), with
  a special row in `list_operation_types`. Dropped for the MCP reason
  above. The cost: a Deburr saved by this build has one more key.
- A stricter refusal that names each edge position. Dropped as larger
  than the issue; the count is what the note already gives.

**Cost to change later**

- A third policy value is one enum variant, one DTO word, one combo entry
  and one digest byte.
- To leave the default out of the file later needs a change to the MCP
  patch check first.

## #1904 - Continuous 4-axis walkthrough for the 770MX + microARC 4

Sources: CamCraft's own UI, post and machine file; the four PathPilot Hub
readings on issue #796; the LinuxCNC G-code reference for G93 / G94. No
Fusion or HSMWorks material was consulted.

- **Decided: the walkthrough ends with an air cut, and tells the reader not
  to cut.** **Why:** Rotary Parallel finishes both end faces of the model
  down to the fitted axis. On a bar held in a chuck the chuck-side end face
  is inside the bar, so that pass is a groove from the skin to the centre
  (the example program feeds to Z-0.03 at X-1.3125 with the stock going on
  to X-2). No setting keeps the pass off an end face: Bottom Z is a floor
  in the laid frame, not a radius, and there is no axial window. A guide
  that told a new user to cut this would be unsafe. Filed as #2343.
  **Dropped:** (a) a model as long as the stock, as the #796 kit golden has
  it: CamCraft then sees air where the real bar goes on, and the guide
  would hide the cut; (b) Bottom Z above the axis: it keeps only a sector
  of the bar and still cuts the end faces; (c) waiting for #2343: the user
  asked for the page now, and the air cut is also the Hub check that
  PR #2342 still needs. **Cost to change:** when #2343 closes, give the
  page a part that can be cut and drop the limit; the tests name the facts
  that must change (`the_pass_cuts_the_chuck_side_end_face_to_the_centreline`).
- **Decided: the demo operation is Rotary Parallel, not Rotary Offset.**
  **Why:** Rotary Parallel provides the finishing pass described here.
  Each Rotary Offset level that cuts develops two laps of the bar. The
  original machine file refused that count at -360..360 (#2344). The
  shipped file now states no A travel limit, and that refusal no longer
  applies. The refreshed example uses the shipped machine without an
  added limit. **Dropped:** retaining a bounded example machine and
  presenting its limit as a shipped restriction. No Rotary Offset machine
  run is claimed. Wrapping a drawing round a cylinder is not implemented.
- **Decided: the example tool has a 5/8 in flute.** **Why:** with a 1/2 in
  flute the shank check blocks the post at the chuck-side end face
  ("shank/holder at move N collides with the uncut stock"). That guard is
  right, and the page says so; the long flute is there only so that a
  program exists to air-cut. Pinned both ways
  (`a_short_flute_is_blocked_at_the_chuck_side_end_face`).
- **Decided: the committed program is what the committed project posts,
  not what a fresh build posts.** **Why:** a saved toolpath keeps fewer
  digits than a fresh one, so the two programs differ in a last digit of
  some A and F words. A reader opens the project file, so the page quotes
  that file's program. The project file is held structurally to the
  document that the test builds. Only cached move coordinates and tool
  axes permit one step in their six-decimal serialization lattice across
  platforms. The version, tool number, machine, parameters, cache structure
  and other values stay exact. Larger coordinate changes are rejected.
  **Dropped:** byte-for-byte comparison of independently generated cache
  coordinates, which can differ at platform rounding boundaries.
- **Decided: the pictures are SVG files drawn by a script from the
  committed project, model and program** (`site/tools/
  first_continuous_4axis_pictures.py`), and a site test holds the files to
  the script's output. **Why:** the UI renderer of #1902 (PR #2078) is not
  merged, and a PR must not add snapshot PNGs or hand screenshots. The
  operation reference already uses drawn SVG (`operation-paths.svg`); these
  use its colours. **Dropped:** stacking on PR #2078 as well as #2342.
  **Cost to change:** when #1902 merges, add UI renders beside them.
- **Decided: the page is in Getting started, beside "Your first 4-axis
  part", and is linked from the Multi-axis section.** Same place and shape
  as the indexed half of this issue (PR #2135).
- **Also corrected:** `continuous-4-axis.md` still said that no shipped post
  writes inverse-time feed, and the Multi-axis index said that
  `tormach.cps` "indexes A only". PR #2342 made both untrue.
- **Not exercised:** the program has not been run in the PathPilot Hub or
  on a machine. The issue's "Done means" asks for a Hub run to M30; the
  page lists what to check and asks for the result on #1904.
- **Review decision: compare the NC examples with tightly bounded numeric
  differences.** **Why:** supported platforms can differ at rounding
  boundaries in A and inverse-time F words. Keep the committed programs
  and the independent rate checks. Reject changes outside the numeric
  bounds, and reject changes to line structure or other words.
  **Dropped:** replacing each golden with one platform's output, which
  does not establish agreement across platforms. **Cost to change:** a
  post-format change needs new bounds and pins.
- **Review decision: this partial delivery uses `Refs #1904`.** **Why:**
  neither program has a recorded PathPilot Hub run to M30, and the wrapped
  engraving or slot is not available. The guide does not complete the
  issue's acceptance work. **Dropped:** keeping a closing keyword without
  that evidence. **Cost to change:** complete and record the missing work
  before closing #1904.
- **Review decision: inherit the feed-time fix and trajectory pin from
  parent PR #2342.** **Why:** the defect originates in that parent, whose
  head `b93fe06131248f91e41e90104e0d050409add852` has a review that clears
  the original feed-time and NC-comparison code findings. **Dropped:** a
  separate safety fix in this child. Refresh this child from the parent
  and validate the merged head before claiming the finding is fixed.

## #1944 - AI context budgets and compact MCP read modes

**Decided.**

- `get_job` takes `summary: true`. The summary removes `machine.definition`
  and keeps the machine `path` and `name`, with `definition_omitted: true`.
  Each operation's `params` keeps only the fields that differ from the
  default that `add_operation` seeds for its kind. Null and empty-list
  fields of operation, setup, tool and model rows are removed. Inside
  `params`, a `null` stays, because there it is a stated value.
- `list_operation_types` takes `kind` (a key or a label, any case) and
  `section` (`Mill2D`, `Mill3D`, `Drilling`, `MultiAxis`, `Turning`,
  `Plasma`, `WireEdm`, `Sinker`). A name that matches no kind or section
  is refused with the valid names.
- `list_features` takes `compact: true`. Compact rows keep the id, the
  name and the facts that a pick is chosen by. Counts replace the loop and
  face lists. A face whose outside is unknown still says so. The compact
  default `limit` is 25 rows for each kind. The full listing keeps 500, so
  that no current caller changes.
- `mcp::provider::tools_in(provider, ToolSet)` gives the full table or a
  core set of 25 workflow tools (`CORE_TOOLS`). `tools(provider)` stays the
  full table.
- The chat worker (`crates/ui/src/egui_app/ai_chat/budget.rs`):
  - Cuts each tool reply that goes back to the model at 12000 JSON
    characters. The cut keeps whole characters and ends with a hint that
    names the compact read modes. The tool card in the panel keeps the
    full text.
  - Sends at most one viewport image in each request (the newest).
  - Stops a turn after 12 model rounds. This cap existed as
    `MAX_TURN_STEPS`; it moved to `budget::MAX_TOOL_ROUNDS` and has a test.
  - Sends at most 6 earlier turns. When it drops older turns, it puts the
    latest successful `get_job` reply of all earlier turns (cut to the
    reply cap) in front of the first kept prompt.
  - Offers the core tool set to a local endpoint and the full table to a
    cloud endpoint.

**Why.** Small local models have context windows of 8k to 32k tokens. The
full tool table and one full `get_job` or `list_features` reply can fill
that alone. Each cap is a constant with a test, so a later change is one
line.

**Dropped.**

- A smaller default `limit` for every `list_features` call. It would change
  the reply of each current MCP client. The small default applies only with
  `compact`.
- A panel control to choose the tool set. The endpoint kind already tells
  local from cloud, and a new control needs layout and snapshot work. A
  follow-up can add it if a user wants the full table on a local model.
- Removing old tool results inside one turn. Provider formats pair each
  tool call with its result; to remove one safely needs the call record
  in each message. The reply cap and the round cap bound one turn.
- A tool refusal for a model that calls a tool outside the core set. The
  call goes through the same MCP door and approvals as any other call.

**Cost to change.** Each limit is one constant in `budget.rs` or
`compact.rs`. The core set is one list in `mcp/provider.rs`.

**PR #3033 review fix.** Keep the upstream importer warning for edges that
lie off their surfaces. Keep the compact `get_job` schema from this branch.
These are separate tool entries. Taking either complete conflict side would
remove the other change, so neither side is discarded. This resolution adds
no behavior. The screenshot check uses a temporary harness that is not
committed. Its images stay on the fork's `pr-screenshots` branch. The full
chat tool card remains visible while the model reply is capped.

## #1945 - AI provider HTTP clients, keychain keys and offline-only mode

**What was decided.** A new `camcraft_app::ai` module holds the provider
transport: `endpoint` (URL parse, loopback test, the offline and https laws),
`presets` (Anthropic, OpenAI Chat, OpenAI Responses, Gemini over https;
Ollama, Unsloth Studio, LM Studio and llama-server on loopback), `wire` (the
request path and body per provider, echoing tool-call envelopes so reasoning
items and Gemini thought signatures survive), `probe` (Ollama `/api/show`
capabilities), `secret` (an opaque `ApiKey`, environment first, then the
keychain), and, native only, `http` (the client) and `keychain`. The AI Chat
dock uses it through `transport_http::HttpTransport`; the browser build keeps
the offline-only default transport and links no socket or keychain code.
`prefs.json` gains `aiOfflineOnly` (written only when on), and the dock's
"Offline only" switch is saved there.

**New third-party crates (need the maintainer's decision).** `reqwest 0.12`
(default features off, `rustls-tls-webpki-roots`) provides HTTP(S).
`tokio 1` uses `rt`, `time`, `net` and `macros` for a current-thread runtime
per request. `keyring 4.2` provides macOS Keychain, Windows Credential
Manager and Secret Service over zbus. `url 2.5` was already in the lock and
is now a direct dependency. These dependencies still need the maintainer's
decision. This change adds no dependency between CamCraft crates.

**Why these.** The first version used blocking `ureq 2.12`. Review #2122
found that its active request could not be cancelled. A silent server could
therefore block chat shutdown for the full request timeout. The client now
selects between the async request and a cancellation check every 20 ms.
Cancellation drops the request and its runtime, which closes the active
connection. The Ollama capability probe uses the same cancellation path.
A detached blocking request was rejected because it would remain active
after cancellation. rustls avoids system TLS dependencies. keyring 4's
Linux store uses Rust over zbus, so the release runners need no `libdbus`
build package.

**Provider errors remove secrets.** JSON and plain-text provider errors
remove the supplied API key before the message is truncated. This also
removes a key that crosses the text limit.

**Offline-only is enforced in the client, twice.** `endpoint::admit` refuses
a non-loopback host before anything resolves; the client's resolver then
refuses any resolved address that is not loopback (a hosts-file `localhost`
pointing elsewhere). No redirect is followed: a local server could otherwise
bounce a call to a remote host. `no_proxy` disables environment proxies,
so a loopback request cannot use a remote proxy. Plain `http://` off the machine is refused
whether or not a key is sent - cloud providers are https only.

**Unsloth Studio and llama-server bases.** The issue names
`http://127.0.0.1:8888` for Unsloth Studio; the base is
`http://127.0.0.1:8888/v1`, the OpenAI-compatible mount every other local
runtime here uses. llama-server's documented default port is 8080; its label
says to start it with `--jinja` for tool calls.

**A model without tools refuses, it does not silently degrade.** When an
Ollama model in the native-tools preset lists no `tools` capability, the
step is refused by name, pointing at the Prompt-JSON and Q&A presets. Falling
back inside the transport would send a request without the prompt-JSON
context (the transport has no project snapshot) and the reply would not parse.

**Considered and dropped.** Blocking `ureq` (no active request cancellation);
`native-tls`
(OpenSSL headers on Linux); keyring's `dbus-secret-service` store (vendored
libdbus C build); storing keys in `prefs.json` encrypted (the issue forbids
any key there); an MCP tool to set a key (an agent should never handle a
user's secret).

**Cost to change later.** Low for presets and wire shapes (data and pure
functions with loopback tests); swapping the HTTP crate touches only
`ai/http.rs`.

## #1947 - Single-source agent docs for the MCP tools

**What was decided.** The live MCP tool table (`crates/app/src/mcp/tools.rs`)
is the one source. A new module, `mcp::catalog`, makes three outputs from it:

- The Markdown tool reference. `camcraft-cli mcp reference` prints it. It is
  committed at `docs/agents/mcp-tools.md`.
- The compact prompt for a local model. `camcraft-cli mcp prompt` prints it.
- The shared working rules (`catalog::RULES`). The local Prompt-JSON context
  (`provider::prompt_context`) now starts with these rules.

The agent wrappers hold no tool list. `.agents/skills/camcraft-mcp/SKILL.md`
(Codex CLI and Antigravity) and `GEMINI.md` (Gemini CLI) point to the Claude
skill and to the generated reference. Codex also reads `AGENTS.md`, and its
skill table already names `camcraft-mcp`, so `AGENTS.md` does not change.

`crates/app/tests/mcp_doc_drift.rs` pins it:

- The committed reference must equal the generated one. The failure message
  gives the command that writes it again.
- Each tool call (`name {`) and each backticked tool name in a table row of
  the skill, the wrappers and the guide must be a live tool.
- Each live tool must be named in the guide and in the local prompt.
- The local Prompt-JSON context and the local prompt carry the same rules.

**Why.** Before this change, the guide did not name 34 live tools, and the
skill listed shipped tools as gaps. A generated reference cannot drift, and
the tests stop new drift in the hand-written files.

**Dropped.**

- A reference under `.claude/skills/camcraft-mcp/`. This session cannot write
  there without an approval prompt. Also, one neutral path suits all agents.
- Generated wrapper files. They hold only pointers, so the tests that scan
  them are enough.
- A `skill_reference` MCP tool. A new tool changes `tools/list` for all
  clients. The CLI subcommands give the same text without that change.
- A rule that the hand-written skill must name every tool. Many open PRs edit
  that file. The generated reference covers each tool already.

**Held.** The edit of `.claude/skills/camcraft-mcp/SKILL.md` (remove
`set_units` and `set_program` from "Known Remaining Gaps", link the generated
reference) and its pin are posted on the issue as a patch. This session
could not write under `.claude/`.

**Cost to change later.** Low. A tool PR runs one command to write the
reference again. The format of the reference is one function.

## #1949 - Document the shipped AI workflow

**What was decided**

- Add the task guide under `site/content/guide/automate/ai.md`.
  Preserve `guide/ai/` as an alias.
- Document the native panel's cloud providers and Ollama connection.
  State that Unsloth Studio, LM Studio and llama-server have library
  endpoints but no supported panel setup.
- Use the actual environment and OS keychain credential routes.
  Do not describe an API key form or endpoint field that does not exist.
- Show the external clients' shared stdio command and arguments.
  Leave each client's surrounding configuration format to that client.
- Give four CAM tasks with JSON-RPC tool calls and named inspection steps.
  Check example calls against the live MCP tool schema.
- Keep context budgets (#1944) and single-source agent skills (#1947)
  outside this pass, as the issue's latest scope comment directs.

**Why**

The old MCP page says that the panel has no live transport.
The transport now ships, but its panel exposes fewer endpoints than the
provider library defines. Instructions must follow the available controls.
A tool call completing does not prove that a program is safe. The examples
therefore retain verification, warning inspection and posting approval.

**Considered and dropped**

- Put the page at the old guide root: the current navigation groups
  automation pages under Automate. The alias retains the short URL.
- Invent setup controls for every library endpoint: those controls have
  not shipped. The guide states the limitation instead.
- Copy client-specific configuration files: their formats belong to
  external clients. The shared command and arguments are the stable
  CamCraft interface.
- Use fixed catalog or face identifiers: those values depend on the
  document and runtime catalog. The guide tells readers how to obtain them.

**Cost to change later**

New panel endpoint controls require changes to the setup table and its
limits. New tool schemas or CLI flags must keep the guide's automated
checks green. The guide can link the agent skills when #1947 ships.

## #1951 - A batch suite step starts its test executable from the build's cargo JSON artifacts

**What was decided.**

- Each batch prebuild (`debug build: <crate> (--no-run)`) has the flag
  `--message-format=json-render-diagnostics`. The executor keeps the JSON messages of the build and makes
  one `cargo metadata --no-deps` call. From the two it records the test executables of the crate
  (`xtask/src/artifacts.rs`).
- A suite step of that crate (`--lib`, `--bins` or `--test <name>`) then starts the recorded executable
  and does not start cargo (`xtask/src/direct.rs`). The step name, the step number, the log file name and
  the plan are the same. `--dry-run` prints the same cargo commands.
- The executable starts as `cargo test` starts it: in the package directory, with the libtest args after
  `--`, and with the variables that cargo sets (`CARGO`, `CARGO_MANIFEST_DIR`, `CARGO_MANIFEST_PATH`, the
  `CARGO_PKG_*` set, `CARGO_BIN_EXE_<bin>`, `OUT_DIR`, the `rustc-env` pairs of the build script and the
  dynamic library path). The list was read from a test process under cargo 1.100.
- The gate writes cargo's `Running <target> (<path>)` line into the step log before the output of the
  executable. `read_log`, the notes and `--failed` read the log as before.
- A step stays a cargo step when one of these is true: its package has no recorded build in this run
  (`--only` or `--failed` selected the step without its build step); its target has no executable in the
  list; it is a `--doc` step; its args are not exactly the known form. The printed command shows which
  way a step ran.
- The executable path comes only from the JSON list. The gate never searches `target/` for one.
- `CAMCRAFT_GATE_NO_DIRECT=1` makes each step a cargo step again. It is for a comparison run, and for a
  platform where a direct run does not behave as `cargo test` does. This PR ran on macOS only.

**Why.**

- Each suite step started cargo to run one binary that was built already. The issue gives about 0.5 s for
  one start on Windows, and the batch plan has several hundred suite steps.
- This PR is stacked on #2788. That PR builds each crate alone, so the executables of the build are the
  same ones that `cargo test -p <crate>` runs. With one build for all the crates the features are
  unified, and the executables are different ones.
- cargo 1.100 puts a test executable in `target/debug/build/<pkg>/<hash>/out/`, not in
  `target/debug/deps/`. A path that the gate computes itself is wrong on one of the two layouts. The JSON
  list is correct on the two.
- When the gate runs under `cargo xtask`, its own process has the `CARGO_MANIFEST_DIR` and `CARGO_PKG_*`
  values of `xtask`. A direct run must set the values of the tested package. If not, a test that reads
  one of them at run time gets the wrong value.

**Considered and dropped.**

- The release tier. Its debug build is one build for all the crates (feature unification). Its steps
  stay cargo steps. A change to builds for each crate changes the plan of the cut gate; that is not in
  this issue.
- The heavy lanes (`--release --ignored`) and the quick tier. They have other build steps and few steps
  for each run. `direct::records` and `direct::of` accept a step only by its args, so a later PR can add
  the JSON flag to those builds.
- A new dependency (`serde_json`, `cargo_metadata`). The gate reads a few fields. `xtask/src/json.rs` is
  a small reader for them.
- A search for `*-<hash>` files in `target/`. It can find an old executable or the GUI binary.
- A hard failure when a target has no recorded executable. cargo runs the step correctly in that case,
  and the printed command shows it.
- A `rustc --print target-libdir` call for the library path. Under `cargo xtask` the path of the gate
  process has the toolchain directories already. The tests link no toolchain dylib.

**Cost to change later.**

- Low. Remove the JSON flag from `plan::debug_build_crate`, and each step is a cargo step again.
- The `gate` skill text still says that each step calls `cargo test`. The worker session could not edit
  `.claude/skills/gate/SKILL.md` (the edit was refused). The text needs an update.
- If a later cargo sets a new variable for a test process, add it in `artifacts::package`.

## #2007 - Tool editor fixed footer, plain-English state lines and label-left shape rows

**What was decided.**

- The Properties tool page (`crates/ui/src/egui_app/tool_settings.rs`) now
  owns its own vertical scroll area (`tool_page_scroll`) and keeps its
  footer fixed below it: `Apply` (or `Add tool` on a new tool) beside
  `Close`, with any name-block message or `ErrorScope::Tool` refusal
  drawn directly above that button row. `pages.rs` delegates
  `UiTarget::Tool` directly before its shared scroll area, matching
  `op_page`.
- The Catalog group's `Tool number` row (`tool_settings_grid.rs`) drops
  the raw `"(0 = next free)"` label suffix and moves that detail into the
  row's hover tooltip (`prop_row_hint`), matching the `Material group` and
  `Holder` rows.
- The Body tab (`tool_body_page.rs`, `tool_body_lathe_page.rs`) aligns
  `Tool axis`, `Tip offset`, and `Body frame` as label-left property rows
  and replaces raw/jargon state strings (`"body: ..."`, `"draft: ... (not
  applied)"`, `"none - the holder is/cylinder is judged"`, `"placed: foot
  ..."`, `"placement: ..."`) with plain-English lines matching the
  Profile tab (`"In use: ..."`, `"Ready to apply: ... (not applied yet)"`,
  `"Placed from ..."` / `"Placed: ..."` / `"Placement error: ..."`).
- The shape window's holder library picker (`tool_holder_picker.rs`)
  puts `Library holder`, `Gauge length`, and `Projection` in label-left
  `prop_row` / `prop_row_hint` rows using unit-suffixed `num_row` fields,
  `tool_profile_page::editor` syncs `tool_profile_ui` before drawing the
  picker so an existing library holder shows immediately on the Body tab,
  and `pages::tool_shape_editor_window` renders `ErrorScope::Tool` above
  its fixed `Close` button.

**Why.**

After PRs #2663 (`#2014`) and #2764 (`#2397`) merged, #2007 still had
two unowned UI items from the maintainer's 2026-11-18 report and the
2026-11-19 status audit: `Apply` / `Add tool` scrolled off the bottom of
Properties at 720 px height, and several state lines and labels still
used raw fragments (`"(0 = next free)"`, `"body: ..."`, `"judged"`,
stacked `field(...)` labels in the shape editor).

**What was dropped.**

- Removing the typed `holder_d` and `holder_len` fields when no library
  holder is selected. Existing `#2016`, `#2009`, `#2014`, and `#93` pins
  require parametric cylinder dimensions as the fallback when no library
  entry or custom profile is set, and removing them would break project
  and tool-library formats without a separate migration decision.
- Removing the armed-pick 3D placement view in `tool_body_page`. It
  already stays hidden at rest (`BodyPickMode::Off`) and only renders
  while `Pick tip` / `Pick axis` / `Pick radial` / `Pick spindle` needs
  click targets on the mesh.
- Moving `Delete` and `Edit tool shape` out of the top of the tool page.
  Keeping them under the `Tool: <name>` heading preserves `layout_page_tool`
  and keeps them reachable without scrolling while `Apply` / `Add tool`
  and `Close` share the bottom bar.

**Cost to change.**

The tool Properties footer lives in `tool_settings::footer`, the shape
window error footer in `pages::tool_shape_editor_window`, and each
updated label/state line is pinned in `tool_properties.rs`,
`tool_body.rs`, `tool_body_lathe.rs`, `tool_holder.rs`, and
`tool_holder_reference.rs`.

## #2007 - the tool profile page: one preview, a full points table, plain words

**Decided.**

- The Profile tab has no side view of its own. The one to-scale preview
  beside the tool fields draws the draft of the tab. With Custom selected,
  a drawn holder that validates shows as the bands that the collision
  check sweeps (`tool_body::stack`, #2017). On Draw cutter, a drawn cutter
  that validates replaces the steel outline, and the holder goes on top
  of it as bands. A draft that does not validate shows the holder in use,
  and its refusal stays in red under the table. All other tabs show the
  holder in use, as before (`tool_profile_page::preview_inputs`).
- The points table has a least height equal to its greatest height
  (150 px). egui gives a nested scroll area only the space that is left
  in the view (egui 0.36.2 `scroll_area.rs`), so a table low on the
  scrolled page fell to its 64 px least height and showed about two rows.
  This cause was seen in the running app before the change.
- The points table has no 40 px least column width (egui's Grid default).
  With it the six columns were about 300 px wide in the 260 px column, so
  in a narrow pane the "×" buttons stood outside the pane. The tab row
  and the three file buttons wrap in a narrow column.
- The page says "In use: ..." in place of "landed: ...". The revolved note,
  the table headers ("height", "radius", "arc", with hover text) and the
  holder line ("from .. to .. mm above the tip") use plain words.

**Why.** The maintainer reopened #2007 with "the tool editing dialogs still
look bad". Two drawings of one tool at different scales showed the same
holder twice. The removed view gave the flute, stickout and gauge marks;
the holder line under the table now gives the stickout and the gauge.

**Dropped.**

- Hide the main preview while the Profile tab shows and keep the side
  view: then the tool has a different drawing on each tab, and the side
  view did not draw the bands that the check reads.
- Draw the Parametric draft when a body is in use: Parametric then shows
  a cylinder while the check still reads the landed body. The preview
  shows a draft only where Apply profile would land it.
- Remove the inner scroll area of the table: a long imported outline
  (tens of points) then pushes Apply profile far down the page.

**Cost to change.** Small. `preview_inputs` is the one place that picks
what the preview draws, and `TABLE_H` is one constant.

## #2012 - Depth ladder: the remainder ladder stays the default, equal steps is an opt-in parameter

**What was decided**

1. The default ladder does not change. It steps down by the full stepdown
   from Top Z, and the last step keeps the remainder. `top 20, bottom 2,
   stepdown 5` cuts `[15, 10, 5, 2]`.
2. Equal steps is an operation parameter, `equal_steps`, off by default. It
   is a field of the operation's `links.approach` object
   (`camcraft_motion::approach::Approach`). On, the ladder cuts the same
   number of levels, and each step is the span divided by that count. The
   same example cuts `[15.5, 11, 6.5, 2]`.
3. The mode is one function, `machining2d::equal_stepdown(top, bottom,
   stepdown)`. It gives the stepdown that the unchanged level law
   (`cut_levels_under`) then walks. `cut_levels_for(top, &approach, bottom,
   stepdown)` reads the mode and the stock top from the approach. The
   generators call it in place of `cut_levels_under`.
4. With stock over Top Z (#2004) the level at Top Z stays, and the steps
   under it are equal.
5. The stepdown stays the largest step. Code that reads `stepdown` as a
   bound (the 3-D shell's floor under a plane, the contour's first entry
   height) is not changed: with equal steps it reads a bound that is a
   little larger than the real step, which is the safe side.
6. The parameter is on the operations that have a `links` object: 2D
   Contour, 2D Pocket, 2D Adaptive, 2D Offset, Circular, Slot, Bore, 3D
   Pocket and the rotary / multi-axis roughing that run the 3-D ladder.
7. The app's pocket region law (`operation::area::ladder_planes`) reads the
   same mode through `OpParams::ladder_stepdown`, so the region is built at
   the planes that the generator cuts.

**Why**

- The default must not move posted G-code. Each golden file and each saved
  project keeps its programmed depths.
- The project rule "CAM choices are parameters" asks for a parameter, not
  for a silent change of the law.
- The `links.approach` object is already saved field by field (absent means
  default), already rides `EditOperationParams` for undo, and is already
  what the MCP `edit` tools parse. A new field there needs no file version
  step and no new command.
- One function for the mode keeps one level law. No second ladder can drift
  from the first.

**Considered and dropped**

- Equal steps as the new default. Dropped: it changes the posted depths of
  each multi-level operation in each saved project.
- A second level function with its own loop (levels computed as `top - i *
  span / n`). Dropped: two loops with two float behaviours for one law. The
  mode as an adjusted stepdown reuses the tested loop and its refusals.
- A field on each parameter struct of the motion crate. Dropped: Face,
  Trace and Trochoidal Slot have about 30 struct literals in tests and
  callers, and the operations have no `links` object to save the choice in.
- Replacing `stepdown` in each generator's parameters before the run, so
  that each reader sees the equal step. Dropped: Bore and the Circular
  vault have one span for each hole or ring, so only the level law knows
  the span.
- A row beside each Stepdown field on the Passes tabs. Dropped for now: the
  field is saved in `links.approach`, and the one editor of that object is
  the Lead in / Lead out tab. The row is in its Linking group.

**Not done here (follow-up #2832)**

- Face, Trace, Engrave and Trochoidal Slot have no `links` object. They keep
  the remainder ladder. Issue #2832 adds the parameter to them.
- Turning has its own infeed laws (`turning/*`). They are not part of this
  decision.

**Cost to change later**

- To make equal steps the default: change `Approach::DEFAULT.equal_steps`,
  write the field when it is `false`, and regenerate each golden of a
  multi-level operation. Old files without the key would then read as equal
  steps, so that change also needs a file version step.
- To remove the parameter: delete the field and its DTO key. Files that
  have the key still load (unknown keys of `approach` are ignored only if
  the DTO stays tolerant; check before the removal).

## #2014 - Tool settings are a property grid with the labels to the left

**What was decided.** The tool page in Properties draws every setting as
one property row: the label in the left half of the pane, the input in the
right half. The rows stand in four collapsible groups, in this order:
Geometry, Holder, Cutting data, Catalog. `crates/ui/src/egui_app/tool_settings_grid.rs`
holds the grid. `tool_settings.rs` keeps the page, the three columns, the
Apply / Add commands and the kind seeding.

- Geometry holds the type, the cutting shape (diameter, or the kerf, wire
  or electrode sizes), the kind-read rows, the corner radius, the flute and
  the shank.
- Holder holds the holder diameter and length.
- Cutting data holds spindle rpm, feed, the per-material table, the
  turning rows and centre cutting.
- Catalog holds the material group, the catalog facts and the tool number.

The inline help paragraphs became hover tooltips on the row labels
(`prop_row_hint`), per the form law in `layout/form.rs`. The waterjet
recipe and the catalog rows lost their own nested headers: their group is
the one header now. The per-material table keeps its six columns and
scrolls across inside the Cutting data group, so it never widens the page
or the tool editor window. A group's title folds the group as its arrow
does (`group_open`); before, only the arrow was clickable.

**Why.** The maintainer reported the crammed page twice: each label stood
above its input and the right half of the pane was empty. The form helpers
already state the label-left property grid and the collapsible group
(#1122). The page follows them now instead of its own stacked form.

**What was dropped.** The modal `tool_editor_window` in `pages.rs` stays.
It shares `tool_settings::contents` and is retired separately (#2003);
this change is safe for it but removal is out of scope. A `Catalog` group
title now exists on the tool page; the catalog dock's own "Catalog"
heading is a different widget in a different pane. The #2002 tests assert
the dock's controls by their own names, so they still guard that
separation. The waterjet recipe caption "Cutting data by material and
thickness" is gone; the group header "Cutting data" carries it. The plasma
cut-data recipe PR (#2596) brought that caption back on `main` as a nested
`CollapsingHeader`; the merge of `main` into this branch applied the same
rule again and kept the grid's single group, with the plasma PR's rules
intact (a recipe does not fill a material slot).

**What a change would cost later.** A new tool field goes in one group of
`tool_settings_grid.rs` as a `prop_row`; a new group is one `group_open`
call. A test that moves a row expects the label and the input to share a
row (vertical centres within 4 px) and the label to sit left of the input.

## #2016 - A tool's library holder is a reference to the entry

**Decided.** A tool that sits in a built-in library holder stores a
reference: the entry's exact name, the gauge length and the projection
(`camcraft_tools::holder_library::HolderRef`, on `ToolBody::library`).
The project file and the `.camtools` file write it as the tool key
`holder: {entry, gauge_len, projection}` (plus `machine_default: true`
for an assumed holder, #828) and write no `body`. One function turns a
reference into a shape, `tool_body::build_library`; the command
(`SetToolBody::library`, `AddTool`), the project loader and the tool
library reader all call it. `tool_body::judged`, `stack`, `digest`, the
simulation and the preview read the body it returns, as before.

**The document keeps the resolved body beside the reference.** The
`ToolBody` component still holds the outline, facets and bands. They
are derived data: nothing but `build_library` writes them for a library
holder, and no file stores them. The laws therefore read exactly the
steel they read before, with no second resolution path. Resolving on
every `judged` call was dropped: it would add a refusal path to every
law and gain nothing, since both lengths are stored in full.

**Both lengths are stated in the reference**, also when the caller left
them out (the entry's gauge length, the tool's flute plus shank length).
A later edit of the tool's lengths therefore does not move the holder;
`tool_body::fits` refuses at use when the holder no longer fits, as it
did for the drawn copy.

**Same shape, pinned.** For every library entry, at its default and at
other lengths, picked and assumed: the judged tool, the envelope, the
band stack, the stamp term and the facets of the referenced holder
equal those of the drawn copy an older build stored
(`holder_reference::every_entry_reads_the_same_bands_by_reference_as_its_old_copy`).
The stamp term is unchanged, so no operation goes stale.

**Migration: an older file is not rewritten.** A file without `holder`
loads as it did. A drawn copy of a library holder stays a drawn
(custom) profile with the same outline; a `holder_d`/`holder_len`
cylinder stays the tool's own numbers. Neither is turned into a
reference: the copy may have been edited, and matching an outline back
to an entry is a guess. The user picks the entry again to get a
reference.

**Version step.** Project files write v70 (`PROJECT_VERSION = 70`),
after v68 (#2441) and v69 (#1517) on `main`, and `.camtools` files write
version 4 (`HOLDER_REF_VERSION = 4`, after `CUTTING_STEPS_VERSION = 3`)
when a tool names a library holder (keeping earlier minimum versions
when no tool names one). `v0.22.0` reads project v62 and `.camtools` 2,
and pre-#2016 builds read up to project v69 and `.camtools` 3; both
refuse v70 and version 4 instead of dropping `holder` and judging the
tool's smaller holder cylinder.

**Refusals.** A reference to a name the library does not hold refuses
the file by tool name, and so does a grouped pick ("BT40 Weldon", which
names no bore), lengths the entry cannot be drawn at, a holder that
reaches into the flutes, an unknown key in the reference, and a tool
that states both `holder` and `body`. No other holder is put in its
place (#808). The shank fit is checked when the holder is set, not on
load: a file the app saved must open, and a drawn copy was not checked
on load either.

**A change of the library's own numbers now reaches old projects.**
A reference is drawn from the build's tables. If an entry is corrected,
every tool that names it follows. That is the point of a reference; a
copy kept the old numbers.

**Editing.** The outline of the referenced holder applied unchanged
(Apply profile, MCP `points`) keeps the reference. One edited point
makes it a custom drawn profile, in one undo step.

**Tool library import.** The import's "same tool" test still compares
the shape (the body as a save wrote it before). A drawn copy and a
reference with the same outline are therefore the same tool and are
skipped, not added a second time as "Name (2)".

**The holder fields.** With a referenced holder the tool settings show
the holder diameter and length the laws read (the cylinder that
encloses the entry) as text, not as two fields. The tool record's own
`holder_d`/`holder_len` are not overwritten: they are what the tool
goes back to when the holder is cleared, and writing them would move
the tool's stamp. An assumed (machine default) holder keeps the two
fields, because #828 floors it at them.

**MCP.** `set_tool_holder` with `library` writes the reference;
`get_job` and the reply show it as `holder.library`. A `holder`
reference inside `add_tool`'s `definition` is refused by name (the
definition's body was never read there; dropping a reference would land
the machine's default holder in its place). `edit_tool` refuses a
`holder` patch like `body`.

**Dropped.** Removing `holder_d`/`holder_len` from the tool record (every
law and every file reads them; the stand-in cylinder of a bare tool
stays). A reference field on `Tool` itself (the body component already
carries undo, the file key and the delete hook). User-defined library
entries (the reference names built-in entries only; a user library is
separate work).

**Breaking.** A project or tool library saved with a library holder is
not readable by v0.22.0 and older (project v70, `.camtools` version 4).
`ToolBody` has a new public field.

**Cost to change.** Small. The reference type, `build_library`, the
`holder` key (`project/tool_body_wire.rs`) and its readers.

## #2017 - Tool page: one side preview, the 3D view only while a pick is armed

**Decided.** The side preview is the one preview of the tool page. It draws
the bands from `tool_body::checked_bands`: the checked profile (a machine
default is floored by `tool_body::checked_profile`, the same call as
`judged`) through `tool_body::stack`, the stack the collision check sweeps.
The 3D mesh view no longer shows at rest. It shows only while a Pick button
(tip, axis, radial, spindle) is armed.

**Why.** The 3D view is the only surface where a click picks the tip or
axis. Removing it fully would remove that function and no other control
replaces it. Showing it only while a pick is armed meets "one preview" at
rest and keeps the pick.

**Dropped.** (1) Delete the 3D view and its picks: loses placement by click.
(2) A second derivation of the holder shape in the UI: the issue forbids it.

**Cost to change.** Delete `placement_view` and `preview_3d` in
`tool_body_page.rs` and drop the Pick buttons when numeric placement is
enough.

## #2055 - "Do not touch" protected faces and edges on 2D Offset and 3D Pocket

### What was decided
- **Operations covered in this first slice**: `OpType::Offset2D` (`2D Offset`) and `OpType::Pocket3D` (`3D Pocket`) obey `"Do not touch"` across all strategies (`Waterline`, `Zigzag`, `Auto`, `OffsetRings`, `Adaptive`, `shell`, `rest_rough`, `feed_opt`), all `Entry3D` modes, all `Links` modes (including `KeepDown` level checks and elevated rapid traverses), and tilted 3+2 planes (`Offset2D { tilt: Some(...) }`). Unsupported operation kinds refuse non-default `"Do not touch"` by name across commands, UI, MCP, and generation so nothing is silently ignored.
- **Storage on `AreaControls` (`crates/app/src/operation/types/area.rs`, `avoid.rs`)**: Added `pub do_not_touch: DoNotTouch` inside `AreaControls` (with `has_boundary_edits()` separating 2D region boundary clipping from `"Do not touch"` and preserving exact legacy behavior/stamps when `DoNotTouch` is default), avoiding edits to 185 `Operation` literals while automatically propagating through undo/redo, paste, stale tracking, and UI drafts.
- **Independent 3D verification & generator keep-outs (`crates/sim/src/verify/avoid.rs`, `avoid_links.rs`, `avoid_poly.rs`)**: Added `Warning::AvoidHit { at, item, part, short_mm }` (`Copy`, `blocks_post() == true`). Per-Z-interval keep-out regions (`AVOID_PAD = 0.02 mm`) dilate Z-clipped triangles and 3D edges by each tool stack band (`Flute`, `Shank`, `Holder`) plus `clearance + max(stock_to_leave, 0)`, while `avoid::hits_named` (`AVOID_VERIFY_TOL = 1e-4 mm`) sweeps every move independently across all stack bands and midpose chords.
- **Per-level planners & rapid link elevation**: Extracted `pocket_avoid` (`crates/motion/src/machining2d/pocket_avoid.rs`) and `avoid`-aware `pocket3d_avoid` (`ladder.rs`, `shell.rs`, `entry.rs`), checking `prev_center` on `KeepDown` links and elevating obstructed horizontal rapid moves via `elevate_rapid_links`. Rest-roughing skips safely with a note if only protected columns remain unmachined after a clean roughing ladder.
- **Commands, MCP, UI, live post gate, and project format v64**:
  - `SetOperationDoNotTouch`, `EditOperationParams`, `SetOperationGeometry`, `ChangeOperationKind`, and `EditOperationLinks` validate picks (rejecting vertices) and refuse overlap between protected items and the machining selection or `Include` boundaries by name.
  - Added `get_operation_do_not_touch` / `set_operation_do_not_touch`, `"do_not_touch"` on `get_operation_geometry`, `"Do not touch"` controls under `Geometry` -> `Boundary` -> `Boundaries`, and persistent viewport highlighting (`avoid_viz.rs`) while an operation is selected.
  - Bumped `PROJECT_VERSION` `63 -> 64` (stacked on `#2077`) so older builds refuse `.camproj` files that carry `"do_not_touch"` protection rather than silently dropping it.

### Why
- Separating `has_boundary_edits()` from `is_default()` on `AreaControls` lets `Offset2D` and `Pocket3D` use `"Do not touch"` without altering 2D boundary containment/extension semantics or existing stamps/goldens.
- Using one independent 3D full-stack verifier (`sim::verify::avoid`) across generation (`verify_avoid`) and posting (`live_avoid_problems` + `blocks_post`) prevents any generator quirk, rapid hop, or post-generation part move from ever emitting unsafe G-code.
- Extending `PROJECT_VERSION` prevents pre-v64 readers from silently discarding protection and cutting protected geometry.

### Considered and dropped
- Storing `do_not_touch` directly on `OpParams` or `Operation` instead of `AreaControls`: rejected because it touches hundreds of struct literals and duplicates copy/paste/draft plumbing that `AreaControls` already handles.
- Rolling out across all 2D/3D/multi-axis/turning operations in one PR: rejected in favor of a tight, end-to-end verified first slice (`2D Offset` and `3D Pocket`) that avoids stacking conflicts with open PRs `#1817`, `#1822`, `#2037`, and `#2093`.

### Cost to change later
- Extending `"Do not touch"` to additional operation kinds (`Pocket`, `Adaptive2D`, `Contour`, `Finish3D`, etc.) is additive: add the `OpType` variant to `do_not_touch_applies` and pass `avoid_spec` to that generator arm; `verify_avoid`, `route_links`, UI, commands, MCP, and v64 project format already work unchanged.

### Merge refresh against main v66

Main now writes project v66 for the trunnion schema (#1962), following
cutting rows (v64) and the tilt basis (v65). The protected-pick format must
therefore write v67. Reusing v64 or v66 would let an existing reader accept
the file and silently discard `do_not_touch`. All earlier migrations and
refusals remain. The project test pins a version beyond v66, protection
round trips, future-version refusal, and blocked posting after a moved
protected item. Reusing main's version was rejected because it would weaken
that protection. Main's carried-stock replan and previous-stock mask are
kept together with the protected-item planners.

### Merge refresh against main v70 and review fixes (#2149)

Main advanced to `PROJECT_VERSION` 70 (v68 for Drill `break_through_from`, #2441; v69 for Pocket Adaptive retirement, #1517; v70 for library holder reference, #2016), added `cut_levels_under` (#2004), `pocket3d_open_prev` (#1950), `Field::new` in `crossing_hop_tests`, and `crates/ui/AGENTS.md` Frame cost rules (#2238) + pick-highlight caching (#2201). On the merged branch:
- `PROJECT_VERSION` steps `70 -> 71` for `"do_not_touch"`, keeping v68, v69, and v70 migrations and refusals intact.
- `pocket3d_avoid`, `pocket3d_open_avoid`, and `pocket_avoid` keep `cut_levels_under` and `air_stock` while preserving `avoid` keep-outs, `Field::new` is restored alongside `Field::new_with_avoid`, and `Warning::AvoidHit` coexists with `Warning::DrillUndersize`.
- `avoid::hits_named` sweeps continuous 3D chords `Move::segments3(ARC_SAG)` widened by `Bulge::of(...).deviation()` across all arc planes (including XZ/YZ vertical arcs) instead of stationary `solid::pieces` samples.
- `avoid_viz` memoizes 3D protected geometry and projected screen marks keyed on picks, entity handles, hidden state, `Weak<Features>`, `Weak<[Triangle]>`, setup pose, and MVP bits, and `shell.rs` wraps painting in `frame_cost::time("ui/viewport.avoid_marks", ...)`.

### Example-version review fix against main v72 (#2149)

The branch merges current main and keeps its v72 linked-model fields,
checks, and migration notes. Protected projects use v73 so v72 readers
refuse the file instead of discarding protection. The committed continuous
4-axis example is regenerated at v73. Its test compares the saved project
directly with that example and keeps the posted-program checks.

Keeping the example at an older version, or migrating it inside the
comparison test, was rejected because either choice hides a stale committed
example. Reusing v72 was rejected because it weakens the protection barrier.
A later format change must update the writer, reader-floor pin, migration
notes, and committed example together.

## #2088 - Include shallow flat floors in the 3D Pocket ladder

**What was decided.** Add distinct heights from upward-facing, exactly flat
triangles, plus `stock_to_leave`, strictly between Top Z and the first
scheduled level below Top Z. Keep the regular levels. Use one helper for
plain, offset-shell, open-side and rest generation. The air-split ladder of
the rotary wrap keeps the plain level law: there a flat face is a turned
skin, and a window whose only open level is the wrap top stays air
(`rotary_offset::the_height_window_names_the_stations_and_refuses_an_empty_one`). The rest pass
uses its own half-stepdown. Keep the existing material targets, protected
areas, entry checks and no-gouge checks. Refuse a level count above
`MAX_PASSES`, while preserving an existing Top Z stock pass.

This change was stacked on PR #2149 because both changes touch the same
functions. PR #2149 merged to main. The branch then took a merge of main.
That merge keeps the shared `cut_levels` helper and main's `AdaptiveMethod`
argument on each ladder call. The protected-face integration is main's own.
Use `issue/2088-shallow-floor-levels` for this change. Preserve the older
`issue/2088-pocket3d-shallow-blind-floor` branch from closed PR #2141.

**Why.** The regular ladder can put its first level below a shallow blind
floor. The material checks then correctly reject every level in that hole.
A level at the floor cuts the hole without entering the solid below it.
Adding levels inside the first interval does not increase regular level
spacing. The existing target checks still decide where each level can cut.

**Considered and dropped.** Restoring a Top Z air pass would leave the
shallow hole uncut. Clamping Bottom Z would change the requested depth for
other areas. Retrying only after an empty result would miss a shallow hole
beside an area that already cuts. General discovery of sloped surfaces
would require a separate algorithm and more safety coverage.

**Cost to change later.** Discovery currently covers exactly flat upward
faces. A wider surface rule needs independent safety tests for slopes,
overhangs, stock allowance and shell motion. Keep the shared helper and
the per-level material checks when extending that rule.

**Validation.** All five blind-floor tests pass. Three mutation checks fail
with the corresponding change removed and pass after restoration. The quick
gate passes 611 steps. Clippy passes for `camcraft-motion`.

## #2105 - the machine page action row stands above the visible bottom at 720 px

**What was decided.** Two steps.

1. The "Refresh" button moves from its own prop_grid row onto the
   "Library" combo row. The row is built right-to-left, so the combo
   cannot push the button out of the cell. That change takes one row off
   the page.
2. A review of step 1 found it was not enough, and that the pin test
   measured the wrong edge. The page's visible bottom is not the bottom
   of the Properties leaf: `pages.rs` gives the page's ScrollArea the
   leaf height minus 40 px, and draws the separator and the `Close`
   footer in that bottom band. The pin test now measures each button's
   bottom against the top of `Close`. The page also reclaims height in
   three places:
   - its rows are drawn with a 2 px vertical gap of its own (`ROW_GAP`),
     where the shell draws 3 px;
   - the machine overview readout uses a 2 px row gap (`OVERVIEW_GAP`).
     `machine_grid` takes the gap as a parameter, and the machine editor
     header keeps its 4 px;
   - the two prose lines of the `ownership` block (the "where does the
     pick land" line and the one-machine-one-post line) are drawn small
     and dimmed, like the page's own help line. Each wrapped to three
     lines of 15 px in the 274 px pane; each now takes two lines of 10
     px. The words and the AccessKit labels are unchanged.

The page's three action buttons are "Load other", "Edit" and "Clear".
An earlier version of this file named one of them "New"; no such button
exists on the page.

**Measured.** In `shell_harness()` at 1280x720 with the Tormach 770MX
loaded: the Properties leaf spans y = 104..682, and the `Close` footer in
that pane starts at y = 648 - the page's body must end above it. Before
step 2 the action row spanned y = 644..668, below that edge: its bottom
stood 20 px under the top of `Close` (the review measured the page's
scroll area ending at about y = 642, so the row started outside it).
After step 2 the row spans y = 570..594: 54 px above the top of `Close`.

**Why.** The ribbon grew 22 px in #2027, and the machine page's action
row fell under the fold of a 720 px window: the user had to scroll to
reach "Load other", "Edit" and "Clear". The page is tall for its pane -
three titled groups, four rows of prose and radios, eight overview rows -
and the pane is 274 px wide, so the long lines wrap. One stacked row was
not enough; the page needs its own vertical rhythm and its prose lines
drawn smaller. No label, no command and no project field changed.

**Considered and dropped.**
- A smaller item spacing for every page: drops, it moves a shared value
  and changes every page. The page takes a gap of its own instead.
- Putting "Refresh" with the action buttons in one row: drops, the four
  buttons do not fit the pane's width.
- Reducing the page heading, or dropping the separator under it: drops,
  every other setup page keeps both, and the prose rows were the taller
  loss.
- Making the panel scroll-by-default: drops, the pin test says the
  buttons must be visible without scrolling.

**Cost to change later.** Low. The pin test
`the_machine_page_buttons_fit_without_scrolling_at_720_px` and the
`layout_page_setup_machine` anchors encode the Library row and the action
row; any new machine-file button must join one of those rows, and a
taller row on this page must pay for it from the same three gaps.

## #2158 - Deterministic true-shape nesting in camcraft-geometry

**Decided.** Integrate the held CamCraft nesting kernel from
`origin/issue/2158-nesting-kernel` into the current geometry crate. Keep the
existing `nesting.rs` entry point and its public raster module. Add no ECS,
world access, or crate dependencies. The algorithm follows Bennell and
Oliveira (EJOR 2008) and Burke, Hellier, Kendall, and Whitwell (OR 2006,
EJOR 2007); no third-party nesting implementation supplied code.

- Compute NFPs from convex decomposition and Minkowski sums on the existing
  `geo2d::SCALE` integer grid. Preserve zero-width seams swallowed by polygon
  unions so exact-fit cavities remain candidates. Compute rectangular IFPs
  from bounds and closed-hole IFPs from the container complement's NFP.
  Keep triangulation and its slab fallback local to nesting.
- Place parts with deterministic bottom-left-fill. Sort by decreasing outer
  area, then stable part id, then instance index. Try permitted rotations
  and mirrors, deduplicate equivalent footprints, and cache local NFPs.
  Outer-area ordering places a hollow frame before parts that can use its
  holes even when the frame's net material area is smaller.
- Apply separate-cut inflation by cut side: `cut_width + part_gap / 2`
  outside, `cut_width / 2 + part_gap / 2` on line, and `part_gap / 2`
  inside. Buffer open chains with `Region::sweep`. Offer an explicit router
  single-slot mode and refuse it when `part_gap < cut_width`.
- Reduce the sheet by `edge_margin` with `Region::offset_sharp`, then keep
  each cut footprint inside that usable sheet. The footprint already
  includes outer cutter clearance, avoiding double-counting at the edge.
- Search usable holes before allocating a new sheet. Treat placed hole
  occupants as filled outer obstacles within their parent's hole. Expose
  their own holes separately and report the immediate containing part.
  Require empty intersection and outside-difference regions during exact
  verification; a small positive overlap is not accepted as a tolerance.
- Check requested-quantity addition and refuse totals above 10,000
  instances by name. This bounds placement work and report allocation.
  Report counts, net-area utilization, used bounds, waste regions, and
  named unplaced quantities without producing toolpaths or G-code.

**Why.** Reusing the held clean-room work preserves its existing geometry
coverage while adapting only the entry point and refusal checks to current
main. Convex decomposition makes concavities and swept-chain polygons use
the same geometry operations. Explicit seams retain exact fits, while the
final region checks enforce clearance independently of candidate generation.

**Dropped.** Orbital NFP sliding needs more state around collinear edges and
pinched cavities. Net-area sorting can place a small solid before its
larger hollow host. Raster-only placement cannot establish exact vector
clearance. Changing `geo2d::Region::triangles()` would broaden this issue;
the fallback remains local. Unbounded quantities risk impractical loops or
allocation, and positive-area overlap tolerances weaken the zero-overlap
contract.

**Validation.** The unchanged upstream API failed the pinning build. The
restored kernel passed 66 focused tests. Nine runtime mutations each failed
their pin and passed after restoration: hole containment, tiny overlap,
router gap, negative input, quantity overflow, quantity cap, kerf inflation,
NFP seams, and filled-hole obstacles. Restoring upstream `nesting.rs` also
failed the API pins and passed after restoration. The quick gate passed all
936 steps, and geometry all-targets clippy passed with warnings denied.
No G-code or CL goldens changed. App and motion heavy lanes were planned
but not run; the PR remains a draft.

**Cost to change.** NFP, IFP, and placement search stay behind internal
functions. Another search heuristic or a configurable quantity budget can
replace those policies without changing the geometry primitives. Raising
the quantity cap requires performance and memory measurements. Changing the
public input or report structs requires updating downstream nesting users.
