file without a word (#2648). A silent ignore is not allowed: the run opens
the file or refuses it by name.

**Considered and dropped.**

- Refuse every file on a headless start: simpler, but it throws away a
  useful check - a script can now ask "does this file import and draw?"
  with no window and read the exit code.
- Open the file on top of the seeded document: the seed's own checks
  (Contour1's toolpath) would then pass whatever the file did.

**Cost to change later.** Low: one module and the headless entry; the
tests in `crates/ui/tests/egui_app.rs` pin the exit codes.

## #2649 - Sodick wire post: pass structure for LN1W / LN2W controls

**Decided.** `assets/posts/sodick-wire.cps` now posts a Wire Contour
with skim passes. Before this change, it refused them by name (#617, #538).
- The rough pass keeps its own C word, written after the threading
  (T91), before the first move.
- Each skim's C word is written after the previous pass's return to the
  threading point and before the skim's first move. The wire stays
  threaded. There is one T91 and one T90 for the section, and the pass
  links stay G01 (no rapid with the wire threaded).
- A note line names each skim and tells the operator that its condition
  must exist in the control's table.
- A skim condition id that is not `C` and three digits is refused by name.
- A new boolean post option, `approachCondition` (default off), writes
  `C000` before the first approach move (threading point to the
  contour). The operation's C word follows that move. Skims get no C000.
- With the option off, the output is byte-identical to the output before
  this change (the #617 goldens do not change).

**Sources.** Sodick Inc., "Wire EDM Machine Operation Training, LN1W /
LN2W Control" (AQ400L, AQ600L, AD360L; part number 6300015, January 2012),
public at fab.cba.mit.edu/content/tools/sodick_edm/sodick_user_manual_small.pdf.
Only behaviour is used, and no text or sample program is copied:
- the word list gives C001 for the first cut, C002 for the second and
  C903 for the third;
- the NC program example selects the next pass's C word after the pass
  returns to its start point, before the next pass, with the wire left
  threaded;
- the condition header rows name C000 / H000 "Approach".

**Why.** The #617 refusal was there because no public source showed a
condition change between passes. The LN manual shows it, so the refusal
is no longer necessary. A 2- or 3-pass contour is the normal LN job.

**Inferred, not stated (check at a control).**
- The manual names C000 "Approach" but does not show where a program
  writes it. We read "approach" as the move from the start point onto
  the contour (the manual uses the word for that move). This is why the
  option is off by default, and why only the first pass gets C000.
- Whether C000 is used at each start hole, or only on some controls.
- Flushing for skims: the manual's example changes flushing for the
  finish passes. This post writes the machine's one `edm.flushing` word
  after the threading only. It writes no flushing word for a skim. The
  operator sets it, as the header already says when no word is stated.
- The program writes no condition header table. The operator must have
  each C row in the control (the existing #617 note).

**Dropped.**
- C000 on by default: no source shows its placement, and a C000 row that
  does not exist on the control would stop the program.
- C000 before each skim: a skim starts at the threading point on the
  finished kerf, and the source does not show it.
- A flushing change for each skim: the machine file states one flushing
  word, and no operation parameter carries a skim's flushing.
- A per-pass offset word (H): the path is the wire-centre path with each
  pass's offset in it, as before (#1498).

**Cost to change later.** The skim C word placement is one function
(`startSkim`). The C000 placement is one branch in `startCut`. A change
of the default changes the #617 goldens.

## #2651 - Refresh the continuous 4-axis example project

**What was decided:** Regenerate the example project with the existing test.
Keep the posted NC program unchanged.
Add a direct test that compares the committed version with `PROJECT_VERSION`.

**Why:** The DXF import change raised the project format to version 71.
The example still used version 70, so the existing comparison failed.
The new test identifies this mismatch without generating a toolpath.
Regeneration changes only the version field.

**What was dropped:** Do not relax the project comparison or change the serializer.
The comparison correctly detected a stale fixture.
Do not stack on #2563. The maintainer explicitly accepted this overlap on #2651.
That PR must retain the current version when it refreshes.

**Cost to change later:** A future project format change must regenerate this example.
The version test reads `PROJECT_VERSION`, so it needs no version literal update.

## #2655 - Thread mill on a detected through hole: excuse the exit face in ThreadBore

**Decided.** Add `pub exit: Option<f64>` to `ThreadBore` in `crates/sim/src/verify/thread_bore.rs`, populated as `h.through.then_some(h.floor_z)` in `crates/app/src/operation/thread_rims.rs`. In `ThreadBore::wall_radius`, alongside vertical minor-wall facets and mouth facets at or above `self.top - WALL_BAND`, excuse a facet on the hole's minor circle band when `self.exit` is `Some(exit)` and `at_exit` holds: every vertex satisfies `z <= exit + WALL_BAND`, and every vertex on the minor circle satisfies `z >= exit - WALL_BAND`. `excused` also requires `exit` (when present) to be finite and `<= top`.

**Why.** On a through hole (`through: true`), `machining2d::thread_mill` extends the helix one pitch below `floor_z` so the teeth cut a full thread out the bottom exit, and the cutter spans across the plate's bottom face at `floor_z`. `ThreadBore` previously knew only `top` (`entry_z`) and excused horizontal mouth facets only at `z >= top - WALL_BAND`. Every bottom-face triangle sharing the hole's minor rim had `wall_radius` return `None`, so the solid law convicted the lead-in and helix moves crossing `floor_z` with `Gouge` ("cuts past the finish surface").

Requiring `z <= exit + WALL_BAND` on all vertices and `z >= exit - WALL_BAND` on the minor-circle vertices matches flat exit faces and downward-drafted undersides while still convicting blind hole floors (`exit: None`), intermediate shelves between `exit` and `top`, lower parts or shelves below `exit - WALL_BAND`, steps reaching inside the minor circle, and cuts past the model's major cylinder.

**Considered and dropped.**
- Raising `floor` in `thread_mill` so the cutter never crosses `floor_z`: would leave an incomplete thread at the exit of a through hole.
- Checking only `max z <= exit + WALL_BAND` without bounding the on-circle vertices at `exit - WALL_BAND`: would excuse a separate plate or step sitting below the threaded plate if it shared the same hole XY and minor radius.
- Requiring all three vertices inside `[exit - WALL_BAND, exit + WALL_BAND]`: would falsely convict a bottom face drafted downward away from the hole exit.

**Cost to change later.** One `Option<f64>` field on `ThreadBore` and one helper (`at_exit`) in `crates/sim/src/verify/thread_bore.rs`, populated in `crates/app/src/operation/thread_rims.rs`.

## #2657 - Filter open region rims by wall classification in Boundary tangency with a model

**Decided.** In `sim::verify::section::tangency`, when `cx.mode == Mode::Boundary` and `cx.model.is_some()`, each edge of `cx.region` is checked against the move's `chords` only when `edge_is_wall(p, q, section)` holds (part material in `section` stands `WALL_PROBE` off the edge's midpoint on either side). All edges of `section` itself remain unconditionally checked, and `Mode::Area` as well as no-model `Mode::Boundary` keep checking every edge of `cx.region`. The midpoint probe previously inline in `wall_gouge` was extracted to `edge_is_wall` so both laws share one predicate.

**Why.** A `Face` operation with `holes: lift` clips row pieces at a radius off each hole. When a hole lies within two tool radii of the open outer rim, a plunge or feed endpoint lands less than one tool radius inside that rim. With no material standing above `z + lift` at the rim, that rim is open and not a wall; checking all `cx.region` loops unconditionally raised false `Warning::Gouge` findings that blocked posting. Walls standing above the cut plane — including walls whose top sits below the highest point of the model — remain present in `section` and satisfy `edge_is_wall`, so moves within `r - tol` of those walls still report `Warning::Gouge`.

**Dropped.**
- Dropping `cx.region` altogether whenever `Mode::Boundary` has `cx.model.is_some()`: dropped because keeping `edge_is_wall`-filtered `cx.region` edges preserves per-loop `floor_of` tolerances and aligns `tangency`'s edge law with `wall_gouge`.
- Adding a Face-specific exemption flag on `VerifyContext`: dropped to keep the verifier independent of operation names and consistent with the existing `wall_gouge` geometry rule.

**Cost to change later.** One helper (`edge_is_wall`) and one guard (`boundary_with_model`) in `crates/sim/src/verify/section.rs`.

## #2677 - Whole-model contour: fence the lead room at a shared level

**Decided.** The whole-model 2D Contour plans all its bands first and emits
them at the end (`contour_whole_fence.rs`). Before a band is emitted, its lead
room (`PreparedBand::room`) is its center region plus a thin fence (0.05 mm on
each side) around each ring of another band that is cut on a level this band
cuts too. The lead fitter (`lead_fit.rs`) then shortens, reseats or refuses a
lead that would cross that ring. The levels do not change. An error that
carries the partial path (ghost) emits the planned bands first, so the ghost
is the same as before.

**Why.** With the stock top one stepdown or more over Top Z, the grown ring
must take Top Z as its first level: a lower first level bites more than one
stepdown. So the grown ring shares the Top Z plane with the band-0 ring, and
a lead longer than the gap between the two rings crosses the other ring at
the same Z. The verifier's `Crossing` law then blocks the post. The same
happens with no stock over Top Z, at the flat levels under Top Z. The only
fix that keeps the law and the stepdown is in the lead room.

**Dropped.**
- A level a little off Top Z for the grown ring: that hides the law (two
  passes 1 um apart cross in fact) and was refused by the issue.
- A level under Top Z: the first bite is then more than one stepdown.
- Emit order changes: the `Crossing` law does not depend on the move order.

**Costs and limits.**
- The fence is per band, not per level: a lead of a band on a level that no
  other band shares can also shrink at a fenced ring. This is conservative.
- The fence leaves a 0.1 mm gap around the band's own rings, so a ring of
  another band that runs on one of them (a touch, not a crossing) does not
  close the lead's own start.
- Lead notes of a band now come after the planning notes of the later bands,
  and a planning error of a later band now comes before an emit error of an
  earlier band.
- To change it later: give `room` per level, or make `upper_levels` move the
  other ring's levels instead.

## #2679 - Typed text becomes a profile of engraving strokes (first slice)

**What was decided**

1. The first ride mode is single-line engraving. A typed string becomes
   tool-centreline strokes, not glyph outlines.
2. The strokes come from our own stroke font, drawn from scratch for this
   project (`crates/geometry/src/stroke_text/glyphs.rs`). The font has
   capital letters, digits, the space and `- _ . : / # + = ( )`. Each glyph
   is straight strokes on a 4 x 6 grid with cut corners. The zero has a
   slash.
3. `InsertText` makes the same `Sketch` entity that `ImportDxf` makes: line
   primitives in millimetres on the layer `text`, placed on the top face of
   the setup's stock at X, Y and an angle. `MoveSketch`, `DeleteEntity`, the
   project file and `get_job` work on it with no change.
4. A character with no glyph is refused by name. A lower-case letter is not
   written as a capital.
5. This PR is a first slice (`Refs #2679`). It ships the font, the command
   and the MCP tool `insert_text`. It does not ship the toolpath.

**Why**

- The issue says to use a font bundled in `assets/ui/fonts/`. That directory
  does not exist on `main`, and the repository holds no font file. The UI
  text comes from the default fonts inside the `egui` crates. To read their
  outlines, `camcraft-geometry` or `camcraft-app` needs a font parser and the
  font data as new dependencies. A new dependency waits for the maintainer
  (`needs-maintainer`), and the worker brief forbids a `Cargo.toml` change.
- The Engrave and Trace generators cut along the tool centreline. A
  centreline along a glyph outline gives hollow letters. A single-line stroke
  gives the solid mark that a part number needs, with a v-bit or a small end
  mill, in one pass for each stroke.
- A skeleton computed from outlines is a new algorithm (medial axis). A
  drawn stroke font gives the same ride mode with a table and no algorithm.
- Sketch chaining refuses a chain that branches. The glyphs are drawn so
  that a stroke end meets a different stroke only inside a segment. For
  example the arms of `Y` meet on a short flat, and the stem ends in that
  flat. `stroke_text::sketch` fails if a chain is rejected, and
  `each_glyph_chains_with_no_rejection_at_the_extreme_heights` pins each
  glyph. A text sketch can never hold a rejected chain.
- A silent change of the typed text is a wrong mark on a part. A refusal by
  name is safe.
- On `main`, generation from the chains of a profile is refused by name
  (`sketch_model::generation_problem`). #1869 adds Engrave and Trace on
  sketch chains, and it depends on #1864 (PR #2716). The toolpath, the
  verify and the golden CL of this issue need #1869. This slice does not
  touch those functions, so it does not conflict with that work.

**Considered and dropped**

- Glyph outlines from the `egui` default fonts: needs two new dependencies
  and a decision of the maintainer. It can come later as a second font
  source; `TextSpec` is the place for a font choice.
- A public-domain stroke font (Hershey): the clean-room rule permits it, but
  a data file needs a licence entry and a parser. Our own table is 47 short
  rows.
- Lower-case glyphs: 26 more drawings. Part numbers are capitals and digits.
  A later PR can add them to the table.
- The text string as an editable parameter of the Engrave operation: this
  needs a new schema field and a project version step. PR #2716 also steps
  the project version. In this slice the text is fixed when it is placed;
  to change it, delete the profile and place it again.
- A script verb `cam.insertText`: the MCP tool calls the command directly.
  The verb can follow with the UI.
- Placement on a picked model face: a `Sketch` lies on the top face of the
  setup's stock only (`sketch::face_frame`). Other faces need a change of
  that law.
- New wording for the refusals that say "DXF profile": a text profile reads
  as a "DXF profile" in those messages. The wording is used in many tests
  and in PR #2716, so it stays for now.

**Cost to change later**

- A new glyph or a changed glyph is one table row; the golden string in
  `crates/geometry/tests/stroke_text.rs` moves if its glyphs move.
- A saved project stores the strokes, not the text. A font change does not
  change a saved project.
- An outline font can be added behind `stroke_text` without a change to
  `InsertText` or to the project file.

## #2683 - LinuxCNC and Tormach probe posts: a rotated work offset stops the offset write

**What was decided.** Before each `G10 L20` that writes X or Y,
`tormach.cps` and `linuxcnc.cps` write a run-time test of the XY rotation
of the section's work offset and of the target work offset. A rotation
that is not zero shows `(MSG, PROBE: G54 OR G55 XY ROTATION NOT ZERO -
NO OFFSET WRITTEN)` and ends the program with `M2`. The offset is not written.

```
o903 if [[#5230 NE 0] OR [#5250 NE 0]]
(MSG, PROBE: G54 OR G55 XY ROTATION NOT ZERO - NO OFFSET WRITTEN)
M2
o903 endif
G10 L20 P2 X[#5420-#190] Y[#5421-#191]
```

When the target is the section's own work offset, the test names one
register (`o903 if [#5230 NE 0]`). A result that sets only Z has no test.
A measure-only result has no test.

**Why.**

- The rotation is a register of the control (`R` of `G10 L2`, parameter
  5210 + 20 x the system number: `#5230` for G54). The post cannot read it
  at post time. Only the program can test it.
- The rule "target = active offset + deviation" (#2610) is proved for
  unrotated systems. With all rotations zero, the guard never fires and the
  proof holds.
- Case 1, the target has a rotation that differs from the active system's.
  This is wrong by algebra, with no doubt about the control. Let the active
  system have origin `a` and rotation `α`, the target rotation `τ`, the
  machine position `m` and the deviation `d`. The write gives the target
  origin `t' = m - R(τ-α)(m-a) - R(τ)d`. This depends on `m`. The target is
  correct at the probe position only. At a distance `r` from that position
  the error is `2 r sin(|α-τ|/2)`. `G10 L20` does not write `R`.
- Case 2, the two rotations are equal (the target can be the active
  system). The LinuxCNC reference says that `G10 L20` makes "the current
  coordinates become the given value". For the written axes this gives the
  correct result. For an axis that has no word (an edge probe writes X
  only), the reference does not say if the control keeps the coordinate
  along the rotated axis or keeps the stored offset along the machine axis.
  With the second rule, an X deviation `d` also moves Y by `d tan(R)`.
  Nothing here was run on a control. The Prime Directive permits a
  visible refusal and does not permit an unproved offset.
- A rotation about Z does not change Z. A face result (Z only) stays
  unguarded, so that a rotated system can still get its Z from a probe.

**What was considered and dropped.**

- Guard only case 1 (`[#5230 NE #5250]`), and trust case 2. Dropped: case 2
  depends on a control rule that the public reference does not state.
- Copy the rotation to the target (`G10 L2 P2 R[#5230]`) before the write.
  Dropped: it is a new function, it changes a register that the operator
  set, and it still depends on the rule of case 2.
- Refuse at post time. Not possible: the post does not know the rotation.
- Test before the first probe move. Dropped as not necessary: the probe
  moves and the trip values are in the rotated frame and are correct. Only
  the write is in doubt. The stop comes after the deviation reports, so the
  operator still sees the measured values.
- A LinuxCNC controller model with rotation in the tests. Dropped here:
  #2682 owns the model, and a model that we write cannot prove the rule of
  a control.

**Cost to change later.** If a run on LinuxCNC or PathPilot shows that
`G10 L20` keeps the rotated-frame coordinate of an axis without a word,
the guard can become "the two rotations differ" (`[#5230 NE #5250]`, and
no test when the target is the section's system). That is one expression
in each post, the five tests of `probe_rotated_wcs.rs` and the six
goldens that this PR moved.

**Workaround for the operator.** Clear the rotation (`G10 L2 P<n> R0`),
probe, then set the rotation again. Or probe with a measure-only operation
and read `#190`.. .

## #2686 - Sodick wire post: the flushing of a skim pass

**Decided.** A wire machine file can state `edm.skim_flushing` (`high` or
`low`). It is the flushing of each skim pass of a Wire Contour.
- `assets/posts/sodick-wire.cps` writes its T word (T84 / T85) before
  each skim's C word. The order is the #1499 order: the T word, then the
  C word.
- The rough cut keeps `edm.flushing`, written after each threading
  (#1499). The next operation's rough cut selects it again, so a skim's
  word does not stay active.
- `edm.skim_flushing` needs `edm.flushing`. The machine file parser, the
  parsed-machine check (`Edm::is_sane`, `Edm::refusal`) and the post
  refuse a skim flushing without it, by name.
- A skim on a machine that states `edm.flushing` and no
  `edm.skim_flushing` is refused by name. The app writes no file.
- A machine that states no flushing posts its skims as before (#2649).
  The header tells the operator to set the flushing at the control. The
  three existing Sodick goldens do not change.
- The key is in the post's machine mirror only when stated. The machine
  editor offers it only while a flushing is stated. The MCP
  `edit_machine` tool takes it through the same machine patch.
- `assets/posts/wire-iso.cps` has no word for it. It writes a note that
  the stated skim flushing is not programmed.

**Why the machine file.** The issue permits the machine file or an
operation parameter. `edm.flushing` is a machine fact already (#1499),
and the rough cut's word comes from it. One more key of the same type
keeps the two values together and needs no new command, no project file
change and no new MCP tool.

**Why the refusal.** T84 / T85 is modal. After #2649, a program with
`edm.flushing: high` and skims cut each skim on high pressure, and the
program did not say so. That value was not stated by the user. The
issue's "refuses by name when the value is not known" is read as this
case. This is a behaviour change: such a program posted before and is
refused now. The message names the key to state.

**Sources.** The T84 / T85 words are from the T-code table of the 1998
Sodick "Wire EDM Machine Operation" manual (#617, #1499). The issue
states that the program example of the 2012 "Wire EDM Machine Operation
Training, LN1W / LN2W Control" manual (part number 6300015) changes the
flushing for the finish passes. This PR did not read the manual again.
The position of the word (immediately before the skim's C word) is
inferred from the #1499 order, not read from the manual. The output was
not run on a Sodick control.

**Dropped.**
- A flushing for each skim pass (`WireSkim.flushing`, an operation
  parameter): it needs a project file field, a command change, an MCP
  change and a property panel field. One value for all skims covers the
  manual's example. It can be added later without a change to this key.
- A flushing field on each condition row (`edm.conditions[].flushing`):
  it ties the flushing to the C word, which is closest to the control's
  own table. It is a larger change of the condition table and its
  editor.
- A default (low pressure for a skim): the post never guesses a value.
- Skipping the T word when the skim flushing equals the rough flushing:
  the word is always written, so the program states each pass's flushing.

**Cost to change later.** A per-skim or per-condition value can
override `edm.skim_flushing`. The key then stays as the default for
skims that state none.

## #2689 - A linked model's digest is of the bytes the import parsed

**What was decided.**

- `ImportModel::within` reads the file once
  (`geometry/import/sourced.rs`, `load_model_open_sourced`). A buffered
  format (OBJ, STEP, `.sc`) hashes the buffer it parses. STL keeps its
  streaming parse (the M5.3 E law: the file never coexists with its
  triangles) and is hashed as the stream reads it, through a reader that
  hashes every byte it hands out. The ASCII path rewinds to byte 0 once
  after the sniff; the rewind starts the hash again. Any other seek is
  refused, so the digest is always of one pass. Bytes after the last
  binary facet, if the file grew, are read into the same pass.
- So a file that changes during the import records the digest of the
  bytes that made the mesh. The link check then sees the newer file as
  changed and imports it again. Before, the digest came from a second
  read after the parse, and a change between the two reads was missed.
- The kernel's SHA-256 takes bytes in pieces (`Sha256`, `update`,
  `finish_hex`); `hex_digest` is that over one piece. Pinned against the
  one-shot digest for every split around the padding edges.
- The link check (`model_source::read`) hashes the file in 1 MiB pieces.
  Before, it read the whole file into memory every time a linked file
  changed, which for a large STL broke the same memory law.
- The browser build is unchanged: it records no link.

**Why.** Found in the review of #2563 (#2689). Solidcraft's Send to
CamCraft (tangency-labs/solidcraft#18936) saves the design while CamCraft
may still be importing the previous save; that change must not be lost.

**Considered and dropped.**

- Read STL into memory like the other formats: one line, but it breaks
  the streaming law for the largest files.
- Compare the file's size and time before and after the parse, and
  record no digest on a change: it would unlink the model, or need a
  marker digest that is not a real one.

**Cost to change later.** Low: one module, one kernel type; the tests in
`crates/app/tests/model_link.rs` and `sha256.rs` pin the behaviour.

## #2693 - Explicit `heal_tolerance` on `WireRuled` bounds 2D swallowtail acceptance

**What was decided.**

- Add `pub heal_tolerance: f64` directly to `WireRuled`
  (`crates/motion/src/wire_edm/ruled.rs`), distinct from twist
  `tolerance`, and validate `is_finite() && >= 0.0` at the
  `wire_contour_ruled` door. Existing callers (`operation/wire_ruled.rs`
  and existing tests) pass `0.0` until #2696 exposes the field in
  `WireFourAxis`, UI, and MCP.
- Add `laws::cover_healed` returning `Option<UncutRest>` alongside
  unchanged `laws::cover` and `laws::cover_run` for 2-axis, open, and
  burnout cuts. It accepts `d <= k + heal_tolerance.max(COVER_TOL)`,
  records the worst `d - k` and `Point3` spot whenever `d - k > COVER_TOL`,
  and keeps the `heal_tolerance == 0.0` refusal byte-for-byte identical.
  When `heal_tolerance > 0.0` is exceeded, the refusal states the spot,
  measured depth `d - k`, and stated `heal_tolerance`.
- In `ruled::emit`, enforce strict `laws::kerf` (`PATH_TOL`) on both the
  lower `Toolpath` moves and the upper ring + leads, and append one
  uncut-rest note to `Toolpath::notes` naming the worst rest across both
  planes, its `X/Y/Z` spot, and the `heal_tolerance`.
- In `ruled_widen`, combine `UncutRest::worse` across the `s = 1.0` cover
  checks and the post-widening `scaled(z, wide)` cover checks so twist
  widening on one flank cannot hide uncut corner rest on an unwidened
  flank, while still catching corners whose widening increases rest.

**Why.** `Region::offset_sharp` already trims local inside-corner
swallowtails and bridges shallow slots in 2D, and `laws::cover`
previously refused every case past `COVER_TOL` (`0.002 mm`). Bounding
that acceptance with an explicit opt-in `heal_tolerance` preserves all
strict refusals at `0.0`, keeps `laws::kerf` (`PATH_TOL`) and ruled laws
intact, and lets the user see the exact worst uncut rest left on the
part.

**Considered and dropped.**

- Reusing `WireRuled::tolerance`: dropped because twist widening moves
  the wire outward past the kerf offset on non-developable flanks,
  whereas `heal_tolerance` bounds uncut material left inside tight
  corners or shallow slots.
- Emitting one note per plane: dropped in favour of one note naming the
  worst rest and its 3D spot (`X/Y/Z`) across both planes.
- Passing `heal_tolerance` into `WireRuled` via a separate helper
  function instead of a struct field: dropped because the struct field is
  the explicit public contract for `wire_contour_ruled` and #2696.

**Cost to change later.** Low: contained within `wire_edm/{laws,ruled,ruled_widen}`
and `WireRuled` construction sites; pinned by `ruled_heal_tests`.

## #2694 - Wire input preimages

**What was decided:** Detect healing when an input edge disappears, after
removing redundant collinear vertices. Match surviving offset edges by
direction and midpoint. Project their vertices to input arc coordinates.
Hold each excised span at its trim vertex. `Ring::at` and `Ring::nearest`
use those coordinate spans. When either plane heals, sew both planes on
their input coordinates. Preserve the existing offset-length rule otherwise.

Use nearby surviving offset segments for widening directions on healed
rings. Include tiny bevels within one offset distance to prevent reversal.
Keep cover, folds, crossing, lean, and 33-height clearance against the
unhealed product. Refuse unknown or non-monotone source matches by name.

**Why:** Shortened offset lengths caused phase drift and missing fans.
Normals from removed input edges caused a widening fold. Eleven pins,
the 12-step quick gate, and clippy pass. No golden files change.

**Considered and dropped:** A vertex-count check missed healing after
straight-edge subdivision. Direct pairing of shortened rings failed the fan
pins. Original-edge widening failed its mutation check. Relaxing cover is
separate work. Changing all unhealed pairings would change established behavior.

**Cost to change later:** Broader join support needs new fixtures and source
matching rules in the wire module. This change adds no dependency, file
format, or command.

# docs/decisions/2710-arc-swept-extremes.md

## #2710 - The travel check judges the quarter points that an arc sweeps

Date: 2026-11-19. Taken unattended by the issue worker.

**What was decided**

`machine::judge::move_extremes` returns the two endpoints of an arc, plus a
quarter point of its circle only when the sweep passes that point. The sweep
runs from `from` to `to` in the direction of `arc.ccw`, in the arc's own
plane. This is the same reading that `cl::plane::sweep` gives to the chords
and that the post writes as G2/G3.

The check stays strict. It keeps all four quarter points in these cases:

- The in-plane endpoints are 0.01 mm apart or less (`SAME_WORD`). Their NC
  words can be equal, and a control turns equal endpoints a full circle.
- The sweep reads zero or is not finite (endpoints on one ray, a bad center).

The radius is the larger of the two endpoint radii. The old code used the
radius at `from`. A ramping arc (a thread ramp) can be larger at `to`, and a
selective check must not read it smaller than it is.

A quarter point within 1e-9 rad of an endpoint counts as swept
(`ANGLE_SLACK`). No test can show this guard alone, because the endpoint
itself is always judged. It costs nothing and it cannot hide a point.

One function now serves XY, XZ and YZ arcs. `ArcPlane::uvw` is the identity
for XY, so the XY values do not change.

**Why**

A four-decimal inch post has a 0.00254 mm step on each axis. Endpoints
less than 0.0036 mm apart can round to the same point on a diagonal.
The 0.01 mm bound includes margin and agrees with `ring_zig::MIN_ARC_CHORD`.

A shallow arc of a 22 m radius is a legal move. The old check judged points
22 m away from the tool and refused the program on each machine size. The
issue's reporter and the triage comment asked for the swept reading.

**Considered and dropped**

- A 0.001 mm endpoint bound. It misses endpoints that round to one point
  with four-decimal inch words or three-decimal mm words.

- A cap on the arc radius, or a switch to chords for large radii. Two
  readings of one arc can disagree; the swept quarter points are exact.
- A call to `cl::plane::sweep`. It is `pub(crate)` in `camcraft-cl`, and the
  judge needs the start angle, which `ArcMove::radius_sweep` does not give.
  A wider `camcraft-cl` API is not needed for six lines of angle math.
- A change to `#1882` (program bounds) and to `#2585` (the move of
  `judge.rs` to `camcraft-post`). They are separate issues.
- A check for a non-finite quarter point. The comparison with the stroke
  already passes NaN silently in the callers; that is older behaviour and a
  separate defect, if it is one.

## #2713 - A refined STEP face has no flat cap facets

**What was decided.** The STEP importer flips edges after it splits a curved
face (`geometry/import/step_fit.rs`, `relax`). The rule is Lawson's edge
flip, measured in space: an inside edge whose two opposite angles sum to
more than a half turn is replaced by the other diagonal of its two facets.
A flip is made only where the two new facets keep their winding in the
parameter plane and the new edge passes the chord-height limit of the
split. No point moves. No boundary edge changes. Only a face that the split
of #2600 changed is flipped.

**Why.** The test `feature_edge_g1_join` was red on `main` for the fixture
`bar_cross_holes.step` (116 split pieces). The join law was not the cause.
The split of #2600 measures facet edges only. It left flat "cap" facets on
the bar's wall: three points on the cylinder, the apex over the middle of
the long edge. Each edge of such a facet is within the limit, but the
facet's normal stood up to 65 degrees off the radius (2 147 of 131 834
wall facets over 25 degrees). The feature graph read the edges of these
facets as creases, and some facets as faces of their own. The pick showed
3 701 edges on the bar; most were on the smooth wall. Those false edges
were the split pieces. After the flip the worst wall normal is 6.5 degrees
off, the bar has 642 pickable edges and 0 split pieces.

**Considered and dropped.**

- *Keep the fixture out of the test.* The issue permits it. It makes the
  gate green, but the user still sees false edges on the wall of each bar
  or tube with a cross hole, and facet normals that are wrong by 40 to 65
  degrees stay in the mesh.
- *Change the join law (`feature/g1_seam.rs`, `feature/trail.rs`).* The
  law is correct for real edges. A law that joins false creases makes them
  longer, not absent.
- *Make the crease rule of the feature graph ignore thin facets.* This
  changes face and chain ids of every model (saved selections, goldens) to
  hide a defect of one importer.
- *Flip in rounds over the full face.* The first version did this. The
  import of the bar took 18 s in a debug build (2.6 s before). The queue
  version builds the edge table one time; the import takes 5.5 s.

**What it costs.** The import of a face that the split changed takes
longer (the bar: 2.6 s to 5.5 s in a debug build). The facet count does
not change. A face that the kernel meshed correctly is not changed, so
other models import as before. The flip is capped at 8 flips for each
facet of the face; a cap facet that is left then stays as it was.
A cap facet whose long edge is on the face's boundary cannot be flipped
and stays.

## #2713 - Add the missing kernel fixture row in this PR

**What was decided.** Add the triage row for `bar_cross_holes.step` to
`crates/kernel/tests/step_agreement.rs` in this PR. The import refuses with
`solidcore refuses: #655 at read: pcurves failed on`. The mesh reports
`no exact solid to judge against`. The test `step_bar_cross_holes` pins
these results.

**Why.** The review found that the fixture has no row. The agreement test
must cover every STEP fixture. The issue requires both this test and
`feature_edge_g1_join` to pass.

**Considered and dropped.** File a separate issue for the missing row.
That leaves the agreement test red after this PR.

**What it costs.** Run the kernel agreement suite explicitly. A later
change to the fixture requires a new triage of its agreement row.

## #2713 - Keep the measured bound when merging #2718

**What was decided.** Keep the split and flip limit at
`tol / kind.inside()`. Keep the measured height from #2718 and include the
largest height of every new diagonal accepted by the flip. Multiply this
bound by `kind.inside()` when reporting the mesh error.

**Why.** The split measures the edges before the flip. A new diagonal can
have a larger chord height than those edges. The reported bound must cover
the edges that the flip adds, as well as the edges already measured.

**Considered and dropped.** Keep the old measured bound without the new
diagonals. That bound can understate the error of the mesh after a flip.

**What it costs.** Each accepted flip updates the largest height. No extra
surface evaluation or pass over the mesh is needed. The bound can retain
the height of an edge that a later flip removes, which is conservative.

## #2718 - STEP import: report the height of the kept curved facets, and split to the tolerance

**What was decided.** The curved-face fit (`step_fit.rs`, #2600) measures
every edge of the facets that it keeps, inside and boundary. It reports the
highest edge height times a bound for the inside of a facet:

- cylinder: 1.0 (the facet is inscribed in the circle; its edges bound it);
- cone, sphere, torus: 1.5 (the bound for a surface curved two ways is
  4/3, from the linear-interpolation error identity of Waldron, SIAM J.
  Numer. Anal. 35, 1998; 1.5 is a margin over it).

The import takes the larger of this value and the pass tolerance as the
model's chord. An inside edge is now split until its height is at most
`tol / inside`, not `2 x tol`.

**Why.**

- Before, the fit kept inside edges up to `2 x tol` (0.01 mm) and the
  import reported `tol` (0.005 mm). The model said full fidelity while its
  facets stood up to twice the cap off the surface.
- With only the honest report, the D50 cross-hole bar fixture
  (`bar_cross_holes.step`) reads 0.00999 mm. That is over `CHORD_CAP`
  (0.005 mm), so the bar becomes reduced fidelity and verify refuses ops on
  it. To keep the bar at full fidelity with a raised cap is a loosening of a
  threshold. To split to the tolerance keeps the report honest and under the
  cap: the bar reads 0.005 mm after the change.

**What was considered and dropped.**

- Report only, keep `2 x tol`: honest, but it moves the bar fixture and
  each similar model to reduced fidelity. Dropped.
- Raise `CHORD_CAP` to 0.01 mm: a loosening of the gouge verdict's margin
  (#689: half the verdict for the mesh, half for the cut). Dropped.
- An exact per-facet nearest-point measure: more cost for each facet, and
  the edge identity already gives a sound bound. Dropped.

**Cost to change later.** The split limit is one line in `fit()`. A
tighter split makes more facets: a face that runs out of facet budget keeps
its larger edges, and the import then reports them (reduced fidelity, a
refusal, not a silent pass). Issue #2713 may change the split rule in the
same function; a merge must keep the limit `tol / kind.inside()` and the
report of all kept edges.

## #2719 - STEP import: a curved face that the fit cannot measure is logged and makes the model reduced fidelity

**What was decided.** When the curved-face fit (`step_fit.rs`, #2600)
cannot read a face's mesh, it returns the reason. The reasons are: no
surface parameters, parameters that do not give the mesh's points, a facet
that is not a triangle, a point index that the mesh does not hold, too
many points, a tolerance that is not positive, and no surface in the shell.
The import then:

- keeps the kernel's facets of that face;
- logs `step: face <n> keeps the kernel's facets unmeasured (<reason>);
  the model is reduced fidelity` at warn level;
- reports the face's height as `UNMEASURED` (1000 file units). The model
  is then reduced fidelity (#864), and verify refuses its operations.

**Why.**

- The issue permits two ways: measure the kept mesh, or mark the model
  reduced fidelity. To mark it is the smaller change, and it is sound: a
  face that was not measured is never verified as exact.
- To measure the kept mesh needs a nearest-point search on the surface.
  For a mesh with no parameters there is no start point for the search, and
  truck's search on an unbounded cylinder or cone without a start point can
  fail. A failed search then needs a second fallback.
- 1000 file units is past every verdict tolerance in each unit from the
  micrometre to the kilometre, and under `model_fidelity::UNKNOWN_MM`
  (1e12 mm), so the "saved before v58" words of that sentinel do not show.

**What was considered and dropped.**

- Measure the kept mesh by a nearest-point search (see above). Dropped for
  now; it is the better result for a user, because a fine kernel mesh would
  stay at full fidelity.
- Refuse the import (an infinite chord fails at `step.rs`): too strong for
  a model that only has one face that is not measured. Dropped.
- Reuse the unknown-fidelity sentinel: its words say the project is old.
  Dropped.

**Cost to change later.** `judged()` in `step_fit.rs` is the one place.
A measure can replace the `UNMEASURED` value there, with no change to the
import. The refusal text that the user sees is the general
`TOO_COARSE` text ("re-import with a larger STEP facet budget"). A larger
budget does not help this face; the log line names the true cause.

## #2720 - Audit: each tilted operation kind refuses a gouge at generation

**Decided.** One new test binary, `crates/app/tests/tilted_gouge_kinds.rs`,
holds one probe for each kind that accepts a tilt, except Slot (its pins are
in `tilted_gouge.rs`). Each probe cuts into a correct box part (12 facets)
in a box stock on the 4th-axis mill, upright, at A 90 and at A -90, each
case in its own world. The test asserts a blocking verdict at generation
(`Warning::Gouge`, or `Warning::StockChamferGouge` for the 2D Chamfer), a
refused post ("post blocked", and "cuts past the finish surface" when
tilted) and no file written. All kinds are refused; no P1 was filed.

**Why.** Under a tilt the stock sim does not judge posed moves, so the
operation's own verdict is the only guard (#2600). A synthetic box part has
no mesh defect, so a miss would be a law gap and not an import fault.

**Probes chosen, and the ones dropped.**
- Contour: a contour of its own part cannot cut that part. Side Inside on a
  whole section, and a negative stock to leave, are refused at create. The
  probe is a second part 2 mm past the contoured part's wall, along X (the
  tilt axis), so the neighbour stands beside the wall in every pose.
- 2D Chamfer on a part source has no depth law by design (it breaks the
  part's edge). The probe is the stock-source chamfer where the part fills
  the stock (#1631).
- Face and Circular: stock source, cut below the part's skin (#1607).
- Pocket, 2D Adaptive and 2D Offset: whole part, area offset 3 mm into the
  part (#1603).
- Engrave and Trace: whole part, 7 mm deep on a 3 mm mark budget (#1595).
- 2D Adaptive is the slow kind in debug: one test for each tilted pose
  keeps each test under the 60 s budget. Its upright pose took more than
  60 s and was dropped; the keep law's own suite (#1603) pins it. A higher optimal load (0.5) was tried to
  shorten it and dropped: it ran for more than 9 minutes in debug.
- A known-fail layout (one assert in each test) was not needed, because no
  kind missed.

**Cost of a later change.** A new tilted kind adds one `Case` builder, one
arm in `set_tilt` and one test. A change of the refusal text changes the
two `contains` asserts in `convicted`.

## #2724 - A Drill or Thread op is rated by the lower of the material row and the running feed

**What was decided.**

- The feed rating of a Drill or Thread op (`operation::feed_rating::rated_feed`)
  is the lower of two values when the material in force on the op's setup
  is the document's material:
  - the feed of the tool's cutting-data row for that material;
  - the tool's running feed.
- The post clause (`feed_rating::problems`) and the seed of a new or
  retargeted Drill or Thread op (`feed_rating::seed_into`) use the same
  rating. Thus a seeded op is never refused by the check that follows it.
- When the setup's stock states a material that is not the document's
  material, the row of the stock material alone is the rating, as before.
- A running feed that is not a positive, finite number does not lower the
  rating. The row stays the rating then, as before.

**Why.**

- The running feed follows the document's material: `SetWorkMaterial` and
  `ChangeTool` set it, and `cutting_rows::follow_running` does not move a
  row that names the material. When the user lowers the running feed below
  that row, the lowered value is the limit that the user set on the tool.
  Before this change an op at the row feed posted with no refusal.
- The seed takes the same value. A seed of the row feed would make an op
  that the post check then refuses.
- The running feed is stated for the document's material. A stock with its
  own material (#2015) has its own row. The running feed of another
  material is no limit for it: a plain lower-of-two would refuse a legal
  program and seed a feed that is too low.

**Dropped.**

- Lower of the two for the check only, with the seed kept on the row: a new
  op would be seeded at a feed that its own post refuses.
- Lower of the two for every material in force: wrong for a stock that
  states its own material (see above).
- Move the named row with the running feed in `follow_running`: that edits
  the user's cutting-data table without a word, and a later material change
  could not restore the row.
- A change of the existing ops' feeds when the running feed drops: the post
  refuses by name instead, so the user decides (Prime Directive: no silent
  change of a stated value).

## #2727 - The batch gate builds each crate alone and runs its suites in parallel lanes

**What was decided.**

- `plan::batch` starts with one `--no-run` build step for each crate (`debug build: <crate> (--no-run)`),
  not one build step for all the crates.
- `Run` has a `lanes` flag. It is on for the `batch` and `release` labels. The quick gate sets it when it
  falls back to the batch plan. With the flag on, `Run::plan` uses the lane queue of `queue.rs`
  (`run_lanes`, before `run_release`).
- The batch queue takes its order from the newest `timings.tsv` of a `batch-*` or `release-*` run. The
  release queue reads `release-*` runs only, as before.
- The `heavy` tier of #2779 and a quick plan stay one step at a time.

**Why.**

- The batch tier ran about 900 steps one after the other. On a 16-core machine the load was below 3
  (#2727).
- `crates/kernel` has a dev-dependency on itself with the `truck` feature. One `cargo test --no-run` call
  with all the crates gives the shared dependencies the features of all of them. A later step with one
  `-p <crate>` resolves a smaller feature set, so cargo compiles that crate and its dependents again. One
  build call for each crate uses the same package selection as the steps of that crate. The steps then find
  their artifacts ready.
- The lane queue is the code that the release tier uses since #2057 and #2461. It keeps the guarantees of
  the gate: each step runs and has its own log, a red step fails the gate, a failed build stops the run,
  and the checkout is read before each step (VOID).
- The rules of `lanes::alone` apply without a change: the builds, the `ISOLATED` targets (wall-clock
  asserts), each ui step and clippy run alone with the whole job budget.

**Considered and dropped.**

- One parallel prebuild for all the crates (the first proposal of the issue). It is the build that batch
  had. Its feature set is not the feature set of the steps, so the steps compile again.
- One prebuild call with `--workspace` feature flags that copy each step. Cargo has no flag that selects
  the per-package feature resolution in a build of many packages.
- The crate prebuilds in parallel lanes. Two cargo calls on one `target/` wait for the same build lock, so
  they do not overlap. Each build call already uses the whole job budget (`-j`).
- `cargo nextest` (measured on the issue: 18.8 min cold). It is a new tool on each runner, it does not run
  doc-tests, and the known-fail and VOID records of the gate read libtest output. That is a larger change.
- Lanes for each quick plan. A quick plan is short, and its build steps are for each crate already. Only
  the fallback to the batch plan uses the lanes.
- The same split of the debug build of the release tier. The release plan still has one debug build for
  all the crates. This PR does not change the cut gate.

**Cost to change later.** Small. `Run::lanes` is one flag, and `plan::debug_build_crate` is one function.
To go back, give `plan::batch` the one `debug_build` step again and set the flag for `release` only.

## #2736 - 2D Adaptive at optimal load 0.5: a slow path, not a hang

**What was decided.** The cause is a slow path, not a loop that does not
end. The fix makes the door search of a routed microlift return
(`adaptive::route::door`) cheaper and keeps its result exact:

- A door from a point whose own disc holds stock or wall is refused
  before any leg is read. Every leg's capsule holds its start disc, so no
  leg longer than `ZERO_LEG` can pass there.
- The other doors read their candidate cells nearest first and stop at
  the first legal leg. The old search read every free cell nearer than
  its best so far, in raster order. The chosen cell is the same: the
  nearest legal cell, the lower index on a tie.

**Why.** Measured in release on the issue's region (the box part, area
offset 3, D6, load 0.5): the plan took 29.6 s, and 23.7 s of that was the
microlift schedule. In the schedule, 13 routed returns took 18 s, and
the door search took 16 s of it. All 22 doors that failed had a blocked
start disc, and each read the leg law on each free cell within 6 mm (the
grid is 0.05 mm). After the fix the plan takes 9.8 s with output
identical by hash on nine region and load cases.

**Considered and dropped.**

- A refusal of a large optimal load at command creation. The load law
  accepts (0, 0.5], and the plan at 0.5 completes with a legal path.
- Plan the passes one time when the app carries the stock top and plans
  again (`generate.rs`, the Adaptive2D arm). This halves the upright
  case. It is not exact without more work: the trochoid fallback reads
  `material_top`. A follow-up issue holds it.
- Cache the doors inside one `LinkLaw::find`. It saves less than the
  fix and adds state.

**Cost to change later.** Low: `door` is one private function with two
unit tests.

## #2739 - A basis-0 tilt saved after an angle edit by a #2599 build is a documented limit

**What was decided.** The load door does not find, mark or change a legacy
tilt (`basis_version: 0`) that a build with defect #2599 saved after an angle
edit. Such a file opens, generates and posts as it did in the build that saved
it. The limit and its manual repair go into the release notes. Nothing in the
code changes; `crates/app/tests/tilt_basis0_edited_file.rs` pins the facts.

**The facts** (A-only Tormach 770MX + microARC 4, a slot drawn from (10,0) to
(30,0), A0 B180):
- Basis 0 generates the slot along world Y at X0; basis 1 generates it along
  world X at Y0. The cut plane is turned 90 degrees about the tool axis.
- The post agrees with the preview. The basis-0 operation posts
  `G1 X0 Y-10` / `X0 Y-30`, the same lines and the same world toolpath as a
  basis-1 operation drawn at (0,-10)..(0,-30). Basis 1 posts `X10 Y0` /
  `X30 Y0`. The program cuts what the viewport shows; it does not cut what
  the plane coordinates mean in a new operation.
- No field tells this file from a legal one. A pre-#2133 project that held
  A0 B180 at basis 0 from the start (the shape of
  `crates/app/tests/fixtures/legacy-tilt-basis.camproj`, operation
  "Flat A180", behind `examples/first-4axis-part.nc`), opened and saved by a
  current build, is the same file byte for byte as one that a #2599 build
  saved after the edit A90 -> A0 B180. The file states no saving build and
  no edit history. The project version does not help: every build from v65
  (#2133) to v72 had the defect, v0.24.0 included, and the fixed build also
  writes v72.

**Why.** A load warning needs a test that is true for the edited file and
false for every legal old file. None exists: any test that fires on the
edited file also fires on the legal "Flat A180" project, whose output
`tilt_basis_compat` pins byte for byte. A warning on a legal file asks the
user to re-enter an angle, and that re-entry steps the basis and moves a
correct cut. The output of the edited file is not a hidden hazard: the
preview and the post read the same frame, so the user sees
the turned slot before posting.

**Manual repair** (release notes): open the operation, change Tool axis A
or B to a different value, then set it back to the wanted value. The edit
moves the tilt to the current basis (#2599), and the operation is drawn and
posted in the current plane coordinates. Check the preview before posting.

**Dropped.**
- Warn at load on each basis-0 tilt whose basis-0 frame differs from the
  basis-1 frame (A0 B180 and the other dust angles): it fires on the legal
  "Flat A180" file too, and a re-entry there moves a correct cut.
- Warn only on files of version 65..72: the legal file re-saved by any
  build in that range is the same file.
- Migrate every basis-0 tilt at load: the issue and #2599's decision forbid
  it; it changes the output of legal old projects.
- Add a "saved by build" or "basis set at" field from now on: it helps no
  file that already exists (a fixed build already steps the basis on each
  angle edit), and a new file field needs a project version step.

**Cost to change later.** If a later file field records the edit history,
a load note can use it. No code depends on this decision.

## #2740 - Select quick suites for changed fixtures and importers

**What was decided:** Add fixture readers to the existing quick selection.
Scan the source files of each integration suite, including declared helper modules.
Match quoted paths against directories that contain changed test data, fixtures, goldens, or snapshots.
Resolve paths from the repository root, crate root, and source directory.
Use the static prefix of a formatted fixture path to select readers of nested golden directories.
Use lexical path resolution so new and deleted files do not need to exist.
Keep all suites selected by the existing rules.

Changes to the app STEP/mesh importer or kernel Solidcraft and STEP import code also select three suites:

- `app:feature_edge_g1_join`
- `kernel:step_agreement`
- `kernel:machining_mesh`

**Why:** PR #2664 changed the importer and added a STEP fixture.
The quick gate omitted suites that read the model directory or use an independent importer.
The new rules select these checks before the change reaches main.
The directory scan is conservative and does not interpret test I/O.

**Considered and dropped:** Gate maps alone cannot detect a changed fixture that a suite reads.
A full batch gate for every fixture change adds work unrelated to the changed directory.
Coverage-based selection belongs to #2738 and is outside this fix.

**Cost to change later:** Update the importer path list when an importer moves or a required suite changes.
The text scan can select extra suites when they name a sibling fixture in the same directory.
A computed path without a fixture directory name can need an explicit rule or coverage-based selection.
Future selection can replace this helper while the plan tests preserve the required checks.

## #2744 - The Report door sends file names, not full paths

**Decided.** The Report door puts a shared form of the Debug info report
into the GitHub URL (`debug_info::shared_report`). That form names the
project file and the machine file by their file names only. The Debug info
panel in the application keeps the full paths (`debug_info::report`). An
unsaved project still reads `Project: unsaved`. A path with no file name
part reads `(no file name)`, never the path.

**Why.** The browser sends the URL to github.com, and the user can publish
the body without notice. A full path usually holds the user name. The file
name is enough for a triage. The machine line had the same leak (`from
<path>` of a user's own machine file), so it takes the same rule.

**Dropped.**
- A second, separate report text for the door: two sources drift. One
  builder with a "names only" switch keeps the fields the same.
- Only the exact project path replaced in the status (the first form of
  this PR): the review found other status texts with other full paths
  (`open failed: <path>`, `written to <path>`). The shared form now scrubs
  the whole report text (`report_scrub::scrub_paths`): each path-like word
  shrinks to its last component. A path starts with `/`, `\`, UNC `\\`, a drive
  (`C:\`, `C:/`), `~`, `./` or `../`, or has a `\` or two `/`. A path runs
  over spaces and marks to the last later word of the same line that has a
  separator. A mark (`,`, `;`, `)`, a quote) inside a folder name does not
  end the path (`OneDrive - Contoso, Ltd\...`). Two paths on one line merge
  into the last file name. One `/` alone (`mm/min`) is not a path. Known
  limits:
  - A path to a folder keeps the last folder name.
  - A relative path without a root keeps its first word when that word has
    no separator (`jane doe/x/y` keeps `jane`).
  - A non-path text with two `/` (for example a GPU driver text) shrinks
    to its last part.
- Changes at each status message: there are many, and a new one can leak
  again. One scrub at the report builder covers each field.
- `Path::file_name` for the file name: it reads only the separators of the
  running system, so a Windows path in a project opened on Linux came back
  whole. `report_scrub::last_component` reads `/` and `\` on every system.
- A home-directory replace (`~/...`): the directory names under the home
  can still identify the user or the customer. The file name is enough.

**Cost to change later.** Low: one switch in `debug_info::report_with`
and one scrub pass in `debug_info::shared_report`.

## #2752 - ribbon cell fill holds its whole label

**Decided:** the fill and the click target of a ribbon cell extend down to
the bottom of its label. The extension stops 2 px above the group caption
row. On a filled cell, the label ink is the on-fill ink of the fill, the
same rule that the glyph uses. The cell code moves from `painted.rs` to
`ribbon_cell.rs`, because `painted.rs` was 468 lines.

**Why:** the label sits at `glyph_px + 2` below the cell top, but the fill
was `cell_h` tall. The shipped themes set `glyph_px` to 22 and keep
`cell_h` at 30. The label then ran from 24 to about 38 px, and the fill
covered only its top half. The built-in tables overflow by about 2 px. The
light themes showed it most, because a pale fill shows its edge.

**Dropped:**

- Raise `cell_h` from the glyph and the font (`ribbon_h` and
  `ribbon_cells` follow). That moves every ribbon row and needs an estimate
  of the line height in a `const fn`. The ribbon layout already permits
  the label below `cell_h`: `ribbon_rows` pins
  `cell_h + ribbon_caption_gap >= label_bottom + 2`.
- Change the shipped theme files to a larger `cell_h`. A user theme file
  with a large glyph has the same defect.

**Cost to change later:** low. `ribbon_cell::cell_box` is the one place
that sets the box.

## #2754 - STEP: divide the boundary edges of faces curved two ways finer

**Decided:** the importer divides each shell edge before the tessellation
pass by the largest inside bound (`step_fit::Curved::inside`) of the faces
that it bounds: 1.5 for an edge of a cone, sphere or torus face, 1 for all
other edges. A cylinder face then gives the largest divisor of its edges to
all of its edges, until no edge changes (`step_fit::edge_divisors`). The
division happens once, in the shell's own edge polyline
(`CurveGuard::finer`), so the two faces of an edge get the same points and
the shell stays closed.

**Why:** #2731 made the report true: the kept height is the highest facet
edge times the inside bound (#2718). `fit` never splits a boundary edge,
and the kernel held the boundary edges only to the pass tolerance. Every
model with a cone, sphere or torus face thus read 1.5 x the tolerance
(fig8: 0.00749 mm), past `CHORD_CAP`, and became reduced fidelity. With a
boundary edge at tolerance / 1.5, the report is the tolerance again (fig8:
0.005 mm), and it stays true. The 1.5 bound and #2731 stay as they are.

The cylinder step: a cylinder meshes rim to rim. When only the rim next to
a cone is divided finer, the wall facets slant, and each slice height cuts
a different chord of the wall. The fig8 outline then had 70299 points in
place of about 2500, and the adaptive region and its order changed.

**Dropped:**
- A divisor with a margin (2.0 = 1.5 x 4/3). It gave the same chord, but
  the fig8 adaptive path then ended with an extra ring at the stock edge
  after the wall pass (`fig8_outside_containment_with_em0800_and_clearing_kinds_works`
  failed at "ends at selected face", dist 31.406). The bound with no margin
  is exact for a circle on its own surface. Where the curve's parameter
  midpoint and the face's differ, the report goes over the tolerance and
  says so; it is never under-stated.
- No cylinder step: the slanted wall facets above.
- Option A (report only the inside edges), C (raise `CHORD_CAP`), D
  (relax the test expectations) and a revert of #2731: each makes the report
  false again or weakens a fidelity guard.
- A split of the boundary edges per face, with a repair of the T-junctions
  on the neighbour face: more code, and a risk to the closed shell.

**Cost to change later:** the divisor is one function
(`edge_divisors`); a new curved kind adds one `Curved` arm. Note: the
adaptive path order on fig8 is sensitive to small mesh changes (the dropped
margin above); a later mesh change can show it again.

## #2758 - Simulate cylinder stock along X or Y

**Decision.** Use analytic vertical sections for a cylinder whose axis lies
along X or Y. Support both directions on each axis. `sim_frame` returns the
stock shape with its actual placement. `stock_grid` selects the analytic
builder.

Retain the initial top and the rounded floor in `Dexel` metadata. Count
removed volume from the initial top and limit it to the material above the
floor. `Body::on_floor` uses the same rounded floor when it builds a carried
body.

Keep the raw tool cut heights. The existing gouge verdict needs those heights
when a tool cuts through the stock. Do not clamp the cut heights to the floor.

**Reason.** A laid cylinder has a curved top and a curved underside. A top
surface alone invents material below the underside. Analytic sections retain
the round boundary without a mesh approximation. The simulation can count
real material and preserve its existing gouge checks.

**Dropped.** Do not add optional oblique stock support in this change. Keep
the named refusal for stock that stands off the machine axes. Keep the field
carry engine's cylinder refusal.

Do not build the cylinder from an inscribed polygon mesh. That mesh holds
less material at the round rim and can report removal that the tool did not
make. Do not clamp cut heights to the floor, because that can hide a gouge.

**Later cost.** More stock shapes need generic initial-top and floor metadata.
Arbitrary orientations need an oriented solid representation and checks for
its cutting, volume, carry and verdict laws.

## #2762 - The fill triangulation bridges a hole to a walk vertex first

**What was decided.** `merge_hole` in `crates/geometry/src/geo2d.rs` (the hole
bridge of `Region::triangles`) tries the walk vertices first, nearest
first. The computed ray hit on an edge is now the last candidate. Before, the
ray hit came first.

**Why.** The four red frame-cost UI tests on main came from the product
code, not from the test helper. After #2760 the fig8 mesh is finer. The 2D
Adaptive Outside region of the biggest fig8 patch has a hole whose rightmost
vertex looks onto a steep, short outer edge. The ray hit on that edge rounds
to a point 3e-16 inside the material. The ear clipper then reads that bridge
point as strictly inside the ears beside it and stops with "no ear in a
non-triangle walk", so `preview_fill` gave `None`. A small region with the same
edge gave a fill with a lost part (1814 of 2223 mm2) and no error. A bridge to
an existing vertex adds no new point. Eberly's construction ("Triangulation by
Ear Clipping", hole bridging) shows that a walk vertex with x >= r.x is
visible when the ray hits an edge. The same candidate checks (no proper
crossing, on material) still accept or refuse each bridge.

**Considered and dropped.**
- Change the test helper to pick another patch or Inside. Dropped: the
  region is legal and the product gave a wrong preview. A helper change would
  hide the defect.
- An epsilon in the ear tests (`tri_contains`, `is_left`). Dropped: it
  changes every ear decision of every fill, and a tolerance can accept a
  wrong ear.
- Remove the ray candidates. Dropped: they stay as the last resort for a case
  that no vertex can bridge.

**Cost to change later.** Local to `merge_hole`. The pin is
`region_triangles_bridge_a_hole_to_a_steep_edge` in
`crates/geometry/tests/geo2d.rs`. The triangulation is not display-only:
`motion::entry::dive_room` takes the centroid of the largest clear triangle
as the plunge or helix point. A region with a hole can thus get a different
dive point. Each candidate point is still checked with `Region::contains` and
`boundary_clears`, so a changed point stays inside the room. The motion
suites and the golden CL and G-code suites were run to show the effect.

## #2766 - The pocket region on a part drops loops of near-zero area

**What was decided.** `minus_standing` (`crates/app/src/operation/area.rs`)
removes each loop whose absolute area is below `ISLAND_AREA_MIN` (1e-4 mm2)
from the difference "enclosed area minus standing part material". The removal
is `Region::without_slivers` (`crates/geometry/src/geo2d/slivers.rs`), a new
method that only filters loops. It does not change a kept loop.

**Why.** The enclosed area and the part section share a wall. The two
tessellations of that wall disagree by about one grid unit (1 um). The
difference then has 3-point loops of 5e-9 to 1.5e-7 mm2. A clockwise loop of
that kind stands outside each boundary, and `Region::triangles` refuses the
whole region ("hole outside any boundary"). Thus the area preview of the
biggest fig8 patch had no fill with the default Containment. `minus_standing`
already uses `ISLAND_AREA_MIN` as the measure of tessellation noise for the
standing material. The same measure now applies to its result.

The region is the one that generation cuts (`selection_region`). Thus the
slivers are removed for generation too, and the outline, the fill and the
toolpath agree.

**Considered and dropped.**

- Make `Region::triangles` ignore a hole without a parent. Dropped: the
  refusal is correct for a real hole, and each other reader of the region
  would still get the slivers.
- Build the result again with `Region::new` from the kept loops. Dropped:
  the constructor normalises each loop again and can refuse a loop that
  touches itself. A filter cannot change or refuse a real loop.
- Put the filter in `Region::difference`. Dropped: that changes each boolean
  in the product and each golden that depends on one. The defect is in this
  one difference of two tessellations of the same wall.
- Stack on #2767 (the #2762 fix). Dropped: the pin is red on `upstream/main`
  and green with this change alone. The two PRs are independent.

**Cost to change later.** One call in `minus_standing` and one 20-line
module. A different threshold is one constant.

## #2776 - Explain the bottom toolbar buttons on hover

**What was decided:** Give each of the 13 buttons an original name and one
sentence that describes its action. Use an egui hover response with the
standard tooltip behavior. Honor the existing hover suppression during a
drag. Keep the existing button actions and layout.

**Why:** A user must know what an icon does before clicking it. The tooltip
explains each control without taking space from the model view.

**Considered and dropped:** Permanent text labels would need more width in
the compact toolbar. A custom popup would duplicate the standard egui
tooltip behavior and add maintenance work.

**Cost to change later:** Names and descriptions need local text edits in
the toolbar module and corresponding hover test expectations. No saved
project data or command interface depends on this wording.

## #2777 - Delete models and tools from the browser menu

**What was decided:** Add Delete to the model and tool context menus. Route
the clicked model to `DeleteByName` and the clicked tool to `DeleteTool`.
Reuse the existing menu renderer. Add a tool menu target with its name and
row so the menu stays attached to the clicked item.

**Why:** These commands already provide undo and redo. A menu action must
delete its own target even when another item is selected. The shared menu
renderer keeps the existing pointer handling and command dispatch.

The existing `DeleteTool` command permits deletion of a referenced tool.
The operation then shows `BLOCKED` and names the missing tool. Undo restores
the tool and clears that block. A regression test pins this behavior. This
change preserves that command behavior rather than adding a refusal policy
outside the menu scope.

**Considered and dropped:** Direct world changes would bypass command
history. Selection-based deletion could remove a different item. A second
menu renderer would duplicate interaction code. A new command and MCP tool
are unnecessary because the existing commands perform these actions.

**Cost to change later:** Menu labels and command dispatch remain small
changes in the shared menu. A different tool deletion policy would require
a separate command change and tests for its affected callers.

## #2789 - The STEP readers of the app read through solidcore's Part 21 parser

**Where the readers live.** The tool coordinate-system reader
(`step_csys` + `step_csys_read`), the length-unit reader (`step_units`) and
the syntax locator (`step_diag`) moved from `crates/app/src/geometry/import/`
to `camcraft-geometry`. They read text and give domain values; their `use`
lines name none of the five things that `app` holds. The app keeps:

- `step_csys.rs` as a thin wrapper: the nesting scan, the empty and UTF-8
  checks, and the map to `ImportError`. It re-exports the types, so the
  callers (`tool_body*`, MCP) did not change.
- `step_depth.rs` unchanged in code (the nesting law, see below).

The parser comes through `camcraft_kernel::p21`, a one-line re-export of
`solidcore_step::p21` in the kernel. The solidcore pin thus stays in one
manifest (`crates/kernel/Cargo.toml`). No new edge between our crates: the
app already depends on geometry, and geometry on the kernel (native only).
Dropped: a direct `solidcore-step` dependency in the app or in geometry (a
second copy of the pin to keep in step), and the kernel's own unit reader
(`solidcore_step::units`, other refusal wording than the pinned one).

The browser build (wasm32) has no solidcore. There `read_tool_csys` refuses
by name ("STEP files open in the desktop app only"), as the model import
already does, and the locator passes each record (the import refuses the
file after it).

**Entity id defined twice: refused.** ruststep's reader kept the last
definition; solidcore's parser keeps the first. A file with a duplicate id
is malformed (ISO 10303-21: an instance name is unique), and the two
readings can place the tool body at two places. The reader now refuses the
file by name ("entity #N is defined more than once ..."). No tracked
fixture has a duplicate id (scan of every tracked `.step`/`.stp`).
Dropped: keep the first (silent change of reading), and refuse only when
the duplicate is an entity the reader reaches (more code, and the same
file then reads in one place and not in another). The model import keeps
the kernel's reading (first wins, as before #2789 on its side).

**DATA sections.** A file with no DATA section is refused with the old text
"file has no DATA section": the parser reads it as a file with no
entities, so the reader asks the locator when the parser gives none.
Several DATA sections are now read as one (ISO 10303-21 edition 3 permits
them; the kernel reads them so). The old reader read only the first and
ignored the others without a word. No tracked fixture has two.

**Syntax errors.** A syntax refusal of the tool-body read now has the
locator's wording, the same as the model import ("syntax error in DATA
section: entity #N at line L cannot be parsed: ..."), else the parser's
("STEP syntax error at line L: ..."). The old text was "syntax error:"
and ruststep's message. No test asserted the old text.

**The nesting limit.** `step_depth::MAX_NESTING = 64` and `check` stay the
law in front of every read. solidcore's parser has its own private cap of
64, but it refuses only a parameter read deeper than 64: an empty
innermost `()` one level past the cap is never read as a parameter, so the
parser takes it. The scan refuses it. Pinned on both sides:
`the_parser_alone_takes_an_empty_list_one_past_its_depth_cap`
(camcraft-geometry) and `an_empty_list_one_past_the_cap_is_refused_by_the_scan`
(app). The scan's table was written against ruststep's tokenizer; re-audit
it when the solidcore pin moves.

**A length unit that no context states: refused (review of PR #2918).**
The parser maps some ISO 10303-21 short names to long names (`A2PL3D`,
`CRTPNT`, `DRCTN`, `LNGUNT`, `CNBSUN`, `LMWU`, ...) but not the short forms
of `GLOBAL_UNIT_ASSIGNED_CONTEXT` and `SI_UNIT`.
- Old reading (ruststep): it mapped no short names. A short-name tool file
  gave no placement, and the tool body fell back to its numeric placement
  ("the file names no coordinate systems").
- Reading at the reviewed head: the CIP is found, the unit context is not,
  and the reader took 1 mm per unit. An inch or metre file put the tool
  25.4 or 1000 times too small, with no refusal.
- New reading: when no context states a length unit but the file has one
  (a `LENGTH_UNIT`, an `SI_UNIT` of the metre, or a `CONVERSION_BASED_UNIT`
  over a `LENGTH_MEASURE_WITH_UNIT`), the read is refused by name ("length
  unit #N is in the file, but no GLOBAL_UNIT_ASSIGNED_CONTEXT states a
  length unit ..."). The maintainer confirmed: refuse.
- A file with no unit record at all keeps 1 mm per unit, as the ruststep
  reader did (`mm_per_unit` gave `None`, read as 1.0). Angle units alone
  (radian, degree) are no length unit.
- Pins: `a_short_name_tool_file_in_inches_or_metres_is_refused_by_name`,
  `a_short_name_tool_file_with_a_long_unit_context_reads_at_its_scale`,
  `a_long_name_tool_file_in_inches_reads_at_twenty_five_point_four`,
  `a_tool_file_with_no_unit_record_keeps_millimetres` (`step_csys_read`) and
  `a_length_unit_that_no_context_states_is_refused_by_name` (`step_units`).
- Dropped: read the short-name context and SI unit (no public source in
  the repository or the solidcore checkout states those two short names,
  and a guessed name is a guessed scale); refuse every coordinate-system
  read that finds no unit context (it would also refuse the old
  no-unit-record files, which read the same as before).
- The model import has the same gap in the kernel's `length_units`; that
  is #2919, a separate fix.

**Cost to change later.** Low. The readers are behind
`camcraft_geometry::step_csys::read_tool_csys`, `step_units::length_unit_mm`
and `step_diag::locate`; a change of reading is local to those files and
their suites (`step_csys_read`, `step_units`, `step_diag` in
`crates/geometry/tests/`).

## #2790 - Remove truck-stepio, ruststep and truck-topology; the STEP bench reads recorded truck verdicts

Part 3 of #917. It completes #917 with the scope below.

### Scope (the maintainer, 2026-11-20)

**Decided.** This PR removes three crates from the workspace:

- `truck-stepio` (the STEP reader of truck),
- `ruststep` (with its `[patch.crates-io]` git pin of #887 and the
  rationale text in the root `Cargo.toml`),
- `truck-topology` as a direct dependency (its only direct user was the
  bench's face meter, `crates/kernel/tests/step_util/truck_guard.rs`).

The non-STEP `TruckKernel` (`crates/kernel/src/truck_impl.rs`, the `truck`
feature, the tests `agreement.rs`, `blend.rs`, `heal_import.rs`) and the
truck crates that it needs stay. Their removal is #2922 (Part of #27).

**Consequence.** The first "Done means" item of #917 ("no `truck-*`
package in `Cargo.lock`") is met for the STEP crates only. Nine `truck-*`
packages stay in the lock for `TruckKernel`: `truck-base`,
`truck-derivers`, `truck-geometry`, `truck-geotrait`, `truck-meshalgo`,
`truck-modeling`, `truck-polymesh`, `truck-shapeops`, `truck-topology`.
`truck-topology` stays as a transitive package of `truck-meshalgo`,
`truck-modeling` and `truck-shapeops`; no member names it.

**Dropped.** Removing `TruckKernel` in this PR: the maintainer put it in
#2922. Keeping `ruststep` for the #1075 nesting scan: the scan only mirrors
ruststep's tokenizer rules in a table; it never calls ruststep.

### The truck side of the STEP bench: recorded readings, not deletion

**Chosen.** Each test of the bench stays. The truck side of each row is now
a recorded reading in `crates/kernel/tests/step_agreement/rows.rs`
(`Truck::Read { shells, volume, area, min, max, open_edges, chord_mm }` or
`Truck::Refused(reason)`). The live solidcore reading is judged against
the recorded truck numbers by the same rules and tolerances as before
(`verdict.rs`: `REL_TOL` 1e-3, `BOX_CHORDS` 2). Every pinned verdict
string is the same as before.

**Where the numbers come from.** The bench's own printout, one run of
`cargo test -p camcraft-kernel --test step_agreement -- --nocapture
--test-threads=1` at commit `4b694c7c7` (the head of PR #2918, before this
change), with truck-stepio 0.3.0, truck-meshalgo 0.4.0 and ruststep 0.4.0
at the #887 git pin. Volume and area are recorded at 6 decimals, the box
at full `{:?}` precision, the chord at 4 decimals. The fillet_corner and
bar_cross_holes numbers agree with `917-kernel-pcurves.md` (20651.68 and
45816.21 mm3; 121 and 1090 open edges).

**Why.** A recorded reading keeps the independent check of solidcore's
volume, area, box, solid count and unit against a second reader. A
deletion of the truck side keeps only solidcore's own numbers, and a
change of those numbers would then pass where the truck reading would
catch it.

**Dropped.** Deleting the truck side: it loses the second reader. Keeping
truck-stepio as a dev-dependency: the maintainer wants the crates out of
the workspace and the lock.

**Cost to change later.** A new STEP fixture needs a row; its truck side
can no longer be measured. Write `Truck::Refused("not recorded (added
after #2790)")` and pin the import verdict that results ("both refuse" or
"truck refuses"), or compare against a closed form in
`step_closed_form.rs`.

### The other truck users of the bench

- `step_import.rs` `corrupt_step_files_never_panic_or_hang`: the third
  column of `KNOWN_STEP_VERDICTS` (truck's verdict per corpus file) stays
  as a record and is no longer asserted. The solidcore column is asserted
  as before.
- `step_import.rs` `truck_side_refuses_a_runaway_face_and_obeys_its_cancel`
  tested the bench's own truck reader and its face meter (#1697), which
  this PR removes. It is replaced by
  `step_agreement.rs` `recorded_truck_readings_keep_their_findings`, which
  checks the recorded table: the runaway face of bspline_discontinuous is
  a recorded refusal by name, the smooth dome is a recorded mesh, the open
  meshes of fillet_corner and bar_cross_holes and the zero volume of
  twisted_flank stay recorded, every recorded mesh is finite with a sane
  box and chord, and the truck side agrees with the pinned verdict. The
  cancel half of the old test has no equivalent: the reader that it
  cancelled is gone.
- `mesh_deviation_bench.rs` (release lane, ignored): the truck column was
  printed and never asserted. It is dropped. The recorded numbers of
  `917-kernel-pcurves.md` are for two files that are not rows of this
