  bench, so they cannot replace it. The test and its solidcore asserts
  stay.

### Split of step_agreement.rs (#2800)

`step_agreement.rs` had 498 lines. It is split along its domain seam: the
pinned table with the recorded readings (`step_agreement/rows.rs`), the
verdict rules (`step_agreement/verdict.rs`) and the reading and the tests
(`step_agreement.rs`). The two modules are loaded with `#[path]`, so cargo
does not see them as test targets of their own. Each `#[test]` stays.

### `#[test]` count

`cargo test -p camcraft-kernel --features truck --tests -- --list` plus
`--lib -- --list`: the count is the same before and after (see the PR body
for the numbers). Per binary: `step_import` goes from 4 to 3 and
`step_agreement` from 22 to 23 (the moved test above).

The release tier (heavy lanes) did not run for this PR. The cut gate runs it.

## #2814 - Use available CPUs for the default gate budget

**What was decided**

- Use `std::thread::available_parallelism()` for the default job budget.
  Clamp the default to 2 through 64 jobs. Use 2 if CPU detection fails.
- Keep `CAMCRAFT_GATE_JOBS` as a positive whole-number override.
  Apply no CPU floor or cap to an explicit override.
- Use the CPU default for an empty value. For a bad value, print a
  diagnostic that names the value and the chosen fallback.
- Print the source beside the chosen budget, including in `--dry-run`.
- Keep the existing batch and release queue split. It already allows
  `max(1, budget / 2)` lanes. Builds, isolated tests, UI steps and clippy
  continue to run alone with the full budget.
- Keep `plan::J` at `"6"`. It is a marker that `budget::scale` replaces
  when a step runs. It no longer describes the default budget.
- Leave `.claude/PROCESS_VERSION` unchanged. The merging session bumps
  it after the process changes merge.

**Why**

- A fixed budget of six leaves CPUs idle on larger machines.
- The standard library reports the CPUs available to the process and
  needs no new dependency.
- The floor keeps two jobs available. The cap limits automatic concurrency.
  The override lets a runner owner choose a different limit.
- The existing queue already scales with the budget. Changing the queue
  would add work without changing the required behaviour.
- Keeping the marker avoids unrelated changes to tests of raw plans.
  The lane fixtures use an explicit budget of six to remain deterministic.

**Considered and dropped**

- A free-memory guard. Portable free-memory detection adds scope and may
  need a dependency. `CAMCRAFT_GATE_JOBS` can limit a machine with little
  memory. This optional guard can be a separate change.
- A cap on explicit overrides. Existing runner settings must continue to
  choose their own budget, including one job or more than 64 jobs.
- Changes to the lane scheduler. Its limit already follows the budget.

**Cost to change later**

- Low. CPU selection and override parsing are in `budget::from_cpu_value`.
  Unit tests supply CPU counts to check the fallback, floor and cap.
  A memory guard can extend that selection without changing the queue.

## #2818 - Viewport Display menu: display modes, Look at, graphics switches

**What was decided**

- The viewport toolbar has a 13th button, "Display", after the wireframe
  switch. It opens a menu above the toolbar with three groups: Display mode,
  Look at, Graphics.
- The four display modes are those of #2818, in the maintainer's words:
  "Shaded, with edges", "Shaded", "Wireframe", "Shaded, with hidden edges".
  #2636 names a different fourth mode ("Wireframe, see-through"). This PR
  does not add it. #2636 stays open for that mode.
- The display mode choice moved out of the Browser pane ("Solids" radios).
  #2818 says that the choice moves to the viewport menu. The Projection
  radios stay in the Browser pane and the menu has their twin.
- The draw order is one pure function, `draw_list::plan`. `View3D::render_with`
  follows the list. The lists of "Shaded, with edges" and "Wireframe" are the
  same as before.
- "Shaded" drops the wire of the model and of the stock. #2636 says that a
  mode applies to the model, the stock and the fixtures in the same way. The
  stock still shows as its translucent faces.
- "Shaded, with hidden edges" draws the cached model edge list a second time
  with the depth test reversed and 50% alpha. No new buffer and no rebuild
  on a frame.
- "Look at a face" arms one click. The click takes the first visible
  triangle under the cursor and turns the view to its normal with
  `Camera::toward`. The view does not pan or zoom. The click selects
  nothing. A miss changes nothing and says so. Each case disarms.
- The Graphics group has: "Grid" (new field `show_grid`), "Origin axes"
  (the existing `show_world_axes`), and the projection (one of two).
- The display mode and the grid switch are saved in the per-user `view.json`
  with the gizmo names (`ViewPrefs.display`, `ViewPrefs.show_grid`). The
  display mode is a string key, so `camcraft-app` does not know the UI
  type. A missing key or an unknown key loads the default.
- The wireframe switch stays. One press gives wireframe from each mode. The
  next press gives "Shaded, with edges".

**Why**

- One pure draw list lets a test read the passes of each mode without a GPU
  ("Done means" of #2818), and the renderer cannot differ from the test.
- The hidden edges reuse the cached edge list, so the frame cost rule holds
  (`crates/ui/AGENTS.md`, "Frame cost").
- Each setting draws through the one wgpu pass that the native window and
  the browser shell share. No entry needs to be hidden on wasm.
- The menu was written from the group list in the issue text. No SolidCraft
  screenshot, asset, text or look was used (`crates/ui/AGENTS.md`, "Icons
  and assets"). The Display glyph is our own three slider rows.

**Considered and dropped**

- Replace the wireframe switch with the Display button (the ribbon keeps 12
  buttons). Dropped: it removes a one-press switch that users have.
- Keep the "Solids" radios in the Browser pane with four modes. Dropped: two
  doors for one choice, and the issue says the choice moves.
- "Look at" on the current selection in place of an armed click. Dropped:
  the selection is a body, not a face, outside an open operation.
- A `DisplayMode` type in `camcraft-app`. Dropped: the app crate holds the
  document; a display mode is a UI value. The file stores a key.
- Ground shadow, ambient occlusion and the quality preset in this PR.
  Dropped: each needs a new render pass and a frame cost measurement. The
  issue permits the split. The follow-up issue is named in the PR body.
- "Look at" for a picked plane (a work plane that is not a model face). It
  is in the same follow-up issue.

**Cost to change later**

- A new display mode is one enum variant, one `draw_list::plan` branch and
  its words in `display_mode.rs`. The stored keys must stay stable.
- Moving the menu to a different anchor changes `display_menu::draw` and
  `layout_window_display_menu` only.

## #2834 - Display menu: quality preset, ground shadow, ambient occlusion, Look at a work plane

**What was decided**

- The Graphics group of the Display menu has four new rows: the presets
  "Performance" and "Quality" (one choice), and the switches "Ground shadow"
  and "Ambient occlusion". The Look at group has a new entry, "Look at a
  work plane".
- A preset is a set of values for the two switches. "Performance" sets the
  two off. "Quality" sets the two on. No preset is stored. The active preset
  is the preset whose values the switches have now. A switch changed by hand
  leaves no preset active, and the menu cannot show a preset that the view
  does not have.
- The two switches are view state: direct field writes, no command. They are
  saved in `view.json` (`ViewPrefs::ground_shadow`, `ambient_occlusion`).
  An old file without the keys loads them off. The default is off, so the
  view and the pixel snapshots of #2818 do not change.
- Ground shadow: the model bodies are projected straight down on the floor
  (`floor::floor_z`). The footprint is sampled on a grid of 96 nodes at
  most, blurred two times, and drawn as blended triangles with the shade on
  each vertex. The pass is `Pipe::GroundShadow`: after the model, before the
  translucent stock.
- Ambient occlusion: one value for each model vertex, baked on the CPU. The
  value is the share of ten short rays over the face that meet the body
  again, marched through a surface voxel grid of 48 cells. The pass is
  `Pipe::FacesOccluded`: the face shader with the value on its light. The
  values are a second vertex buffer, so the model vertex buffer and the
  other pipelines do not change.
- Caches (`shade_cache`, held on `State::frame_cache`): the shadow keys on
  the facet allocation and the shown pose of each body and on the floor
  height. The occlusion keys on the facet allocation of one body, so a moved
  body keeps its values. A switch that is off builds nothing. Each cache has
  a counter test.
- Wireframe draws no lit face and no shadow. The two switches are disabled
  there, keep their values, and their tooltip says why.
- No entry is hidden on wasm. The two passes are vertex buffers and alpha
  blending in the one wgpu pass that the two shells share. They use no
  texture and no second render target.
- "Look at a work plane" arms one click on an origin axis in the view. The
  view turns to face the plane that the axis is normal to: Z gives XY, X
  gives YZ, Y gives ZX. A click on the origin point gives the XY plane. The
  origins are the work offsets (WCS) and the world origin. The reversed axes
  of a WCS (#1720) are applied. The view does not pan or zoom. A miss
  changes nothing and says so.
- `world_verts`, `world_verts_by` and the new `model_src` moved from
  `egui_app/world.rs` to `egui_app/world_verts.rs`. `world.rs` was at 392
  lines and the scene shade data put it past 400.

**Why**

- The issue asks for data that is calculated one time for each geometry
  change and cached. Baked vertex values and a baked shadow mesh are that
  data. A still frame adds one blended draw and one extra vertex attribute.
- The issue asks that the wasm build uses the same settings. Plain vertex
  buffers work on each backend, so the menu says nothing false there.
- The light of the shadow is at the zenith. The first version used the key
  light of the face shader. That light is behind the camera in the house
  view, so the shadow was behind the model and nobody saw it. The straight
  shadow shows as a soft rim from each view direction.
- A derived preset has no state that can disagree with the switches.

**Considered and dropped**

- Screen-space ambient occlusion (a depth texture and a second pass). It
  costs work on each frame, it needs a sampled depth target, and it is not
  "data calculated one time for each geometry change".
- A 3D occupancy texture sampled in the fragment shader. It gives a value
  for each pixel, but it needs a texture binding in the shared pass and one
  volume for all bodies in world space, built again on each pose change.
- A shadow map (a depth pass from the light). It needs a second render
  target and a sampled depth texture. The projected mesh needs neither.
- Occlusion between bodies (a part in a vise). The values are for one body
  alone, so that a moved body keeps them.
- A stored preset name in `view.json`. See "Why".
- Construction planes. The document has no construction plane entity. The
  world origin planes and the WCS planes are the reference planes that
  exist. A construction plane type can add its axes to `axis_marks` later.

**Limits**

- The occlusion is a value for each vertex. On a large flat triangle the
  shade is a linear ramp between its corners, so a coarse CAD face shows a
  soft diagonal ramp and not a narrow dark line in the corner. A fine mesh
  shows the corner well.
- The first frame after "Ambient occlusion" goes on bakes each body on the
  UI thread. The cost grows with the triangle count. It was not measured on
  a large model.
- The shadow is black with 60% alpha at most. It is faint on the dark
  viewport ground and strong on a light ground.
- The shadow of the simulation tool body is not drawn: the tool moves on
  each playback frame and would build the shadow again on each frame.

**Cost to change later**

- The two passes are behind `Pipe::FacesOccluded` and `Pipe::GroundShadow`
  and the `Shade` data. A different occlusion source fills the same
  `Shade::occlusion` values or replaces the one pipeline. The preset list is
  `QualityPreset::ALL`; a new switch adds a field to `Effects`.

**Merge with #2958 (MSAA and wide lines)**

- Chosen: the two shade pipelines take the sample count of the viewport's
  3D pass, and `View3D::set_samples` builds them again with the other
  pipelines (`ShadePass::rebuild`).
- Why: the two passes have no target of their own. They draw inside the
  one 3D pass, into its colour target (the multisample target when MSAA is
  on) and its depth target. A pipeline whose sample count differs from the
  pass is a wgpu validation error at run time.
- Dropped: moving the two pipelines into `viewport::pipes::Pipes`. The
  shade pipelines need a second vertex buffer layout and their own buffers.
  `ShadePass` keeps them together with the count passed in.
- The Display menu order is: projection, "Line width", "Anti-aliasing"
  (#2958), then a separator and the quality rows of #2834.

## #2840 - pin golden, machine, STEP and workflow fixtures to LF in .gitattributes

- **Chosen:** pin all test fixtures, golden post outputs, machine definitions, STEP/STP models, agent and skill definitions, and GitHub workflows to LF line endings (`text eol=lf`) in `.gitattributes`.
  - Why: Git for Windows checks out text files with CRLF by default (`core.autocrlf=true`). Test suites comparing post programs byte-for-byte (such as `explain_fanuc_family`), parsing machine definitions (such as `wire-iso-fixture.mch`), importing STEP models (`import_step_curve_guard`), and xtask tests parsing skill markdown or workflow concurrency blocks expect and require LF line endings (`\n`).
  - Dropped: modifying individual tests to accept CRLF. Normalizing line endings at the repository boundary via `.gitattributes` guarantees deterministic behavior across platforms without weakening byte-exact golden test assertions.
- **Pinning tests:**
  - `xtask/tests/example_line_endings.rs`: added `all_golden_and_fixture_files_have_eol_lf` asserting that `git check-attr eol` reports `lf` across all golden, recorded, machine, STEP, skill, and workflow directories.
  - `xtask/tests/example_line_endings.rs`: added `golden_and_fixture_files_keep_lf_with_autocrlf` asserting that checked-out files maintain LF line endings without carriage returns under `core.autocrlf=true`.
  - Verified affected suites pass cleanly: `explain_fanuc_family`, `wire_taper_angle`, `import_step_curve_guard`, and `post_merge_concurrency`.

## #2844 - a runaway strip face is divided over its boundary nodes

**What was decided.** The kernel seam (`machining_mesh::planned`) calls
`mesh_redivide::redivide` on each plan, before the measure. A face that
the planner gave a runaway count gets a second division: the Delaunay
fill of its boundary loop, over its shared edge nodes only, with no node
inside. The seam keeps that division only when
`mesh_deviation::measure_within` proves it inside the tolerance. If not,
the face keeps the planner's triangles. The measure of the whole plan
runs after that, as before, so the guarantee of a machining mesh does not
change. A kept division is a note in the mesh report.

Readings on the four-turn thread flank at 5e-3 mm (debug):

| Plan | Planner | Boundary division | Measured |
|---|---|---|---|
| chord 5e-3 mm | 274192 triangles | 926 triangles | 7.3e-3 mm, not kept |
| chord 2.5e-3 mm (replan) | 391338 triangles | 1150 triangles | 3.8e-3 mm, kept |

The test time went from 68 s to 35 s. The two planner runs and the
measure of the first plan remain.

**Why.** This is option 3 of the issue comment of 2026-11-20. Options 1
and 2 are changes in `NeoTech/solidcore` and a move of the pin. Option 3
needs only the public fields of `TessPlan` and `FacePlan`. The shared
edge nodes (`fixed`) stay bit for bit, so the neighbouring faces meet
the face as before.

**Decisions inside it.**

- *Which faces.* Only a face with 10 000 planned triangles or more
  (`REDIVIDE_MIN_TRIANGLES`) and 16 or more for each boundary node
  (`REDIVIDE_RATIO`). The two numbers are our judgement, not measured
  optima. They keep the meshes of ordinary models as they are: no golden
  moves. Dropped: a division of each face that passes the measure. It
  would change the facet counts of many models for a small gain.
- *No node inside.* A face that needs inside nodes (a wide twisted or
  bulged patch) fails the measure and keeps the planner's triangles
  (`machining_mesh_redivide.rs` pins this). Dropped: rows of inside nodes
  by the curvature of each direction. That is the anisotropic planner of
  option 1, and it belongs in solidcore-tess.
- *One loop only.* A face with a hole, a pole, a triangle turned over in
  (u, v) (a period), a pinched boundary, or a boundary node that is not a
  shared one is not divided.
- *Own fill, not `solidcore_tess::triangulate_planar`.* The public
  triangulator cuts across a boundary run that is exactly collinear in
  (u, v) (the straight run-out trims of the flank), so its triangles do
  not keep the boundary. The fill here is ear clipping and Lawson flips
  (`mesh_redivide_fill.rs`), bounded at 8192 vertices because ear
  clipping is quadratic. The seam checks that the fill has the planner's
  boundary sides and one sense for each triangle. With these two facts
  the triangles cover the face one time.
- *The fill's plane.* (u, v) scaled by the mean lengths of the two
  partial derivatives at the boundary nodes, so that "near" in the plane
  is near on the surface.

**Not done.** The replan at half the chord remains (the first plan's
boundary division measures 7.3e-3 mm against 5e-3 mm, mostly the chords of
the edges themselves). The planner still makes its isotropic division
before the seam replaces it, so the import time of a threaded part falls
by about half, not by the factor of the facet count. The speed item of
#2780 stays open for that.

**Cost to change later.** Small. When solidcore-tess plans a strip
anisotropically, the planner's count falls under the two thresholds and
`redivide` does nothing. Then the two modules and the one call can go.

## #2845 - Keep contact faces with their closed solids

**Chosen.** Link fragments at a four-use edge only when one complete
matching remains. Each pair has opposite edge directions. Facets on the
same ray cannot pair because they enclose no material there. Keep an
existing two-use body together. Check every shared edge again after all
links. Keep the slicer's closure and outward-volume checks, and the winding
check's existing fault classifications.

**Why.** A contact face can have no plain boundary edge. Plain-edge links
then leave its facets apart from the rest of its solid. A unique matching
can restore that link without choosing an arbitrary angular neighbour.
The later checks must still prove that the proposed links form valid
bodies. Larger or ambiguous fragment arrangements retain their refusal.

The feature graph keeps all incident facets until it checks the contact.
It then emits one facet pair for each valid solid. This gives face patches
and edge chains the same contact rule as slicing and winding. Store the
first two uses inline. Allocate extra storage only when an edge needs it.

One model can hold two closed solids. The former `stitch_cross` refusal
fixture contains two complete outward cubes with one shared face. It has
no extra bridge or other self-intersection. The test now requires the same
cut and verification result as the single-block reference. It also requires
that no depth level is skipped. This follows the expected-change rule.
The actual non-manifold refusal cases keep their assertions.

This branch started from the open PR #2904 at `853522f2e`. That prerequisite
merged as `bac4a96c` while this work was in progress.

**Dropped.** Do not pair arbitrary angular neighbours. Coincident walls
can make that choice ambiguous. Do not rely only on STEP solid ranges:
the facet-only winding and slicing APIs must handle the same contact.
Do not add a `SmallVec` dependency for two inline uses.

**Cost to change later.** Support for more fragmented edge uses needs a
unique matching rule and safety cases for closure, winding, fins and
line-only contact. Keep the final edge and volume checks. A larger inline
capacity can change locally without a project-file or public type change.

## #2845 - Refresh the Linux bore pin after the importer change

**Chosen.** Pin the Linux bore path to 3158 moves, 3130 planar feeds and
1141 arcs. Require the imported mesh to contain 6228 facets. Require all
four cutting levels: Z 0, 5, 10 and 15. Keep the clean verification,
fallback and planning-budget checks. Reject adjacent path counts in a
separate exact-pin test.

**Why.** PR #2904 replaced the 952-facet truck mesh with the solidcore
mesh at the same chord cap. Decision #917 records this mesh change. The
new mesh changes the cutting regions and fitted arcs. The fixture and
HSM planner did not change. The old Linux counts described the truck
mesh, while the review measured the solidcore path.

**Dropped.** Do not widen the count range or disable the heavy pin. Do
not weaken the arc proof or verification checks to match an old count.
Rejected arc fits retain their safe chords.

**Cost to change later.** A future mesh or planner change must explain
and measure the new counts. The mesh, cutting levels and verification
checks must still agree with that measurement.

## #2848 - rotary operations and a face selection

**What was decided**

- Rotary Parallel keeps its cut over the picked faces. The kernel plans the
  raster on the whole model, as before. Then it keeps each cut point where the
  line from the axis out through the ball centre meets a picked facet (the
  radial shadow of the picks). The radial relink builds the links between the
  kept pieces, as it does for the whole raster.
- The axis fit, the tangency law, the gouge laws and the verify read every
  facet of the picked model. Only the cut is bounded.
- A pick resolves to facet indices of its model, not to points. The indices
  name the same facets after the WCS yaw (#760) turns the material.
- A selection that Rotary Parallel cannot use refuses by name:
  - a pick that is not a face (an edge chain, a vertex);
  - picks on two models;
  - a face that does not look away from the axis (an end face, a bore wall);
  - picks that form two or more groups that do not touch;
  - picks that no pass lies over.
- Rotary Contour and Rotary Offset refuse a face selection by name. Before,
  they cut the whole model without a message.
- The generation stamp of a rotary operation with a selection gets a version
  mark. A path that was cached under the old reading (the whole model) is
  stale until the operation is generated again.

**Why**

- The clip plans nothing new. A kept point is a point that the whole-model
  raster already certified. The pattern is the one `rotary_ends::clip` uses
  for a held end (#2343), and `finish_clip` uses for the 3-axis finish.
- The maintainer's triage comment names the defect: the operation ignores the
  selection without a message, and an unusable selection must refuse.
- The issue's "Done means" list asks for a refusal of disconnected picks. The
  kernel can link two groups (a mutation run proved it), but the list is the
  contract. This is my reading of "disconnected"; it can be relaxed later.
- "Non-cylindrical" in the issue is read as "a face that a radial tool cannot
  stand over". A cone or a sculpted face of the turned surface is legal. This
  is my reading, not the reporter's words.

**Considered and dropped**

- Face containment for Rotary Contour. Its rings need a new link between the
  kept pieces: the waterline's plunge column is certified per ring entry, and
  the kind has no clearance radius to retract to. That is new safety logic.
  Follow-up: #2851.
- Face containment for Rotary Offset. A clip is wrong for a roughing ladder:
  a kept piece would plunge into stock that the dropped passes did not clear.
  The correct form is a picked region in wrap space, with the seam law. That
  is new algorithm work (`effort:max`). Follow-up: #2852.
- Generating on the picked facets only. An open mesh has no axis and no
  solid to check against, and the tool would gouge the faces next to it.
- An MCP pick-time door for the rotary refusals. Generation refuses by name
  already; the door is polish.
- A change to the preview region. It stays the model's shadow.

**Cost to change later**

- Low. The clip is one module (`multiaxis::rotary_pick`) and one call in
  `rotary_parallel_over`. The refusals are in `operation::rotary_picks`. To
  permit separate groups, remove the `groups` check. A rotary kind that learns
  to keep to picks replaces its `not_yet` refusal.

## #2849 - The corner check reads a cusp loop that crosses itself by the even-odd rule

**What was decided.** `connected_pieces` in
`crates/motion/src/machining2d/unreached.rs` builds the fill of each outer
loop with `Region::from_slices`, not `Region::new`. A loop that crosses
itself is read as its even-odd lobes. The corner check then runs and applies
its usual noise filters (`PIECE_AREA_MIN`, `SLIVER_HALF_WIDTH`,
`CORNER_HALF_WIDTH`).

**Why.** The loops that `connected_pieces` reads are the output of a
boolean (`piece.difference(&swept)`), not sketch input. A bore drawn as
chords less its own swept area leaves a cusp a few microns wide at each
chord vertex. On the micron lattice, the boolean can return such a cusp as
one loop that crosses itself. `Region::new` refuses that loop, so the whole
corner check stopped with the note "the check for corners of the stock
tighter than the tool did not run (invalid geometry: loop crosses itself)".
The refusal in `Region::new` is for ambiguous user geometry. It has no
purpose for a noise cusp that the next filter drops. A loop that does not
cross itself gives the same region from the two constructors.

The defect does not need the solidcore importer. A synthetic 25 mm bore
shows it on `main`: in a sweep of 24 to 400 chords, 9 tool sizes and 4
phases, 4726 of 13572 cases stopped with the error. With the fix, no case
stops.

**Scope: partial.** The issue names three toolpath tests. The owner's
diagnosis on the issue says that each has its own cause (the pass start
choice, `axis_reseat`, the ring order) and that this fix does not change
them. Their `known-fail #2849` markers are on the unpushed PR B of #917.
This PR therefore ends with `Refs #2849`, not `Fixes #2849`.

**Merge with main.** `main` got the same code fix in `bc5daa32d`
(`outer_fills`, pinned by a hand-made bow-tie loop). The refresh takes
main's code. This PR now adds only the chord-bore pin: it reads the real
path (a bore less its swept area) through `unreached_corners` and
`unreached_corner_note`, where main's pin reads `outer_fills` alone.

**Considered and dropped.**
- Relax `Region::new` itself. Dropped: the refusal protects sketch input
  (Prime Directive), and many callers rely on it.
- Skip a loop that fails `Region::new`. Dropped: that hides a loop without
  a look at its size. The even-odd reading keeps the area and lets the
  existing filters decide.
- Raise `PIECE_AREA_MIN` above the cusp area. Dropped: the filter runs
  after the constructor, and a threshold tuned to one mesh breaks with the
  next mesh.
- Change the planners for tests 1 to 3 (start choice, reseat tolerance,
  ring order). Dropped here: they cannot fail on `main`, and other pins and
  goldens read that behaviour.

- Close this PR as superseded. Dropped for now: the chord-bore pin covers
  the full corner check, not only the fill constructor. The re-review
  decides if that coverage is worth the test.

**Cost to change later.** One line. The pin
`a_chord_cusp_that_crosses_itself_does_not_stop_the_corner_check` fails if
the refusal comes back.

## #2854 - Describe the shipped features and their limits in the guide

**What was decided.** Update the existing guide pages for the features
listed in #2854. Describe the current merged implementation and its tests.
Explain the holder-reference, DXF-profile and protected-operation format
barriers beside their workflows. Keep the AI section to a short connection
pointer because #1949 owns the full guide.

**Why.** The next documentation build must explain the controls that ship.
Some merged slices store data without making it available for machining:
DXF chain generation still refuses, and plasma recipes do not yet change
operation parameters or output. The guide states these limits explicitly.
It also follows current Report code, whose issue buttons request the
clipboard screenshot; an older PR body described a separate copy button.

**Considered and dropped.** A separate release feature page would duplicate
the guide and split instructions between pages. A complete AI guide would
overlap #1949. New screenshots are unnecessary for these text changes.
No executable behavior, output golden, dependency or process file changes.

**Cost to change later.** Low. These are guide text and coverage tests.
The overlap with #2799 concerns the same files but different sections;
the second PR to merge refreshes its branch.

## #2855 - Catalog metadata and operation example links

**Decided.** Each catalog case has a required `case.toml`. `kinds` uses the
canonical display names read from the bounded `KindInfo::ALL` source table.
`machine` and `expect` are required descriptive strings, not executable checks.
The flat TOML format accepts quoted strings and arrays, comments and multiline
arrays. It refuses escapes, unsupported syntax, duplicate or empty values,
unknown fields and unknown kinds.

Every known operation-kind heading gets a deterministic marked Example cases
block, including a placeholder when no case exists. Turning headings use an
explicit alias map where their prose titles differ from registry names. Links
point to the canonical GitHub source folder for each case. The generator
preserves surrounding prose and refuses malformed blocks or missing headings
before writing partial guide updates.

Metadata and links are checked across the whole catalog even with `--case`.
The default and rebuild commands regenerate the lists. Screenshot-only and
PDF-only commands leave the guide unchanged. `--check` validates the metadata
and links without writing, before building the CLI. Existing NC rebuilding and
byte-for-byte parity checks stay unchanged.

**Why.** A separate metadata file keeps case READMEs readable and gives the
catalog one source for guide links. Reading the registry source avoids a second
kind list and an app dependency in the small process tool. Early diagnostics
name metadata and link problems before an expensive CLI build. Validating all
links avoids making a filtered case command silently accept broken guide pages.

**Considered and dropped.** Embedding machine-readable fields in READMEs would
mix prose with tooling input. A new app dependency or TOML dependency would
change Cargo dependencies for a small flat schema. A separate links-only CLI
would add another workflow when the existing catalog commands can generate and
check the lists. Treating `machine` or `expect` as executable assertions would
duplicate the build script and its verification checks.

**Cost to change later.** The metadata reader, guide generator and turning alias
map are isolated in xtask. Supporting richer TOML later requires extending or
replacing the reader and its tests; existing flat metadata remains valid.
Changing link destinations requires regenerating the marked guide blocks.

## #2857 - Catalog case results

**Decided:** Give each of the five catalog cases separate `regenerates`
and `rebuilds` tests. The ten tests have independent libtest results.
A discovery test requires both tests for each catalog directory and keeps
the required seed case. Move the shared assertions to a support module
to keep each file below about 400 lines. Keep the existing golden assertions.

Each case has a 60-second wall clock budget. Use the worker and channel
pattern from `import_step_guard`. Keep the original panic when a case fails.
Write each case's elapsed time directly to stderr on success and failure.
The timeout bounds the test result; it cannot cancel the worker thread.
Each rebuild removes only its own temporary case directory, so parallel
tests cannot remove another case's files.

**Why:** A failure must name its case without hiding another case's failure.
All ten case workflows stay below the budget in debug mode. Keep them in
the default lane. A future slow case must use a smaller model or move to
`app heavy: example_catalog`, with that lane in its ignore reason.

**Dropped:** Keep no aggregate loop, because it gives one result and adds
all case times. Add no test harness dependency, because std and libtest
provide the required results. Move no current case to the heavy lane,
because each case is below 60 seconds.

**Cost to change later:** Add two test wrappers for each new catalog case.
The discovery test reports a missing wrapper. A different timeout or
cancellation mechanism changes the shared support module.

## #2858 - Publish catalog images for each operation

**What was decided:** Capture one model image without toolpaths and one image for each operation.
Use selection commands to show one operation's toolpath at a time.
Keep the same camera for all images of a case.
Use `0-blank.png` for the model image.
Use the document order and an operation name with sanitized characters for each operation filename.
Collect every PNG in each case's output directory.
Commit the images to `catalog-screenshots` and push that branch to `origin` without force.
Link the published seed images from its README and the catalog documentation.

**Why:** Separate images let a reader inspect each operation without other toolpaths covering it.
Stable paths keep the README links valid when the command runs again without a source change.
An images-only branch keeps PNG files outside the product tree.
The user forbids pushing to `upstream`, so publication uses the fork's `origin` remote.
A normal push refuses a conflicting remote history and reports the error.

**Considered and dropped:** A combined toolpath image does not show each operation separately.
PNG files in the product tree violate the requested image storage rule.
Pushing to `upstream` violates the user's instruction.
An automatic force push could remove remote commits.
Reusing the review screenshots branch would mix catalog images with review evidence.

**Cost to change later:** A different path scheme requires updates to the renderer, collection tests, and README links.
Moving publication to another remote requires a deliberate remote choice and updated image links.

## #2859 - Example case 2d/contour-tabs: one plate, one 2D Contour

**What was decided.** The case `examples/catalog/2d/contour-tabs` is a
90 x 50 x 6 mm plate with four 10 mm corner chamfers, in a 120 x 80 x 6 mm
sheet. One 2D Contour cuts the outside with a 6 mm flat end mill. The lead-in
is a 3 mm arc. The lead-out is a 4 mm line. There are four tabs, 8 mm wide
and 2 mm high. The stepdown is 2 mm, so the levels are Z4, Z2 and Z0.

**Why.**

- One operation keeps the program short (104 lines). A reader sees each lead
  move and each tab lift without a search.
- The outline has only straight edges. Each `G03` block is then a lead-in,
  and each `G02` block is a corner roll. The pinning test counts them.
- An arc lead-in and a linear lead-out are two different shapes. The program
  shows that the two parameters are independent.
- The sheet is as thick as the plate. The contour goes to the sheet bottom,
  and the tabs are the only material that holds the plate. This is the usual
  cut-out job.
- The stepdown equals the tab height. The tab top (Z2) is a level of the
  stepdown ladder, and no extra level is added (#2579).
- The model is a prism that the generator script writes. No outside geometry
  is used (Clean-Room Protocol).

**Considered and dropped.**

- A plate with holes and a Drill operation. The seed case `2d/first-part`
  shows Drill. A second operation hides the lead moves and the tab lifts.
- A rectangle. The chamfers give corners that are not 90 degrees and make
  the geometry original for this case.
- A stock top above the plate top with a Face operation. It adds levels and
  an operation that this case does not show.
- A lead-in written as `lead: { arc: { radius: 3.0 } }`. `add_operation`
  refuses it: the patch merges with the seeded linear lead, and the result
  has two shapes. The script writes `linear: null` with the arc. The refusal
  message does not name the cause; #2876 is the bug for it.

**Cost to change later.** Small. Change `build.camscript`, run
`cargo xtask catalog --case 2d/contour-tabs`, and update the counts in the
test `contour_tabs_case_posts_the_lead_moves_and_the_tab_lifts`.

**Pinned by.** `crates/app/tests/example_catalog.rs`:
`contour_tabs_case_posts_the_lead_moves_and_the_tab_lifts`, and the two
catalog tests that read each case.

**Review fix (PR #2877).** Keep the imported mesh embedded, and remove its
source link in both the committed project and `build.camscript`. The UI
checks a relative source path from the process directory. The example must
open when that directory differs from the case directory. The seed project
also embeds its mesh without a source link. An absolute path would tie the
example to one checkout. A product path-resolution change is outside this
example fix. The two app catalog tests pin the embedded mesh and the absent
link in the committed and rebuilt projects. The existing UI catalog test
checks that the committed project opens.

## #2860 - Adaptive roughing and Pocket finishing

**What was decided:** Add an original U-shaped pocket with one open end.
Use 2D Adaptive before 2D Pocket through the existing commands.
Adaptive leaves a nominal 0.5 mm wall allowance and stops 0.5 mm above the floor.
Pocket uses zero wall allowance and reaches the model floor.
Keep the case-specific pin in a separate test file.

**Why:** The case demonstrates roughing followed by finishing with explicit stock allowances.
The existing commands can generate, verify, save, and post the example.
A separate test avoids extending the shared catalog test beyond its existing 431 lines and avoids overlaps with open PRs.

**Considered and dropped:** A closed pocket would not meet the open-pocket requirement.
Rest machining is not needed to demonstrate this sequence.
Algorithm changes are not needed because the existing APIs provide the required behavior.
Extending the shared catalog test would increase its length and create overlap with other work.

**Verification scope:** Verification checks for gouges, rather than complete stock removal.
The cutter leaves material in the model's sharp inside corners.
Adaptive also reports up to 0.71 mm of extra corner scallop beyond the nominal wall allowance.
The case README states these limits.

**Cost to change later:** Regenerate the mesh, project, and NC program.
Update the pinning test and the README to match the new geometry or allowances.

## #2861 - Example case 2d/slots: one block, a Slot and a Trochoidal slot

**What was decided.** The case `examples/catalog/2d/slots` is a
100 x 60 x 12 mm block with two closed slots along X. Each slot is 10 mm
wide, 6 mm deep and 60 mm long. A Slot cuts the slot at `Y15`. A Trochoidal
slot cuts the slot at `Y-15`. The two operations use the same 6 mm flat end
mill, the same width and the same floor (`Z6`).

- Slot: stepover 2 mm, stepdown 3 mm, `F600`. The levels are `Z9` and `Z6`.
- Trochoidal slot: full depth in one level, `max_engagement` 60 degrees,
  `step` 0.8 mm, microlift return of 0.3 mm, `F1200`.

**Why.**

- One part with the two slots lets a reader compare the two programs in one
  file. Only the operation kind and its cutting data are different.
- A 10 mm slot with a 6 mm tool leaves 2 mm of room on each side. The Slot
  needs more than one row, and the Trochoidal slot has room for its loops.
- Each operation uses the cutting data that is usual for it. The Slot cuts
  with the full tool diameter, so it takes two levels at a low feed. The
  Trochoidal slot keeps a small contact angle, so it takes the full depth at
  two times the feed. The README table shows the result: 19 motion blocks
  against 803, and 0.60 min against 1.28 min of feed moves.
- The slots are closed and are inside the block. The gouge check then judges
  each tool path against real walls on all sides.
- The model is a mesh that the generator script writes. No outside geometry
  is used (Clean-Room Protocol). The script checks that the mesh is
  watertight and that the top area is correct.
- The round ends of the model have 64 chords for each half circle. The
  chords are inside the true circle by less than 0.002 mm. `verify` is ok
  with the true 10 mm width.

**Found during the work.** The Slot leaves up to 0.86 mm in its round ends,
and `verify` is ok. The rows touch a round end only at their end points.
#2906 is the bug. The README names it under "What to look at". The case
keeps the 2 mm stepover, because it shows the behaviour clearly. A fix for
#2906 changes `slots.nc`: rebuild the case with the fix.

**Merge with main: the case tests are in the heavy lane.** Main now has
one test module for each case (`catalog_<family>_<case>`), with a 60 s
budget for each test. The module `catalog_2d_slots` takes about 40 s for
each test in debug when it runs alone. In the parallel suite, it went over
its budget. It also pushed `turning/cone-thread` over its budget. The two
tests of `catalog_2d_slots` are `#[ignore]`d with a heavy-lane reason. The
budget message tells the author to do this. `cargo xtask gate heavy` runs
them in release. The default suite keeps
`slots_case_posts_a_slot_and_a_trochoidal_slot_to_the_same_floor`, which
reads the committed program. Dropped: a smaller model (it changes the
committed program), and a larger budget (it changes a rule of main).

**Considered and dropped.**

- Two parts or two cases, one for each operation. The comparison needs the
  two programs side by side.
- Slots open at the two ends of the block. The end points are then outside
  the block. This was not tried: a closed slot is the plain job, and its
  round ends show the difference between the two operations.
- The same stepdown and feed for the two operations. A Trochoidal slot at a
  3 mm depth and `F600` does not show why a user selects it.
- A smaller stepover for the Slot to make the leftover in the round ends
  small. The leftover does not go to zero, and the example would hide #2906.
- A check of the embedded mesh for this case in the two catalog tests. The
  check for `2d/contour-tabs` pins a review fix of that case. The script of
  this case removes the model link in the same way.

**Cost to change later.** Small. Change `build.camscript`, run
`cargo xtask catalog --case 2d/slots`, and update the test
`slots_case_posts_a_slot_and_a_trochoidal_slot_to_the_same_floor` and the
README table.

**Pinned by.** `crates/app/tests/example_catalog.rs`:
`slots_case_posts_a_slot_and_a_trochoidal_slot_to_the_same_floor`, and the
two catalog tests that read each case.

## #2862 - Hole-work catalog case

**What was decided.** Add one original 90 x 90 x 20 mm plate with four
drill holes on a 60 mm bolt circle. Use a separate hole for Bore, Circular
and Thread. Add a tap-drill operation before the internal M8 x 1.25 thread.
Use the existing command scripts, catalog discovery and default Fanuc mill
post. Keep the model embedded in the saved project.

**Why.** One small case makes the four operation types easy to compare.
The posted program shows G81 cycles, hole milling arcs and the thread
helix. The prior tap drill gives the thread mill an open hole. An embedded
mesh lets the project open without a path relative to the script directory.
The multi-form thread mill tip follows the helix from Z8 to Z9.875. Its
axial cutting teeth cover the intended 12 mm thread length.

**Model and tool choices.** The original generator tiles annular cells and
checks their edge pairs. It uses 96 flats around each hole. The drill,
bore and circular envelopes have 0.2 mm radial clearance. The thread hole
keeps the M8 x 1.25 minor radius, 3.3235 mm, with its floor at Z4.
The script extends the drill and end-mill flutes to 25 mm. A custom
6.6 mm tap drill starts from the catalog drill. No holder is modelled.

**What was dropped.** Do not use automatic drilling cycle selection.
An explicit Drill cycle makes G81 stable when the hole dimensions change.
Do not use a 10 mm radius Circular cut with several radial passes in this
case. Verification refused that cut because of rapids through stock.
Helical entry also produced crossing warnings. Use a 5 mm radius cut with
a plunge entry; it needs one radial pass and verifies without warnings.
The separate Circular defect is #2898. It is linked from #2862 and the
catalog umbrella #2392.

**Limits.** The through-drill point reaches Z-2.803 and the bore reaches
Z-1. These moves require clearance below the plate. The report names the
break-through. The case has no fixture or spoil board. No machine or
control simulator has run the program. The model represents the thread
minor hole, not its teeth.

**Cost to change later.** A different hole size, tool, entry or cycle
requires a script change and a rebuild of the committed project and NC
program. A change to the model also requires a generator change. Update
the case pin and README when their stated dimensions or output change.

## #2864 - Outside groove and part-off catalog case

**What was decided:** Add one original revolved bar with a 6 mm outside groove and a separate part-off plane.

## #2876 - Name retained shape keys in parameter patch refusals

**What was decided.** Keep RFC 7386 merge-patch behavior for operation
parameters. When the parser requires a single map key, add context for
former single-key objects that now contain multiple keys. Keep the original
parser error. Give dotted field paths, including `links.approach.lead_out`,
and the merged keys. Tell the caller to remove unwanted keys with `null`.
Document this removal for both `add_operation` and `edit_operation`.

**Why.** The issue accepts a refusal that names the field and conflicting
shapes. The shared parser serves both tools and nested parameters. This
change preserves parameter values, command validation and undo history. It
requires no dependency or toolpath behavior change. Context describes merged
objects because a single-key object is not necessarily an enum.

**Considered and dropped.** Automatic shape replacement would change merge
semantics. A Lead-only check would miss other enums and nested fields. A new
parser dependency would expand this small diagnostic fix.

**Cost to change later.** Exact typed error paths may require a parser that
uses the parameter schema. Keep validation before command execution and
preserve history when a patch is refused.

**Validation.** Three pins cover creation, editing, nested paths, explicit
removal and unchanged state after refusal. All three fail with the original
parser and pass with the fix. The quick gate passes 17 steps. Clippy passes
for `camcraft-app`.

## #2878 - Fanuc lathe G76 free-air start law (`start_in_air` on `ThreadCycle` and `AIR 1` in `THREAD`)

- **What was decided**:
  1. Carry `start_in_air: bool` on `cl::ThreadCycle`, serialize it as optional `AIR 1` on the intermediate `THREAD` record (absent = `false`) and `#[serde(default, skip_serializing_if = "is_false")]` in `ThreadCycleDto`, and expose it to post scripts as `properties.StartInAir`.
  2. Refuse G76 by name in `assets/posts/fanuc-lathe.cps` (`g76Why`) whenever `p.StartInAir !== true`, so a start point above material (or a cached pre-#2878 record or legacy stream without `AIR 1`) never writes a G76 cycle.
  3. Compute `start_in_air` from the revolved meridian across the full rapid-infeed axial band `[min(start_s, s_deep) - insert_width/2, max(start_s, s_deep) + insert_width/2]` (where `s_deep = start_s + dir * height * tan(infeed_angle/2)`): true only when the part silhouette stays at or below `root` across the band (in front of the end face or in a relief groove wider than the insert) AND no remaining stock stands above `root` there after prior Facing, Grooving, Turning or Drilling operations (`operation::g76_start`).
  4. Allow `turning::thread` to extend `k_hi` up to `top_z` past the bar's free end face and fix `revolve::lattice` not to re-push out-of-domain window endpoints after `lat.retain`, so a G76 thread can start in free air in front of the end face.
  5. Update the three Fanuc G76 golden fixtures (`thread_g76.nc`, `thread_g76_area.nc`, `inch/fanuc-lathe/thread_g76.nc`) to use a free-end bar starting at `Z16.` (`Z16.625` flank, `Z0.6299` inch) in free air instead of `Z14.` inside a solid Z=40 bar.

- **Why**:
  - A Fanuc-type G76 moves the insert from the start point to each pass's depth at rapid traverse. Checking `StockZTop` alone in `.cps` cannot distinguish a faced end or a machined relief groove from uncut stock, nor does the post script know the insert width or part silhouette. Computing `start_in_air` from the revolved part, stock and prior cuts in the generator/verifier and requiring `StartInAir === true` in `fanuc-lathe.cps` is fail-safe by default: older caches and hand-written streams without `AIR 1` refuse G76 rather than silently rapiding into steel, while G32 passes (which plunge with `G01`) stay unchanged.
  - Putting the `StartInAir` check at the end of `g76Why` preserves more specific plan/range/hand refusals (such as chip-break dips or alternating flank infeed).

- **What was considered and dropped**:
  - **Checking only `StockZTop` inside `fanuc-lathe.cps`**: dropped because it rejects valid relief grooves and faced bars (where `start.z < StockZTop`) and misses narrow end-face overlaps where `start.z > StockZTop` but `start.z - insert_width/2 < StockZTop`, as well as flank-infeed shifts.
  - **Auto-shifting the G76 start point inside `fanuc-lathe.cps`**: dropped because the post never shifts verified points (`fanuc-lathe.cps` law) and shifting past a solid bar would cut unmodeled length.
  - **Changing `tormach-lathe.cps` in the same PR**: dropped to stay scoped to #2878 (Fanuc lathe G76); LinuxCNC G76 can adopt the same `StartInAir` property in a follow-up without changing the stream format.

- **Cost to change later**:
  - Low: `AIR 1` is an additive optional flag on `THREAD` and `ThreadCycleDto`, and `tormach-lathe.cps` can read the exact same `properties.StartInAir` field whenever its G76 fixtures are updated.

### Review fix: prove continuous stock clearance

- **What was decided**: Bound each interval between stock profile breakpoints by a solid rectangle above the thread root. Prove that each rectangle is inside prior cut regions. Subdivide a rectangle when several cuts provide the coverage. Refuse G76 if the proof exceeds its depth or cell budget. Use the actual swept segment for blade cuts. Reduce blade and nose credit by the clearance margin.
- **Why**: Isolated axial and radial samples can miss a narrow stock rib or a gap between prior cuts. A rectangle proof covers the material between the samples. Keeping each capsule proof on one signed side also avoids credit across the spindle axis.
- **What was considered and dropped**: More samples cannot prove clearance between samples. Stock hole credit and tolerance-based gap closure were also dropped because they could credit material that the prior cuts did not remove.
- **Cost to change later**: The conservative bounds can refuse hollow stock or a cut union whose boundary cannot be proved within the budget. A later exact coverage method can reduce these refusals without changing the cycle record or post contract.

## #2879 - Threading: allow free-air starts in front of the end face and keep the meridian lattice inside the bar

- **Decided:**
  1. Remove the post-filter re-insertion of `window`'s endpoints `(w0, w1)` in `revolve::lattice` (`crates/motion/src/turning/revolve.rs`). Every endpoint inside the bar domain `[d_lo, d_hi]` is already in `lat` from each move's `raw_band`; dropping the re-insertion keeps `lat` strictly inside `[d_lo, d_hi]` as the module's domain law states.
  2. In `thread_planned_in` (`crates/motion/src/turning/thread.rs`), compute `k_hi` from the unclamped `f.station_of(p.top_z)` instead of `blade::setup`'s clamped `s_hi`, while keeping `s_lo..=s_hi` clamped for `ref_top`, valley phase discovery, and the empty-window refusal. The same change landed on `main` first in #2892 (#2878) in the form `let s_hi_pass = f.station_of(p.top_z).max(s_hi);`. Because `blade::setup` sets `s_hi = f.station_of(top_z).min(d_hi)`, `s_hi <= station_of(top_z)` always and the two forms give the same value. The merge of `main` into this branch kept main's `s_hi_pass` form; this PR now adds the pinning tests of `turning_thread_end_face`, which also guard the #2892 fix.

- **Why:**
  - Re-inserting `w0` and `w1` after `lat.retain(|s| (d_lo..=d_hi).contains(s))` added intervals outside the bar whenever a move's band extended past an end face (by 0.1 mm on a free-end groove, by full pitches on a free-air lead-in, or by half a blade width on a free-end groove). In those air intervals `E(s) = 0`, so `revolve::scan` reported the capped wave floor (or blade tip) as rest and blocked the post.
  - Because `blade::setup` clamps `s_hi` to `d_hi`, setting `top_z` in front of the end face could never place lead-in lattice points in free air; every pass still started inside the part. Using `f.station_of(p.top_z)` for `k_hi` preserves exact bit-for-bit behaviour whenever `top_z <= d_hi`, keeps `k_hi - k_lo > blade::MAX_RUNGS` intact, and lets passes start in free air in front of the end face so spindle and feed synchronise (and so G76 cycles can start in free air, see #2878).

- **Considered and dropped:**
  - Skipping `e_u == 0.0 && e_v == 0.0` intervals inside `revolve::scan` while leaving `w0`/`w1` in `lat`: dropped because `revolve.rs` already documents that `lat` never lives outside `[d_lo, d_hi]` and keeping the invariant in `lattice` avoids special-casing air intervals in `scan`.
  - Unclamping `s_hi` inside `blade::setup`: dropped because `blade::setup` is shared with grooving and form turning, where `win` must stay clamped to the bar domain `[d_lo, d_hi]`.
  - Unclamping `s_lo` (the chuck end) in `thread_planned_in`: dropped because passes travel toward `-Z` (the chuck) and must not run past the chuck-end face.

- **Cost to change later:** Low. Both changes are self-contained inside `crates/motion/src/turning/` (`revolve.rs` and `thread.rs`) with no API or file-format change.

## #2880 - Turned hidden-rest parity on revolved meridian edges and open-recess bounds

**What was decided.** Fix both false-rest readings on a turned part with a neck and a modelled thread at their geometric causes in `camcraft-sim`:

1. In `crates/sim/src/solid_rest.rs`, record each boundary claim's orientation-free CCW XY angular sector (packed into `Claim.sector: [f32; 2]`, keeping `Claim` at 40 bytes) and settle multiple non-coplanar bare-boundary plane groups at one Z level by angular multiplicity: emit 1 crossing when any open angular sector around the column has odd group multiplicity (a single manifold surface crossed on a revolved meridian edge, cone apex or rim), and 0 when every sector has even multiplicity (a grazing V-root or overhang fold). Single coplanar groups stay 1, keeping the knife-edge `Open` verdict on flush stacked shells.
2. In `crates/sim/src/stock_sim/scan_turned.rs`, replace the `±reach`-inflated recess and band check in `TurnedBand::excuses` with strict overlap against the open recess `(p, roof)`. A turning pass whose segments never enter the open recess `(p, roof)` (stopping at the step face `Z20..Z60` or starting at the roof `Z63..Z78` of a `Z60..Z63` neck) does not own that recess's floor; any pass that enters or bridges the open recess still owns it and convicts.

**Why.** On a 64-segment revolved thread, grid columns on the 45-degree meridian (`x == y`) hit the shared edge of two non-coplanar tilted flank facets at the same Z. The old plane-group merge only merged coplanar boundary claims, so each flank emitted two crossings instead of one; across an even number of flanks that stayed `Paired` while inverting solid and air inside each V-groove and exposing the downward-facing upper flank as a hidden top (`0.7028 mm rest`). Separately, inflating a recess `[lo, hi]` by `±reach` (`±(r + floor)`) made a cone pass ending cleanly at `Z60` (and a thread pass starting at `Z63`) claim the `Z60..Z63` neck step face even though no non-gouging tangent ball centre can sit outside `(60, 63)` (`0.2435 mm rest`).

**What was considered and dropped.**
- Filtering zero-width gaps (`roof == hi`) in `scan_hidden.rs` alone: rejected because it leaves `solid_rest::column_crossings` inverted on every revolved meridian edge (affecting any closed cone or threaded bar, and hiding real crossings inside the inverted interval).
- Symbolic perturbation (Simulation of Simplicity) in `solid_rest`: rejected because it changes the documented contract on box boundary edges (`columns_on_edges_and_vertices_stay_even` and `flush_stacked_shells_are_reported_not_guessed`).
- Asymmetric recess inflation (strict on `lo`, `+reach` on `hi`): rejected because it would still block a Profile Finish window starting cleanly at the top of a neck (`Z63..Z78`) with false rest from the neck floor 3 mm below it.
- Adding a turning-specific bypass for modelled threads: rejected because the Minkowski offset (`profile_offset`) and `Access::reachable` already agree on every true upward-facing thread flank once `solid_rest` reports true parity.

**Cost to change later.** Both changes are self-contained inside `camcraft-sim` (`solid_rest.rs`, `scan_turned.rs`, `scan_hidden.rs`) with no public API or schema change; adjusting either law later touches only those files and their unit/integration pins.

## #2881 - Turning nose offset: a segment claims only where its tangent point is on it

**What was decided.** In `profile_offset` and `profile_offset_in`
(`crates/motion/src/turning/offset.rs`), the line claim of a profile
segment holds only over its claim window. The claim window is the
segment's own station window, shifted by `d*b/sqrt(1 + b^2)` (toward
the outside normal for the OD ride, the inside normal for the bore
ride). At these stations the tangent point of the ball is on the
segment. At other stations the nearest point of the segment is an end
point, and that vertex's circle makes the claim.

**Why.** The old claim held the infinite offset line over the
segment's own window. That is wrong in two directions:

- A steep, short chord (the first chord of a fillet) claimed its
  line far above the bar. The ride went out to X354 on a 30 mm bar.
  The bisection toward that spike wrote many zero-length moves.
- A sloped face did not claim the stations before its inside corner,
  where it is the nearest piece. The ride stood nearer than `d` to
  the face there. The pin measures 0.884 instead of 1.0 at a 45
  degree corner. In the catalog example `cone-thread`, the rough and
  finish rides dropped vertically at the cone-to-flat corner.

The window rule is the exact Minkowski boundary of a segment swept
by a disc. The no-gouge theorem of the module comment is now true at
every station.

**Considered and dropped.**

- Extra candidate stations at each claim window end. At these
  stations the line meets its end circle at the tangent, so the
  curve has no kink there. The extra samples changed four catalog
  programs and added near-duplicate blocks, and the chord settle
  already samples the curve. Dropped.
- A clamp of the ride to the profile maximum plus `d`. It hides the
  wrong claim and does not fix the inside-corner case. Dropped.

**Cost to change later.** Low. The claim is one private struct and
two helpers in one file. The catalog programs `turning/cone-thread`
and `turning/contour-finishes` are the goldens that show the change.

## #2882 - Thin turning profile samples that are closer than half the chord share

**What was decided:**
- Add a private `thin` step in `crates/motion/src/turning/offset.rs`.
- `thin` drops each sample that lies closer than `MIN_GAP_SHARE * share` to the last kept sample. `MIN_GAP_SHARE` is `0.5`.
- `thin` always keeps the first sample and the last sample. The window ends stay.
- `profile_offset` and `profile_offset_in` both run the outside ride and the inside ride through `thin`.

**Why:**
- Near a vertical tangent of the offset curve, the chord bisection places samples less than 1 micrometre apart. The lathe posts then write runs of identical G01 blocks. The Fanuc example wrote 408 identical blocks in one cone-thread program.
- `out.dedup()` removes only exact duplicates, so it does not fix this case.
- Thinning at the source fixes every turning ride. This covers profile rough, profile finish, contour and boring. It also covers every lathe post.
- Each kept sample is still an exact point of the offset curve. No kept sample gouges.
- Each dropped sample lies within the gap of a kept sample. At the window end, a kept sample can give way to the last sample, so a dropped sample lies within two gaps of a kept one. A chord therefore moves by at most two gaps. The chord bound becomes `2 * share`.
- The callers pass a quarter of the user tolerance as the share. The ride therefore stays within half of the user tolerance.
- At a tolerance of 0.01 mm, the share is 0.0025 mm. The least gap is then 0.00125 mm. That gap is more than the posted resolution of 0.001 mm.

**What was considered and dropped:**
- Drop repeated feed blocks in each lathe post (`assets/posts/fanuc-lathe.cps` and `assets/posts/tormach-lathe.cps`), when a block has the same words as the last block.
  - Dropped because it hides the cause in each post.
  - Dropped because it changes posted output in two dialects.
  - Dropped because the project file still keeps the dense samples.
- Use a fixed absolute gap, for example 1 micrometre.
  - Dropped because a fixed gap does not scale with the tolerance that the user sets.

**Cost to change later:**
- Low. The change is one private function and one constant in `offset.rs`. The pinning test is `crates/motion/tests/turning_offset_spacing.rs`.
- Changing `MIN_GAP_SHARE` changes the chord bound. Keep the bound at `2 * share`, or update the tolerance claim in this entry.
- Known limit: at a very small user tolerance, for example 0.001 mm, the gap is below the posted resolution. Two rounded blocks can then still be equal. This is rare and it costs no position.

**Review fix (PR #2897).** The catalog case `turning/cone-thread` reached main after this branch was cut. Its committed `.nc` had the repeated blocks. The branch merges main and rebuilds the case with `cargo xtask catalog --case turning/cone-thread`. The rebuild removes 465 `G01` lines and adds none. The runs of same-X `G01` blocks go from 509 to 82. The case README drops the limit line for #2882. The taper and thread blocks that the README names stay the same.

## #2887 - A no-pick 2D Chamfer refuses a top loop that is bevelled on only some sides

**What was decided.** A 2D Chamfer with no picks refuses at generation when a top edge loop carries a modelled chamfer on only part of its length. The refusal names a point on the bevelled part and a point on the sharp part. It asks the user to pick the edges. The check is `partly_bevelled` in `crates/motion/src/machining2d/chamfer_ride.rs`, called from `ride_loops`.

The check runs per segment of the top loop. It measures both ends and the middle of each segment against the wall loop at the corner depth:

- A segment on the wall (within 1e-6 mm) is sharp.
- A segment farther than 0.05 mm from the wall is bevelled.
- Between the two is tessellation noise. It counts as neither.

The loop is refused when it has a bevelled segment and more than one chamfer width of sharp length.

**Why.** The issue allows two results. The op can ride only the bevelled segments. Or it can refuse by name and ask for picks. The refusal is the smaller change. It adds no new toolpath shape. Before this fix, the verifier already refused the operation as a gouge. So no program that posted before is refused now. The user gets the reason and the workaround in place of a gouge coordinate.

The per-segment check does not depend on tessellation. An extra collinear vertex on the bevel's top edge changes nothing.

**Considered and dropped.**

- An open (partial) ride along only the bevelled segments. It needs open-path entry and exit moves on a chamfer ride. It needs edge-break credit for part of a loop in the verifier, and new goldens. It is a feature, not this defect fix.
- A two-sided Hausdorff gap for the whole loop. It makes the classification independent of tessellation. But it still classifies the loop whole, so the sharp sides are still cut.
- A change to the verifier (`models_a_bevel`, the edge-break credit). The issue says the verifier's refusal of cuts into sharp edges must not change.
- A separate note that lists the edges left sharp. The refusal message names the sharp part of the loop. A note for whole loops left sharp (#2596) needs a warning channel from `ride_loops` to the operation. That is separate work.

**Unchanged.** An all-sharp part breaks every top edge (#303). A loop bevelled all round rides its wall (#2435). A sharp loop beside a bevelled loop is left alone (#2596).

**Cost to change later.** Low. The rule is one function in `chamfer_ride.rs` and one call in `ride_loops`. The two tolerances (1e-6 mm and 0.05 mm) and the one-width rule are constants in that function.

## #2901 - The opening rapid starts over its entry; the first traverse needs a clearance plane over the stock and every fixture

- **What was decided** (the coordinator's decision on the issue, built as written; the maintainer can change it):
  1. **Seat.** The opening rapid of a clearance-seeded path starts over its own entry X/Y on the clearance plane (`cl::Toolpath::seat_approach(seed)`). It no longer starts over the WCS origin (#2382's seat, reversed) or over the frame zero. The toolpath, the CL `START` line, the simulation, the viewport lines, the fixture checks and the link router see no travel from a point that the machine never visits. The end of the rapid does not change, so no posted block changes.
  2. **First-traverse law.** After a tool change the control does not know its X/Y. The post sends Z to the plane that the path starts on, then X/Y at that plane. That one traverse can cross any point of the setup. The law (`sim::verify::first_traverse_low`) requires the start height of the path to be at or above the top of the start stock and the top of each fixture, in the frame of the operation. A 3+2 plane reads the eight corners of each box along its tool axis. If the start is lower, the result is the blocking verdict `Warning::FirstTraverseLow { at: 0, height_mm, top_mm, fixture }`. Its text gives the clearance height and the height to clear, for example: "the first rapid (move 0) comes from an unknown X/Y at the clearance height Z8.000, under the stock top at Z10.000 - raise the clearance height above Z10.000". The post gate puts the operation name first and writes no file.
     - The stock top is the full start stock (the stock box, and the top of the operation's material), never the in-process stock. The start X/Y is not known, so no line can be read again against what an earlier operation cut.
     - The steel is the setup's fixture boxes (`fixture::named_boxes_for`: the tagged fixtures, grown by their chord error, then the machine table). A 3+2 plane does not read the machine table: its box is a slab under the whole travel (`MAX_FIXTURE_DIM` wide), so a tilted axis reads a far edge of that slab (about 1e6 mm) and not a top that the plane can clear: with the table read, every indexed and 3+2 operation was refused (`fourth_axis_pose`, `index_swing`, `first_4axis_part`). The stock and the tagged fixtures are read in every frame. Upright, the table top is under the stock and is never the higher top. The coordinator accepted this narrowing. What it leaves unjudged: the first traverse of a 3+2 operation against the machine table (a tilted plane drops toward the table on its low side, for example about 0.36 mm for each mm of travel at B 20 deg). #2987 (P1) owns that gap (one design: clip the table box to the machine travel before the corner reading). The rotary, multi-axis and cross-drill kinds are #2965.
     - A start at the top passes (within `Z_TOL`), as the rapid law passes a traverse at the stock top.
     - `app` passes the extents and selects the kinds (`operation/first_traverse.rs`). The verdict is a `Warning` that blocks the post like the other verdicts. MCP names it `first_traverse_low`.
  3. **Scope.** Milling paths on a mill without a rotary axis: the 2D and 3D milling kinds and the vertical hole kinds, upright or 3+2. Not in this law: the multi-axis kinds, the setups with a rotary axis, the cross drill, turning, plasma, wire EDM and sinker EDM. Turning, plasma and EDM read their clearance on other axes or surfaces (a lathe station, a torch height, a wire). The rapid laws and the simulation judge the moves of their paths. The rotary, multi-axis and cross-drill kinds have no first-traverse law yet: #2965 (P1) owns it.
  4. **Cache.** The op stamp salt changes from `camcraft-op-stamp-v3` to `v4`. A saved cache holds the rapid from the origin and was judged without the new law. It reads Stale once, and the post refuses it until a regenerate.
  5. **Words.** The door word at creation (`clearance_stock::creation_advice`) and the "Clearance in stock:" note no longer offer "face the stock first" as a fix. A face ahead does not lift the first traverse over the start stock, so that fix is now false. Both say: raise Clearance above the stock top. The guide's troubleshooting page (`site/content/guide/reference/troubleshooting.md`) drops the same advice and gets an entry for the new message: what it means and how to fix it.
- **Reuse check.** The existing laws were read first. `RapidInStock` (rapid law (d)) judges a rapid along its known line. The first traverse has no known line, so the rapid law cannot judge it. The "Clearance in stock:" note names the cause of a convicted `RapidInStock` and never blocks. The door word is a word at creation, not a verdict. The `grblhal` and `tinyg` post scripts refuse a clearance under `StockZTop`, but only in those two posts and only for the stock. No existing law blocks this case on every path. Thus one new verdict is added, and the old laws stay.
- **Changed expectations** (old reading -> new reading; none is weaker):
  - `stale_rapid_law::regenerating_the_old_cache_judges_it_under_the_new_law`: `RapidInStock { at: 0 }` and "travels through stock" -> `FirstTraverseLow { at: 0, height_mm: 8.0, top_mm: 10.0, fixture: false }`, and a refusal that names `Op1Contour`, "under the stock top at Z10.000" and "raise the clearance height above Z10.000". The same program is refused at the same move for the same cause. The assert now pins both heights where it pinned only the index.
  - `clearance_in_stock`: the contour, face-to-Z9, first-operation and stepped-stock cases name the first-traverse verdict in place of `RapidInStock { at: 0 }` (move 0 has no X/Y travel now). The slot case is unchanged (its traverse inside the path is still `RapidInStock`). `the_same_plane_over_stock_an_earlier_face_cut_down_is_air_and_posts` becomes `..._holds_only_for_the_first_traverse`: no traverse inside the path is convicted (the #2121 acquittal by the program ahead still holds), but the post is held by the first traverse. This is the known cost below. The door word's expected text changes from "face the stock first" to "raise Clearance to the stock top or above", and the test asserts that the word no longer offers a face.
  - `wcs_start::a_clamp_on_the_old_origin_to_entry_line_changes_nothing` (new in the held work) becomes `..._is_judged_by_the_first_traverse_law_only`: the clamp is 40 mm tall over a 30 mm clearance plane. There is still no struck-move verdict on the old line and no routed link. The only verdict is `FirstTraverseLow { fixture: true, top_mm: 40.0 }`, and the post is held.
  - `center_cut_owed::an_inner_patch_face_runs_its_entry_out_to_air_for_a_tool_that_is_not_centre_cutting`: the expected facer path gets the same `seat_approach` that generate applies.
  - `deburr_cache_stamp`: `LEGACY_AUTOMATIC_STAMP` is captured again under salt v4 (the salt moves every stamp one time).
  - `operations::an_entry_edit_marks_the_slot_stale_and_the_orbit_proves_itself` (helper `height_notes_only`): the slot's clearance plane Z 5 in a 20 mm block gave the "Clearance in stock" note (move 0 crossed the block from the frame zero). Now the plane is the first-traverse verdict, and the notes hold only the Top note. The helper asserts both.
  - `stock_source_holes::framed_stock_chamfer_live_refusal_keeps_hint_without_local_move_number`: the B 10 deg chamfer had its clearance at 25, and the tilted block's high corner stands at 25.77 along the tool axis. The new law refuses it (the known cost, in a test). The test now sets the clearance to 30; its subject (the live refusal of a moved part) is unchanged.
  - `wire_stamp`: `ONE_PROFILE_STAMP` is pinned again under salt v4.
  - `stock_play::the_transport_maps_onto_the_plan_by_name` and the UI test `egui_app::tests::sim_readout_names_the_op_and_the_verb`: the opening rapid has no length now, so the timeline's first segment takes no time. The transport test expects that segment done at t = 0 (it is a rapid and cuts nothing); the readout test probes the first segment that takes time, which is still a RAPID.
  - `regression_models`: the measured minutes of the cube and the wavy slab lose the opening traverse from the frame zero (`0.35983333` -> `0.35933333`, `1.47475343` -> `1.46766667`).
  - CL goldens, the `START` line only (WRITE_GOLDEN through each test, except `pocket_adaptive_v63.cl`, which the test reads with `include_str!` and which takes the same one-line change by hand): `circular_ramp_stay_down.cl` (`0 0 10000` -> `1000 0 10000`), `contour_start_point.cl` (`0 0 30000` -> `40000 0 30000`), `pocket_waterline_square_dogbone.cl` (`0 0 25000` -> `1000 -1000 25000`), `pocket3d_trochoidal_pocket.cl` (`0 0 30000` -> `-9033 -1472 30000`), `pocket_rest_corners.cl` (`0 0 30000` -> `27700 16451 30000`), `pocket_adaptive_v63.cl` (`0 0 25000` -> `400 -400 25000`), `thread_mill_external_m10_single_form.cl` (`0 0 30000` -> `10770 3000 30000`), `thread_mill_external_m8_multi_form.cl` (`0 0 30000` -> `9744 3000 30000`). Each new `START` is the end of the opening rapid. No NC golden changes.
- **Example projects.** `examples/first-4axis-part.camproj`, `examples/first-continuous-4axis-part.camproj` and `examples/first-router-part.camproj` are loaded, each operation is regenerated with `GenerateOperation`, and the project is saved with `project::save`. The diff is the stamps, the start of the opening rapid, the file version and the tool `number` fields that the current save writes. The committed `.nc` files do not change.
- **`examples/guide-multiaxis.camproj`** (the maintainer's answer: regenerate it): loaded, each operation regenerated with `GenerateOperation`, saved with `project::save`. The project has no `.nc` and is not a catalog case. Its two operations were blocked before and stay blocked: `Indexed Face1` keeps its 30 gouge verdicts and adds `FirstTraverseLow { height_mm: 10.0, top_mm: 11.114 }` (the B 20 deg plane under the tilted block's high corner); its only move change is the opening rapid's start. `Swarf1` keeps 1649 moves; 402 coordinates move by one rounding step (1e-6) and its shank-hit list is the current law's (897 -> 884 entries; the changed moves are 639-1010, inside the path, not the opening move). The site test `site/tests/test_guide_images.py` and the two guide pages beside the images (`multi-axis/indexed.md`, `multi-axis/operations-multiaxis.md`) state the new counts; the indexed page also explains the new clearance verdict. The first-traverse law does not judge swarf (a multi-axis kind).
- **Known cost (accepted).** An operation whose clearance plane is under the stock top or a fixture top on purpose is refused, for example a contour after a facing pass took the whole top down. The message says how to repair it: raise the clearance height.
- **What was considered and dropped**:
  - The post sends X/Y first at a safe height, then Z: each NC golden changes. A larger change for its own issue.
  - No check (the seat alone): the old seat convicted a Z 8 plane under a Z 10 stock only by accident, on a line that the machine does not travel. Without a law the program posts, and the first traverse can go through the stock or a clamp.
  - The in-process stock for the top: the start X/Y is not known, so an uncut corner anywhere can be on the line.
  - The machine table in a 3+2 frame: its slab box gives a "top" a million millimetres away along a tilted axis and refuses each indexed operation.
  - The rule in `camcraft-motion` or `camcraft-cl`: the verdict type (`Warning`) and the steel (`FixtureBox`) are in `camcraft-sim`, with the other rapid and fixture laws. The rule goes there, and no crate dependency is added.
- **Cost to change later**: low. One verdict variant and one law function. A post that writes X/Y first at a safe height can turn the law off for its machines with one condition in `operation::first_traverse::answers`.

## #2908 - Batch tier lanes for separate runners: the `xtask` part

Decided unattended by the issue worker, 2026-11-20.

**What was decided**

- **A flag, not named groups.** `cargo xtask gate batch --lane N/M` selects
  lane N of M. The workflow chooses M. A named group for each crate does not
  balance: the app crate has most of the 973 steps.
- **A round-robin deal in plan order.** The steps that share the machine are
  dealt first, then the steps that run alone (`lanes::ISOLATED`, ui, clippy).
  Each lane gets an equal share of the two kinds (325, 324 and 324 steps for
  three lanes). Clippy is a step of the deal, so it is in exactly one lane.
- **No timing file in the split.** The longest-first order of `lanes.rs` uses
  `timings.tsv`, which is different on each runner. A split from it could put
  one test binary in two lanes, or in none. The split reads only the plan.
  The order inside a lane still uses the timings of that runner.
- **Each lane builds for itself.** A lane keeps the `debug build: <crate>`
  step of each crate that it tests. The runners share nothing but the commit.
  The compile cache (`sccache`) of each runner pays for the repeated builds.
- **A lane record, and one collector.** A lane run writes `lane-result.tsv`
  into its `gate-logs/batch-<stamp>/`. `cargo xtask gate-verdict <dir>...`
  reads the records of all lanes and prints one verdict. The verdict names
  each lane, its runner, its time, its result and each red step.
- **A lane that did not report is red.** The verdict is red for a lane with
  no record, two records, a void run, fewer steps than its plan, or a record
  that cannot be read. An empty lane is an error at the start.
