- **Partial work, `Refs #2908`.** This PR has the `xtask` part and the `gate`
  skill text. The issue stays open for the workflow.

**Why**

The worker's brief does not permit a change in `.github/`. The open PR #2606
changes the `report` job of `.github/workflows/post-merge.yml` and has the
label `needs-maintainer`, and the brief does not permit a stack on such a PR.
The `xtask` part does not depend on the workflow, and the workflow cannot be
written without it.

**What was considered and dropped**

- **The workflow change** (`post-merge.yml`: a lane matrix, one artifact for
  each lane, a collector job in place of the `report` job of #1611). It waits
  for the maintainer's decision on #2606. A proposal is in a comment on #2908.
- **One build job that uploads the test binaries.** The debug `target/` is
  10-20 GB. An upload and a download for each lane costs more than a build
  with a warm compile cache. The absolute paths in the binaries also differ
  between runners.
- **A split balanced by measured time.** It is better balanced, but it is not
  the same on each machine (see above). A committed timing table could do it
  later.
- **The `runners` skill text.** It describes the workflow, which does not
  change in this PR.
- **The macOS runner `m3`** and **the treatment of a push during a run**.
  These are decisions about the workflow and its runner labels.

**What it costs to change later**

The split is one function (`lane_split::assign`). A different deal changes
which lane runs a step, not which steps run: the test
`each_batch_step_runs_in_exactly_one_lane` holds for any deal. The record
format is read only by `gate-verdict`.

## #2919 - Read short STEP unit names before model import

**What was decided:** Change the parsed record names `GUAC` and `SUNT` to
`GLOBAL_UNIT_ASSIGNED_CONTEXT` and `SI_UNIT`. Do this before the existing
unit checks and the topology read. Keep one canonical exchange structure
for both consumers.

**Why:** The pinned parser expands some short names, including `LNGUNT`,
but leaves these two names unchanged. The unit reader looks for their long
names. It can otherwise miss the context and use millimetres for an inch
or metre model. The existing checks can validate the declared units once
both names use their long forms.

The mappings come from the public
[ISO STEP short-name registry](https://standards.iso.org/iso/10303/tech/short_names/short-names.txt).
The parser exposes `Exchange.entities`, `Entity.records`, and `Record.name`
as public fields. Its record lookups compare those names directly. The
change uses that public API and does not change entity references or
parameters.

The authored fixtures `testdata/models/short_units_inch.step` and
`testdata/models/short_units_metre.step` use our unit-box geometry. The
regression tests check the imported dimensions, volume, and declared units.
Separate cases exercise each alias and retain long-name controls.

The agreement corpus lists each model fixture explicitly. Its new rows
record the expected differences for these two fixtures. The model importer
reads their scale correctly. The raw tessellator still assumes millimetres.
The fixture geometry is in long form. The truck readings of the two rows
come from the live bench at `72ab66fc1`. Extending that list keeps the
corpus inventory complete; it does not change those readers.

**Considered and dropped:** Text replacement could change strings and
comments. A guessed scale could silently produce wrong geometry. A refusal
of every short-name file would reject legal files that the existing unit
reader can handle after name expansion. A dependency update would widen
this fix beyond the two missing mappings.

### Refuse a length unit that the reader would read as millimetres

**What was decided (review of PR #2927):** The model read
(`camcraft_kernel::step_length_units`) refuses by name:

- a file with a length unit when no unit context states a length unit
  (the same rule as the tool-body read, `camcraft_geometry::step_units`);
- a unit context that names a unit that is not in the file;
- a solid whose own representation context states no length unit while
  a different context of the file states one;
- a solid or sheet that no representation gives a context, while the file
  states a length unit (second review, P1). Each piece that the reader
  splits from a surface model takes the context of its model, the
  reader's own rule (`topology::items`), and is judged in that context.

**Why:** In each case the reader takes 1 mm per unit without a word, so an
inch or metre model is 25.4 or 1000 times too small. Issue #2919 asks for
the first refusal by name.

**Considered and dropped:** A note instead of a refusal for the third case
would still import a model at the wrong scale. Moving the predicate into a
shared function for the tool-body read would widen the change into
`camcraft-geometry`; the two copies are short and cite each other.
An exception for an item that no representation lists was dropped: the
reader reads such an item at 1 mm per unit, and a split piece in a
unitless context passed through it. A file that states no length unit
keeps the millimetre default (#306).
The two refusals for an item with no unit context apply only when the
file states a unit other than the millimetre. When every unit that the
file states is the millimetre, the reader's 1 mm default is the file's
own unit, and the item imports at the right scale (stack-gate finding:
the app's generated fixtures of bare topology beside a mm context, and
the kernel corpus row "second copy of the solid"). A refusal there would
refuse correct models.

**Cost to change later:** Remove the two mappings when the pinned parser
expands both names itself. Keep the inch and metre regression fixtures and
their scale checks.

### Keep the measured Linux bore path pin after the importer change

**What was decided:** Update the exact Linux x86_64 bore path pin for the
solidcore STEP reader introduced by PR #2904. Keep the verification,
planning-budget, and fallback assertions. Add assertions for the imported
mesh facet count and the cutting levels. Leave the Windows expectation
unchanged because this change does not measure that platform with the
current reader.

**Why:** PR #2904 changes the mesh of `Milling-test.step` from 952 to 6228
facets at the same chord cap. The fixture and the relevant HSM planner
files do not change across that switch. The planner derives its level
regions from that mesh, so a different triangulation can change the
planned moves and fitted arcs. The earlier Linux expectation describes
the truck mesh. The mesh and level assertions make the new expectation's
input and depth ladder explicit.

**Considered and dropped:** Widening the count band or removing the exact
pin would hide later path changes. Rolling back the importer would discard
the intended solidcore switch and exceed the short-name unit fix. Changing
an unmeasured platform's expectation would substitute a guess for a
measurement.

**Cost to change later:** Re-measure an affected platform when its mesh or
planner changes. Explain that change and retain the safety assertions.

## #2923 - Check the full work height against the wire guides

Check each guide height stated by the operation's machine before slicing the work for verification. Use the same height span as the wire sweep. It includes the programmed planes, the source part and the stock. Add the setup origin's Z coordinate to each stated guide height. The comparison then uses the same guide planes as the post. This also lets a 12 mm workpiece fit at an upper guide height of 2.3 mm and a setup origin of 9.7 mm.

A check on the programmed move alone passed a 12 mm workpiece with its upper guide at 5 mm. A check on the operation planes alone would also miss stock extending above the part. The check applies to vertical cuts and ruled cuts because both pass through the work. A guide may meet the surface. No machine clearance is assumed.

Requiring both guide heights for every vertical cut would prevent use of machines with unstated heights. Enforcing an additional minimum clearance later would require a machine-specific value and a test for its boundary.

## #2925 - Accept an explicit zero wire taper

Use the Wire Contour's typed taper angle when checking an operation parameter patch.
Zero selects a vertical cut and the project writer omits it from the saved fields.
Changing project serialization would change existing files when saved. Accepting all
zero fields would hide spelling errors. A later change to how a wire taper is stored
needs an update to this check and its MCP regression test.

## #2926 - Select STEP fixture readers with manifest paths

**What was decided:** Recognize `concat!(env!("CARGO_MANIFEST_DIR"), "/...")` in the conservative fixture text scan. Resolve its suffix from the crate directory. Keep the app and UI reader assertions.

**Why:** The suffix alone looks like an absolute path. The scan discards the crate directory when it resolves that suffix. PR #2904 removed other app readers that had hidden this omission. The app and UI libraries still contain fixture readers.

**Considered and dropped:** Removing the reader assertions would hide a missed reader. Fixed lists of fixture suites would require manual updates. Removing every absolute prefix would change the meaning of unrelated paths.

**Cost to change later:** Extend the macro recognition if the source syntax changes. A Rust parser would cost more to add and maintain.

## #2936 - a wall that leans in the frame is not a modelled chamfer

**Decided**

Fix the check of #2887 (PR #2894). Do not change the fixture of #1700.

`partly_bevelled` in `crates/motion/src/machining2d/chamfer_ride.rs` now
returns `None` when the top loop is the wall loop moved whole by one plan
vector (`leans`). The ride is then the wall at the corner depth, as it was
before #2887.

**Why**

The fixture is a 70 x 70 x 20 box stock with no part. The operation frame
is tilted 10 degrees. The top section (Z10) and the corner section (Z9) are
the same rectangle. The corner section is moved 0.176 mm
(`1 mm * tan(10 deg)`) along one axis.

No edge of that box carries a chamfer. The check of #2887 compared each
segment with the wall loop. It read the two sides that touch the moved
corners as "bevelled" and the middle of the other sides as "sharp". The
refusal text was not true for this model. A legal program was refused.

A loop that carries a bevel on part of its length is never a moved copy of
its wall. Its bevelled side moves in. Its sharp sides stay. The opposite
side would have to move out, and a chamfer does not do that. But an
undercut lip can move a side out. A bevel on one side and an equal lip on
the other side give a moved copy (#2944). Thus #2944 takes the move from
the operation frame, not from the sections. See
`docs/decisions/2944-chamfer-lean-frame.md`.

The test does not depend on tessellation. The vector is the difference of
the two area centroids. A collinear vertex does not change an area
centroid. Each segment of each ring (two ends and the middle) must then be
on the other ring within `LEAN_SLACK` (1e-4 mm). The sections are on a
1e-6 mm grid, and `MATCH_SLACK` (0.05 mm) is the smallest bevel that the
check of #2887 reads.

**Considered and dropped**

- Change the fixture (other tilt, or picks). The fixture is a correct
  chamfer on a plain box. A change would hide the wrong refusal from the
  suite, and a user would still get it.
- Compare signed distances (a bevel is always inside the wall). One side of
  a leaning box is inside its wall too. A sign cannot tell the two apart.
- Remove collinear vertices and compare the vertices one by one. The result
  would depend on a collinearity tolerance.

**Not decided here**

A part with a draft wall on some sides only, in an upright frame, has the
same two sections as a part with a modelled chamfer on those sides. The
check of #2887 still refuses it and asks for picks. That is the safe
reading. This PR does not change it.

**Cost to change later**

Small. The test is one private function with one call. Remove the call and
the check of #2887 is as it was.

## #2944 - the lean of a wall comes from the frame, not from the sections

**Decided**

The lean exemption of #2936 (`leans` in
`crates/motion/src/machining2d/chamfer_ride.rs`) now uses the move that the
operation frame gives to an upright wall. It does not read the move from
the two sections.

- `wall_lean(frame, depth)` gives that move. With no frame or an upright
  frame, the move is zero. When the tool axis is in the world XY plane, it
  gives `None`, and no loop is exempt.
- `ride_loops` takes the move as a new argument. The app caller
  (`material_source.rs`) computes it from the operation frame and the
  chamfer depth.
- `partly_bevelled` now cuts each top segment at the foot of each wall
  vertex that falls inside it. Then it judges each piece as before.

**Why**

The part of the issue has a 1 mm bevel on the -X side and a 1 mm undercut
lip on the +X side. Its top section is its wall section moved 1 mm in X.
The old test took the move from the area centroids, so it found a lean and
skipped the #2887 refusal. An upright frame leans no wall, so the move must
be zero. Now this part is not exempt.

The second change is necessary too. The top segment of each Y side runs
from X-29 to X31. Its X31 end is off the wall, so the old judgement read the
whole segment as bevelled. No segment was sharp, and the check did not
refuse. With the cut at X30, the piece from X-29 to X30 is sharp (59 mm)
and the piece from X30 to X31 is the lip. The #2887 refusal now holds.

The box under a 10 degree tilt (#2936) still generates
(`framed_stock_chamfer_live_refusal_keeps_hint_without_local_move_number`).
A lean with the wrong sign makes that test fail, so the sign of
`wall_lean` is checked end to end.

**Considered and dropped**

- Keep the centroid move and only compare it with the frame move. The frame
  move alone is sufficient, and the centroid code is then not necessary.
- A tolerance of `MATCH_SLACK` (0.05 mm) on the move. `LEAN_SLACK`
  (1e-4 mm) is stricter, and the sections of an upright box under a tilt
  agree with the frame move far inside it.

**Not decided here**

A part with a real draft wall in a tilted frame is not exempt. It is read
as before #2936. That is the safe reading.

**Cost to change later**

Small. One helper, one extra argument, one caller.

## #2946 - AGIECUT Classic 2S machine template

Ship a machine library entry for setup. Section 1.1 (p. 4) gives the U and V limits relative to the vertical wire and the rapid speed for each axis. Section 5.2 (p. 44) lists electrode wires. The template includes the listed diameters within the standard Classic range of 0.20 to 0.33 mm. [AGIE technical data C2.1, June 2002](https://static.gindumac.com/products/9ccc9b7e-b589-49db-9843-eff1da09434c/documents/ES-EDM-AGI-2002-00001.pdf)

Keep the X, Y and Z stroke lengths in the description. Centering them on zero would invent the endpoints in the user's setup. The taper rating depends on the guide and work height. Leave the taper limit and guide heights unset until the operator specifies the installation.

The machine entry supplies no post or generator conditions. A wire operation needs a condition from the user's control before CamCraft can generate its path. An operator can save a configured copy of the template without changing the shipped file. Adding a native job writer requires separate control-specific sources and verification.

## #2952 - Tormach lathe G76: refuse a start point above material

**Decided.** `assets/posts/tormach-lathe.cps` refuses the one-block
LinuxCNC `G76` when the thread record's `StartInAir` is not `true`. The
check is the last test in `g76Why`, so it uses the same refusal channel
as the other G76 refusals of the script (`refuse("G76 threading cycle
refused - " + why)`), and it runs before the drive-line rapid and the
`G76` block. The text has the form of the Fanuc refusal of #2878: "the
start point is above material (G76 moves the insert to pass depth at
rapid traverse) - start the thread in free air in front of the end face
or in a relief groove wider than the insert, regenerate the operation,
or choose G33 passes". The value is the one that PR #2892 computes
(`crates/app/src/operation/g76_start.rs`); the post adds no geometry.

**Why.** The public LinuxCNC G-code reference (G76 section) says that,
with no entry taper, the tool rapids to the cut depth and then
synchronizes. This post writes no entry taper (no `E` / `L`). So each
pass moves the insert in at rapid at the start Z. The old Tormach golden
started at Z14 on a bar that runs on to Z40: a rapid into solid material
(Prime Directive). The cycle words do not change.

**Old records.** A cached record or stream without the `AIR` word reads
`false`. The Tormach `G76` of such a project is refused by name until
the threading operation is regenerated - the same rule as the Fanuc post.

**Fixtures.** `tormach_lathe_support` keeps the solid bar
(`thread_world`, start Z14, used by the G33 goldens and the refusal
pins) and adds `g76_world`: the bar runs from Z-26 and ends at the free
end face Z14.693, and the threading top is one lead further out (16.3),
so the cycle starts at Z16 in free air. This is the fixture change of
#2892 for the Fanuc suites. Every test that must post a Tormach `G76`
uses `g76_world`. The G33 goldens do not change. In the two G76 goldens
the start moves from Z14 to Z16 (inch Z0.5512 to Z0.6299), and the
departure before the closing `G30` loses its `G0 Z40` (inch Z1.5748):
the #1604 departure goes +Z only up to the stock face, and the shorter
stock's face (Z14.693) is below the Z24 retract.

**Other posts checked** (each `assets/posts/*.cps` on `main`, for
`G76`, `G92`, `G78`, `G33`, `G32`, `CYCLE97` / `CYCLE98` and the
`onThreadCycle` hook):

| Post | Thread cycle | Start check |
|---|---|---|
| `fanuc-lathe.cps` | `G76` two-block | refuses since #2878 |
| `tormach-lathe.cps` | `G76` one-block | refuses with this change |
| `fanuc-lathe.cps` / `tormach-lathe.cps` passes | `G32` / `G33` per pass, not a canned cycle | not needed: no rapid infeed in a cycle |
| `linuxcnc.cps` | `G33.1` rigid tap, no THREAD record | not a thread cycle |
| `tormach.cps`, `grblhal.cps`, `tinyg.cps` | refuse `G84` | no thread cycle |
| all other posts | no thread word | no thread cycle |

Only the two lathe posts define `onThreadCycle`.

**Dropped.** A start that the post moves out to free air by itself: the
post does not know the part, and a moved start changes the verified
passes. A Tormach pin for a relief groove wider than the insert: the
fixture set has no grooving op for the Tormach suites; the judge itself
is pinned by `g76_start_tests.rs`
(`relief_groove_wider_than_insert_passes_when_grooved_and_refuses_when_uncut_or_narrow`).

**Cost to change.** One `if` in the script and one fixture flag.

## #2958 - Viewport overlay as wide anti-aliased lines, with MSAA

**What was decided.**

- The viewport overlay draws as screen-facing quads, one 32-byte instance for each segment (two f32x3 points and two RGBA8 colours). The vertex shader makes the six corners. The fragment shader fades the sides and the ends over one pixel. The old 1 px `LineList` overlay pipeline is removed.
- The overlay includes toolpaths, height planes, region outlines, triads, the ground grid and the other overlay lines. All of these use the one width.
- The default width is 1.5 pt, multiplied by the display's pixels per point. The choices are 1, 1.5, 2 and 3 pt.
- Each wide-line vertex moves toward the eye by `LIFT_WIDTHS` = 3 line widths of world distance. The world size of one pixel comes from the `mvp` matrix, so the lift is correct in perspective and in orthographic projection.
- Each end of a line extends half the line width past its point. Two lines that meet thus close the corner and do not overlap past it.
- MSAA is a setting: Off, 2x or 4x. The default is 4x. All the viewport pipelines and the traced-stock composite use the same sample count. A change rebuilds the pipelines and the multisample and depth targets. The resolved colour target stays, so the egui texture stays bound.
- The windowed shell requests `TEXTURE_ADAPTER_SPECIFIC_FORMAT_FEATURES` when the adapter has it, and reads the adapter's sample counts for the colour and depth formats. Without the feature, only WebGPU's guaranteed counts (1 and 4) are offered. The browser build always offers only 1 and 4.
- An anti-aliasing entry for a count that the device does not offer is disabled, and its hover text gives the reason. A pick of such a count is refused by name.
- A kept count that the device does not offer falls back to the highest offered count below it. The status line says so once.
- The two settings are per-user view settings in `view.json` (`app::view`), with the origin-name switch. They are not in `prefs.json`. They are not on the undo history and do not make the document unsaved, the same as the theme.
- The two settings are in the viewport's Display menu (#2818), in its Graphics group, after the projection. They were first in the Theme door. A manual test found that place wrong: line width and anti-aliasing are not part of a theme. #2818 had added the Display menu with a Graphics group, so they moved there. A general Settings window is proposed in #3025.
- Like the other Display menu entries, a pick is a direct `State` method call (`select_line_width`, `select_antialias`), not a queued command.

**Why.**

- A `wgpu` line is always one hardware pixel wide and has no anti-aliasing. Toolpaths were hard to see next to the 3 px egui triad (#195).
- 2 pt and more made the dense paths into one solid area when the camera is far. Thus the default is 1.5 pt.
- Without the lift, half of a wide line that lies on a face failed the depth test. In the pinning test, 292 px were visible on the face against 628 px for the same line in the air.
- An instanced segment uses 32 bytes against 48 for the old vertex pair. At the overlay limit (512k segments) this is 16 MiB against 24 MiB.
- For the fallback, a lower count never uses more memory than the user asked for.
- `view.json` already holds the viewport's look (the origin names). `prefs.json` was already past the 400-line file limit.

**Considered and dropped.**

- Draw the paths with the egui painter, as the triad is drawn. This loses the depth test and is slow on large toolpaths.
- Six full vertices for each segment (the trial). This needed approximately 135 MB at the overlay limit.
- A per-line width class for the ground grid. The grid already fades at its rim, so it uses the one width. This can be added later with a byte in the instance colour.
- A fallback to a higher sample count. This uses more memory than the user asked for.

**Cost to change later.**

- The width and the lift are uniforms and constants in `viewport/wide.rs`.
- A new sample count is one row in `Antialias` and one check in `offered_samples`.
- The file words are `"1"`, `"1.5"`, `"2"`, `"3"` and `"Off"`, `"2x"`, `"4x"`. A word that the build does not know reads as the default.

## #2965 - The first traverse of the rotary, multi-axis and cross-drill kinds

- **What was decided** (issue worker, unattended; the maintainer can change it):
  1. **The post order is the basis.** After a tool change the post sends Z, then X/Y at that height, then the full block with the rotary words (`fanuc.cps` `xyFirst` and `onRapid`). So the X/Y traverse runs before the rotaries move to the pose of the operation. The rotaries stand at a pose that the operation does not state. The Z of that traverse is the higher of the operation's clearance height and the start (`traverseZ`). The #2965 kinds are read at that height: a rotary or multi-axis path opens at its own pose (for example a radial clearance beside a standing bar, at Z -10), and the post does not traverse there. The #2901 kinds keep their reading of the start (their start is on the clearance plane, and the start is never higher than the traverse, so that reading is the stricter one).
  2. **Rotary kinds** (`Mode::Rotary`: Rotary Contour, Rotary Parallel, Rotary Offset). A new law, `sim::verify::first_traverse_low_swept`, reads the work as swept through a full turn about its fitted axis:
     - The start stock's and the part's points are read at their swept top (`swept_top`: the foot on the axis plus the radius, scaled by `sqrt(1 - dz^2)`). A 40 x 40 bar on a horizontal axis reads 28.284 over the axis, not its upright top of 20.
     - The steel that turns with the part (`Workholding::turning`, a chuck) is read swept too, at its corners (the distance to a line is convex, so the maximum is at a corner). The steel that stands still (`Workholding::fixed`, the table, a tailstock) is read at its top in the machine frame.
     - The start's machine height is `origin.z + t . (start - origin)`, with `t` the tool axis of move 0 (`+Z` when the move states none; the frame's axis for a 3+2 path). The machine stands the tool upright by a turn about the axis line. That turn keeps the line and maps `t` onto `+Z`. A radial start reads its radius over the axis line. When no turn about the axis stands the tool upright (a live tool beside a C axis, `stamp_spindle_c`), the start is read at the lowest height that the turn can carry it to: its own Z for a vertical C axis.
     - Which law reads a rotary kind depends on the mounted machine (`AxisLimits::turns_part` of its tilting rotaries). Each one turns the part: the swept law only (the post writes machine heights). Each one rides the head: the tip law of item 3 only (the work never turns, and an RTCP post writes the tip in the part frame). No machine, a mixed machine, or a rotary that an old file never stated: both laws, and the first verdict is kept.
     - The verdict is the same `Warning::FirstTraverseLow` (blocking, MCP `first_traverse_low`), so the post gate, the UI, MCP and the warned moves need no change.
     - The axis is the job's (`fixture::rotary_axis_of`). When the job states none (a stock or selection source), the same fit of the same facets that the generator ran is used. If no axis can be fitted, generation is refused by name ("no rotary axis can be fitted to the part, so its first traverse cannot be judged"). The generator itself fits that axis, so this refusal is not expected in use.
  3. **Multi-axis kinds** (5-Axis Contour, 5-Axis Parallel, Swarf, Advanced Swarf, Multi-Axis Rough, 5-Axis Flow, Multi-Axis Contour). They answer to the #2901 law on their tip, upright in the part frame (or along the plane's axis in a 3+2 frame). Reason: the post writes the tip in the part frame, so the Z move and the X/Y traverse run on the part's own plane at the start height. The tool leans up from its tip in each pose that cuts from above, so the stock and the fixtures under that plane are under the whole tool.
  4. **Cross drill on a mill** (`OpParams::Drill` with a `cross` list). Generation refuses it by name before any move ("cross holes are live-tooling work - the mounted machine is a mill with no turret"), so it can have no first traverse. The test pins that refusal. The selection still includes the kind, so the tip law reads it if a mill ever generates radial holes.
  5. **Cross drill on a lathe or a mill-turn** (`Kind::Lathe`, `Kind::MillTurn`, live tooling) is not judged by this law. `is_mill` is false there, as for the turning kinds of #2901. A lathe turret does not traverse in a mill's X/Y plane. Its radial approach is judged by the cross-drill standoff (`cross_stock::standoff`, the raw stock radius) and the rapid laws. This decision records that limit; it is not proof that the lathe approach has no collision. #3077 owns that gap.
- **Cache.** The post gate trusts the verdicts that a cache carries. The op stamp of the multi-axis kinds, the rotary kinds and the cross drill (`first_traverse::newly_judged`) takes one more word, `first-traverse-2965`. Such a cache reads Stale once and the post refuses it until a regenerate. The salt `camcraft-op-stamp-v4` does not change, so no other kind's stamp moves and the pinned stamps (`deburr_cache_stamp`, `wire_stamp`) stay. Dropped: a salt v5 for all kinds (each saved cache and each pinned stamp moves, for kinds whose law did not change).
- **Example projects (the maintainer accepted: regenerate, stamp only).** The new stamp word makes two committed projects read Stale once. They are regenerated, as #2901 regenerated its four examples. The diff is the operation stamp fields only, and each `.nc` and golden stays byte-identical:
  - `examples/first-continuous-4axis-part.camproj` (operation `Journal`, a continuous 4-axis kind): by its own test, `WRITE_GOLDEN=1 cargo test -p camcraft-app --test continuous_4axis_part`. That run also rewrote `examples/first-continuous-4axis-part.nc` with a last-digit change in seven A words (for example `A-54.14` -> `A-54.141`). That change was discarded: the suite passes (10/10) with the committed `.nc` and the new project, so the program stays byte-identical.
  - `examples/guide-multiaxis.camproj` (operation `Swarf1`): loaded, `Swarf1` regenerated with `GenerateOperation`, saved with `project::save` (the #2901 path). Its own path, `cargo xtask docs-images`, builds all three guide projects again and renders the guide images, which changes more than the stamp; it was not used. `Indexed Face1` (a face, not a #2965 kind) keeps its stamp.
- **Pinning tests.** `crates/app/tests/first_traverse_rotary.rs`: `a_rotary_kind_reads_its_square_bar_swept_about_the_axis`, `a_5_axis_kind_reads_a_far_clamp_over_its_clearance_plane`, `a_cross_drill_on_a_mill_is_refused_before_any_traverse`. The sim unit tests in `crates/sim/src/verify/first_traverse.rs` pin the swept law (corner radius, radial start, chuck and tailstock, axis tilt, a C axis, the clearance height).
- **Why one law per frame and no new verdict.** The #2901 verdict already blocks the post, carries its two heights and has its UI, MCP and warned-move mappings. A new variant would add four mappings and no new information. The words "clearance height Z..." read the machine height over the axis for a rotary kind, which is the clearance radius when the axis is at Z 0.
- **Known limits.**
  - A machine with two rotaries: the rotary kinds read the sweep about the one fitted axis only. The multi-axis kinds read the tip in the part frame; a pose that leans the tool down from its tip (an undercut) is not read.
  - The tool radius is not added: the law reads the tip, as the #2901 law does. A horizontal tool (cross drill) can reach one radius under its tip line.
- **What was considered and dropped**:
  - The rotary kinds read at the start angle only (no sweep): wrong, because the rotary words come after the X/Y traverse.
  - A sweep for the multi-axis kinds about each machine rotary: the machine's axis lines are not stated in the part frame for those kinds (`rotary_axis_of` is `None` for them), so the sweep has no line to turn about.
  - A refusal of every multi-axis and cross-drill operation (no law, only a refusal): it blocks programs that the tip law shows to be safe.
  - The judge in `camcraft-motion`: the verdict and the steel types are in `camcraft-sim`, as for #2901. No crate edge is added.
- **Cost to change later**: low. One law function and the selection in `operation::first_traverse` (`answers`, `turned_axis`).

## #2971 - Named tests for the groove and part-off catalog case

**What was decided.** Add `catalog_turning_groove_part_off::regenerates`
and `catalog_turning_groove_part_off::rebuilds` to the existing catalog
suite. Use the same `run_case` helper as the other cases. Add a focused
test that requires the case directory and both names in the test listing.

**Why.** The groove and part-off example merged after the catalog acquired
its named-test contract. The example had no wrappers for that contract.
The shared helpers already check regeneration, script rebuilds,
verification, timing, and byte-for-byte NC output.

**Considered and dropped.** Do not weaken the catalog contract or skip the
case. Do not duplicate the regeneration or rebuild logic. Do not change
the example fixtures or the posted program to fix missing test registration.

**Cost to change later.** Small. A case rename must update its wrappers
and the focused listing test together.

## #2973 - Read the short name of the plane angle unit, refuse an angle unit that cannot be read

**What was decided:** Expand two more ISO 10303-21 short names before the
STEP model import reads its units: `PLANUN` (`PLANE_ANGLE_UNIT`) and `GC`
(`GLOBAL_UNCERTAINTY_ASSIGNED_CONTEXT`). The expansion of #2919 (`GUAC`,
`SUNT`) moves with them into one table in `crates/kernel/src/step_units_guard.rs`.
After the expansion, a new check refuses a file by name when one of the
units of a representation context is:

- marked as a plane angle unit, but is not an SI radian, or is not a
  conversion of a unit that resolves to a radian with a positive finite size;
- not marked as a plane angle unit, but measures a plane angle all the same
  (a prefixed SI radian, or a conversion whose measure is a
  `PLANE_ANGLE_MEASURE_WITH_UNIT` or whose base unit is a plane angle).

**Why:** The pinned parser leaves `PLANUN` short. The units reader of
solidcore-step then does not see the plane angle unit and uses radians. A
cone semi-angle of 1 degree is read as 1 radian. With our fixture the
pcurve check refuses the solid with a misleading reason ("an edge lies
8.32 mm off the face's surface"). A file whose edges do not hold the
surface to the angle could pass with the wrong shape. The check is the
second layer that the issue asks for: an angle unit that a later short
name or a malformed file hides is refused by name, never read in radians.
Without the `PLANUN` mapping the check alone refuses the fixture by name.

`GC` changes only the distance uncertainty that the reader uses. The issue
asked to check it in the same work. A unit test pins that the uncertainty
of the fixture is read.

The two short names come from the issue's reading of the public
[ISO STEP short-name registry](https://standards.iso.org/iso/10303/tech/short_names/short-names.txt)
(`PLANUN` at line 1554). The worker could not fetch the registry again in
this session, because the fetch needed an approval that was not available.

The new fixture `testdata/models/short_units_degree_cone.step` is our own
draft frustum: base radius 10 mm, height 10 mm, semi-angle 1 degree. A 1
degree draft is a common mould angle. It is also an angle where a radian
reading stays inside the legal range of a cone (0 to 90 degrees). The
volume and the top radius of the frustum depend on the angle.

The STEP agreement bench needs one pinned row for each fixture. Its truck
side is a recording, and #2790 removed the truck reader. A recording for a
new file cannot be made, and a made-up one would be false. So the bench
gets a `Truck::NotRecorded` variant. Its row judges only the solidcore side
and the length unit. The raw tessellator of the bench does not expand the
short names, as #2919 recorded for the length unit. So the pinned mesh
verdict for this file is the refusal that the tessellator gives.

**Considered and dropped:**

- Map `PLANUN` only. A file with a short name that we do not know yet would
  still have its angles read in radians without a word.
- Refuse each unit that is not marked. A legal SI radian without a prefix
  reads correctly as radians, and many files list a steradian unit. A
  blanket refusal would reject legal files.
- Patch the pinned solidcore parser or its unit reader. That widens the fix
  to a dependency update.
- Put the fixture outside `testdata/models/` to avoid the bench row. The
  issue asks for it in `testdata/models/`.

**Cost to change later:** Remove the table rows when the pinned parser
expands the names itself. Keep the cone fixture, its volume pin and the
refusal pin.

## #2976 - The STEP edge-gap cap follows the tolerance that the file states

**What was decided.** The maintainer chose option A (reduced fidelity) on
2026-11-20, after the measurement below. The worker set the details.

1. **Edge cap.** An edge may lie off its face's surface by up to
   `cap = clamp(2 x stated, 0.01 mm, 0.02 mm)`
   (`camcraft_kernel::step_edge_gap::EdgeGapCap`).
   - `stated` is the distance uncertainty of the file, in mm. Solidcore's
     units module reads it from `GLOBAL_UNCERTAINTY_ASSIGNED_CONTEXT` and
     converts it with the unit of the measure. An inch file converts.
   - When the file has more than one context, the least value is used,
     because the face's own context is not known at the check.
   - A file that states no uncertainty, or a value that is zero, negative,
     NaN or infinite, keeps the fixed cap of 0.01 mm
     (`MAX_EDGE_GAP_MM`, unchanged).
   - No file raises the cap past `EDGE_GAP_LIMIT_MM` = 0.02 mm.
   - The floor of 0.01 mm means that a file that states 1e-6 mm keeps
     0.01 mm. No tracked fixture changes its verdict.
   - The lift check of a made pcurve uses the same cap (it used 0.01 mm).
2. **Refusal text.** A gap over the cap is refused by name, with the gap,
   the cap and the source of the cap. For example: `edge 0 lies 0.0210 mm
   off the face's surface, over the cap of 0.02 mm; the file states a
   tolerance of 0.01 mm, and the reader accepts twice that, from 0.01 mm
   to 0.02 mm`. A file without a tolerance gets `...; the file states no
   tolerance`. The start of the old text stays, so the existing pins
   (`bspline_discontinuous.step` at 0.25 mm) did not change.
3. **Looser mesh.** The machining mesh cannot meet the chord on a face
   whose edges lie farther off the surface than the chord (finding below).
   The importer (`camcraft_geometry::step::read`) then meshes the model
   one more time at `min(2 x stated, 0.02 mm)`. This happens only when all
   of these are true:
   - the mesher refused at the chord with `FaceCapped`, `EdgeCapped` or
     `Deviation`;
   - the file states a tolerance;
   - a kept edge gap is larger than the chord;
   - the looser tolerance is coarser than the chord.

   The chord that the importer hands out is that looser tolerance. Thus
   the existing reduced-fidelity law (#864: `step::coarse`, `coarse_mm`,
   the `ReducedFidelity` component, `model_fidelity`) flags the model and
   judges each check against it. The fidelity law is not derived a second
   time. No schema or project-file change was necessary.
4. **Notes.** These are the notes that the user sees:
   - The importer note, in plain words. The geometry crate writes the
     facts: "This file's edges sit up to 0.018 mm off their surfaces. The
     file states a tolerance of 0.010 mm. The model is used at reduced
     accuracy (0.020 mm)." The app adds what the fidelity law does at that
     chord (`geometry::import::step::loosened_consequence`, which reads
     `model_fidelity::excess`, `excess_floor` and `DEV_TOL`, the same law
     as `verdict_tol`):
     - excess over `DEV_TOL` (every chord over 0.015 mm, so 0.02 mm and the
       inch fixture's 0.01524 mm): "A program cannot be posted while this
       model is in the document. Export the file again with a tighter
       tolerance to post one."
     - excess inside `DEV_TOL`: "Gouge checks against this model are
       stricter, and an operation that they cannot check is refused at the
       post."
   - Review fix: the first text said "checks allow 0.020 mm". That was
     false. The checks are stricter, or the post refuses.
   - The kernel note for each kept gap over 0.01 mm: "an edge lies
     0.0180 mm off its face's surface; the file states a tolerance of
     0.0100 mm, so the reader accepts up to 0.0200 mm". The cap is never
     made larger without a word.
   - The "up to" gap is the larger of two values: the gaps that the kernel
     measured, and the edge tolerances that the reader raised, divided by
     its least margin of 1.5. This is an upper bound on the gap.

**Why.**
- `Lobe.step` (a user file, private, not in the repository) states
  0.01 mm. Its worst edge measures 0.0102 mm. A cap of 1 x stated refuses
  a file that is inside its own tolerance by any honest reading: the gap
  is sampled at 20 points, and the writer rounds its numbers. Two times
  covers this and stays small.
- The limit of 0.02 mm is 12 times under the 0.25 mm step that must stay
  refused. It is twice `DEV_TOL`.
- The safety argument does not depend on the edge cap alone. The machining
  mesh bounds each face against its true surface at the chord that the
  importer hands out (`machining_mesh.rs` deviation and capped-sag
  checks). A model meshed at 0.02 mm is flagged reduced fidelity, and
  every downstream check (program verdict, gouge gate, stock) uses that
  chord through `model_fidelity`.

**Measurement** (local harness, not committed; the gap of each bare edge,
as `cover_gaps` measures it, with the cap off for the run):

| File | Stated (mm) | Edges measured | Largest gap (mm) | > 0.001 | > 0.005 | > 0.01 |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Lobe.step (private) | 0.01 | 28 | 1.015e-2 | 14 | 10 | 1 |
| fig8.step | 0.01 | 1 | 3.5e-12 | 0 | 0 | 0 |
| fillet_corner.step | 1e-6 | 2 | 8.2e-13 | 0 | 0 | 0 |
| bar_cross_holes.step | 2e-5 | 4 | 1.19e-6 | 0 | 0 | 0 |
| bspline_discontinuous.step | 1e-6 | 3 | 0.25 | 3 | 3 | 3 |
| twisted_flank, Milling-test (0.01), Milling-test-inch (0.01 converted), sample_ap214 (1e-14), 8 more (1e-6) | - | 0 | - | - | - | - |

With the cap off, `Lobe.step` reads as one solid. The reader raised 7
more edges to tolerances of up to 1.507e-2 mm. The machining mesh refuses
the solid at the chords 0.005, 0.01, 0.0125 and 0.015 mm ("face 1 capped",
sag 9.9e-3 to 1.56e-2 mm). It meshes at 0.02 mm: 10640 triangles,
deviation 1.947e-2 mm. With this PR, `Lobe.step` imports at a chord of
0.02 mm, with the note. The mesh volume is 113192.5 mm3, and the exact
kernel volume is 113295.5 mm3.

**Cost.**
- 0.02 mm is coarser than the verdict tolerance of the stock simulation
  (`DEV_TOL` = 0.01 mm) and four times the import chord (0.005 mm).
- On such a model, a gouge of less than about 0.02 mm is not judged.
- #864 already handles a coarse mesh this way: the program verdict
  tolerance is `DEV_TOL` minus the excess (`chord - CHORD_CAP`). At a chord
  of 0.02 mm the excess is 0.015 mm, which is more than `DEV_TOL`. Thus no
  verdict tolerance is left (`model_fidelity::verdict_tol` is `Err`). The
  program gate refuses an operation on this model by name when its own
  floor does not cover the excess (`op_problem`, `excess_floor`).
  `VouchModelFidelity` does not apply, because the chord is a recorded
  measurement.
- `gate_problems` adds the `verdict_tol` refusal when no operation is
  refused by itself. Thus at a chord of 0.02 mm the post refuses each
  program while the model is in the document, also when each operation
  leaves stock that covers the excess.

**The advice of the reduced-fidelity texts (review fix).** The texts
said "re-import with a larger STEP facet budget". For a model that is
coarse because of its edge gaps, that advice is wrong. The document does
not record why a model has reduced accuracy. Issue #2996 adds that record;
then each text names the one cause. Until then each text names the two
remedies: "re-import with a larger STEP facet budget, or export the file
again with a tighter tolerance". This applies to `model_fidelity::TOO_COARSE`,
the MCP note (`model_fidelity::facts`), the refusal of a kind that cannot
read the excess (`op_problem`), the vouch refusal of a recorded chord, the
model-page hint and the `import_model` tool description. Dropped: a stored
cause in this PR (a schema and project-file change that #2996 makes
anyway).

**Posting waits for #2996.** The maintainer decided on 2026-11-20 to
widen the verdict tolerance for such a model in a follow-up (#2996).
Until then, on a model that opens at a chord of 0.02 mm, the user can:
- open the model, see it, measure it and set up stock and fixtures;
- make and generate operations (the gate names each operation that it
  cannot verify);
- read the reduced-fidelity flag and the note.

The user cannot post a program while this model is in the document.
Export the file again with a tighter tolerance to post one.
- The user sees the reduced-fidelity flag on the model page, in the MCP
  reply and in the project file, and the note names the gap and the
  file's tolerance.

**Considered and dropped.**
- A larger fixed cap for each file (for example 0.02 mm). Dropped: a file
  that states 1e-6 mm would accept a gap 20000 times its own tolerance.
- Keep the refusal (option D). Dropped by the maintainer: the user cannot
  open a file that is inside its own tolerance.
- 1 x stated. Dropped: `Lobe.step` measures 2 % over its own stated value.
- A file that states a tolerance over the limit gets the fixed 0.01 mm
  cap (the first brief). Dropped for a clamp at 0.02 mm (the maintainer's
  rule). The two keep every gap over 0.02 mm out.
- A loose mesh for every refusal of a file that states a tolerance.
  Dropped: the looser mesh is only for a model whose measured edge gaps
  explain the refusal. A planner limit on a sound model stays a refusal.

**Limits found (not exercised as a pass).**
- A file that states a large tolerance (5 mm, `edge_gap_021_stated_5mm`)
  does not reach the kernel's gap check. The reader fits those pcurves
  itself at the loose tolerance. No gap is measured, so the importer has
  no reason to mesh looser. The machining mesh refuses the 0.021 mm step
  at the chord by name. This is safe, but a 0.018 mm gap in such a file
  is also refused.
- A file that states no tolerance, with a gap between the chord and
  0.01 mm (`edge_gap_009_unstated`), passes the edge check. The mesh at
  the chord refuses it, as before #2976.
- The new fixtures are in `testdata/models/edge_gap/`, not in
  `testdata/models/`. The STEP agreement bench (`step_agreement.rs`) needs
  a recorded truck reading for each top-level fixture. The truck reader
  was removed in #2790, so a new fixture has no such reading, and a row
  with an invented reading would be false.

**What it would cost to change later.** The rule is in one kernel module
(`crates/kernel/src/step_edge_gap.rs`: `STATED_FACTOR`,
`EDGE_GAP_LIMIT_MM`, `MAX_EDGE_GAP_MM`) and one retry in
`crates/geometry/src/step.rs`. The pins in `crates/kernel/tests/step_edge_gap.rs`,
`crates/geometry/tests/step_edge_gap.rs` and
`crates/app/tests/import_step_edge_gap.rs` name the numbers.

Move `header_rows` and `coolant_row` to `op_page/header.rs`. This reduces

## #2984 - Encode one Agie setup without erosion steps

Provide a Rust API that encodes the SBL piece script and its SBR import manifest for an existing nominal ISO. Use one closed punch, 20 mm steel 0001, Berco Cut 0.25 and the measured Ra 0.30 request. The stock and 2 mm threading hole use integer micrometres. Derive all names from one validated file stem.

A controller can bind a quality name to stale data after a successful assignment. Clear the work's erosion steps during import. Return the expected control settings and offsets for the operator to check before release.

Main has no native Agie posting path. The separate encoder lets a caller create and inspect these records before that path ships. The first workspace writer must use the guarded encoder and retain its own contour, stock and lead checks. A generic post filter could miss a writer that publishes its own files. Extending this API to more work types or conditions requires measured offsets, geometry checks in the caller and control verification.

## #2987 - The first traverse of a 3+2 plane is judged against the machine table

- **What was decided** (taken unattended; the maintainer can change it):
  1. **The table's top face, not its slab.** In a 3+2 frame, the law reads the machine table as its top face over the stated X/Y travel (the table box clipped to the Z travel, which starts at the table top). The slab under it (`MAX_FIXTURE_DIM` deep) is out of the tool's reach. Along an axis that tilts past 90 deg, the slab's underside read about 5e5 mm; the top face reads the real height. The table box already has the X/Y travel as its footprint (`fixture::table_of`), so "clip to the travel" needs only the Z clip.
  2. **Read the table only when the head tilts.** The machine file states which rotaries turn the work (`AxisLimits::turns_part`, #804). When each tilting rotary (axis not vertical) turns the work, the pose comes from turning the part. The tool stays upright in the machine frame, and the table stays under the work, so the stock top is the higher top. The index-swing clause (#1107) judges the work against the table in that case. The law then does not read the table. When a tilting rotary can be in the head (a head rotary, or an old file that does not state `turns_part`), or when the machine has no tilting rotary, the law reads the table top face along the tool axis. This is the conservative reading.
  3. **The tool starts at the tool-change height, and the table counts only where the move along the tool axis from there can carry the tool under its top** (premise (b), chosen by the maintainer on 2026-11-20). The control does not know the tool's X/Y after a tool change, but the tool stands at the top of the Z travel (the table top plus the Z stroke, `GenJob::z_stroke`). The upright law has the same premise: it judges only the descent onto the plane. The worst start is any point of the X/Y travel at that height. The move along the axis from a start at local height `h` to the plane changes the world Z by `(plane - h) * axis_z`. When the axis points up (`axis_z > 0`), the table counts if that move can end more than `Z_TOL` under the table top. The verdict then names the lowest plane that every such move clears: `h_max - stroke / axis_z` along the axis, where `h_max` is the highest start reading. The in-plane traverse then runs between two points over the table top (a convex half-space), so it cannot go under it. A horizontal axis (B 90) never changes the Z and never counts the table, although the far X edge reads high along it. When the axis points down toward the table (past 90 deg, `axis_z < 0`), a higher plane stands lower in the world, and the verdict can only say "raise", which is wrong there. If the move can end under the table top, the path gets the note "...: the tool axis points down toward the table, so the move along it from the tool-change height (the Z travel top) to the clearance plane can go under the table top" instead of a verdict. A machine that states no finite Z stroke is read with stroke 0: a start on the table top, the stricter reading.
     - Found by the stack gate: a B 90 pocket on `tilthead.mch` at clearance Z95 was refused "under the fixture top Z625", and the `multiaxis/indexed` catalog case "under the fixture top at Z500" (Front and Back pockets) and "at Z134.808" (Tilted pocket, A30 B30). With a start on the table top (premise (a)) the Tilted pocket's move ends 62.0 mm under the table top at the X+ Y- travel corner. From the tool-change height Z500 it ends at Z-124.5, 375.5 mm over the table top. The shipped catalog case does not change.
     - **NOT covered:** a program that starts with the tool low near the table, for example after a manual jog. The operator must send the machine to its tool-change height before the program starts, as for the upright law.
     - Dropped: premise (a), a start anywhere on or over the table top. It refuses the shipped catalog case for a start that a tool change never leaves (the tip parked on the table 1 m from the part).
     - Dropped: drop the table from every 3+2 reading (the #2985 law). A plane that a move from the tool-change height takes under the table passes again (the wide-machine B 30 pin fails).
     - Dropped: a new `Warning` that says "lower the clearance plane" for an axis that points down. It changes the verdict type in `sim`, `app`, `ui` and the MCP surface. Follow-up #3081.
     - Dropped: refuse each plane past 90 deg with the "raise" verdict. Its height to clear is wrong for such an axis, and a refusal with a wrong repair misleads.
  4. **No stated travel gives a note.** A mounted machine that does not state all of its X, Y and Z travel gives no table box (`fixture::table_of` needs the three). On a 3+2 plane that the table would judge, the path gets the note "First traverse: the machine table is not judged on this tilted plane: the machine does not state all of the X, Y and Z travel, so the first traverse is judged against the stock and the fixtures only". With no machine mounted there is no table, and no note (the unstated-limit law).
- **Why.** The #2985 law skipped the table in each 3+2 frame. A head-tilt plane drops toward the table on its low side, so a collision with the table passed. A plain read of the full table box refused each indexed operation on the microARC 4 (`first_4axis_part`, `fourth_axis_pose`, `index_swing`, `tilt_a180`, `tilt_a180_routes`). Even the top face alone refused them (Z 190.5 at A 90, Z 336.55 at A 180). Those refusals are false: that machine turns the work, and its table never stands over the plane.
- **Considered and dropped.**
  - Read the table in every frame, clipped: refuses each shipped 4th-axis example (false refusals, Done-when item 2 fails).
  - Read the table in the machine frame of a work-turning rotary: this needs the rotary axis line for an indexed operation. `fixture::rotary_axis_of` gives it only for the rotary kinds. No gain, because the table is under the work there.
  - Refuse when the machine states no travel: each 3+2 operation on a vendor file without travel would stop posting. A note is visible and does not stop a legal program.
  - A new `Warning` text for the table ("under the table top"): it changes the verdict type and the MCP surface. The existing "fixture top" text names the height to clear, which is the repair.
- **Not judged (known).** The law runs at generation only (as in #2985). Loading a different machine after a generate does not judge the first traverse again until the next generate. A machine with a head tilt and a vertical work C is read without the C turn of the footprint. A mixed machine, with a work-turning tilt (for example a table A) and a head tilt (for example a head B), reads the table top face in the setup frame: the part turn of the work-turning tilt is not in that reading.
- **Cost to change later**: low. One predicate (`work_tilts`), one clip (`table_top_face`) and one reading (`table_read`) in `operation/first_traverse.rs`.

## #2990 - Split adaptive trochoid targets and reduce fixture work

**What was decided.** Move six public shape tests into three independent
integration targets. Use smaller fixtures and a coarser debug measurement
grid. Keep all 22 tests, the one existing ignored test, and all 61 original
assertion lines.

- `adaptive_troch_parallel` holds the wide-pocket and corner-cleanup tests.
- `adaptive_troch_island` holds the island and ring tests.
- `adaptive_troch_neck` holds the triangle-and-neck test and the ignored
  L-shape test.

Shared helpers in `tests/common/adaptive_troch.rs` use public APIs.
The remaining 16 tests stay in the original unit module, which has
388 lines. Private tests keep access to private helpers there. No
production API, dependency, or gate routing changes are needed. Cargo
discovers the new targets. The batch scheduler can run them independently.

The D6 rectangle is 30 x 24 mm. The D10 rectangle is 44 x 36 mm. Both
retain enough width to exercise parallel lanes. The D6 island uses a
30 x 30 mm outer boundary and a 6 x 6 mm hole. The D10 island uses a
48 x 40 mm outer boundary and a 12 x 12 mm hole.

The ring starts with a 12 x 10 mm rectangle. Its offsets remain 12 mm
and 2 mm, so the ring keeps its 10 mm band. The triangle keeps its
original 60 x 60 mm dimensions. The neck keeps its original 30 x 30 mm
wide lobe and 10 mm neck width. Only its narrow end is shorter: its final
X coordinate changes from 60 mm to 48 mm. The explicit-parameter test
uses a 30 x 16 mm face and keeps its rapid-count assertion.

Use `QualitySpec.cell = D / 60` in debug runs of `check_cleared`, as in
the existing project pattern. Release runs keep the default `D / 80`
cell size. Both modes run all geometry assertions. The existing ignored
L-shape test moves without a fixture change. Its release run keeps
the `D / 80` cell size.

Add a 90-second execution budget to the existing wide-rectangle test in
the `adaptive_troch_parallel` target.
Apply this assertion in every run. The initial 60-second budget failed
at 61.93 seconds in a concurrent suite run. The 90-second budget permits
contention. The measurement excludes compilation. The unchanged fixtures
took 178.44 seconds. A mutation that restored those fixtures took
167.53 seconds and failed the 90-second budget.

**Why.** Smaller fixtures and the debug cell size reduce repeated
geometric work. Independent targets let the scheduler distribute that
work. The tests still check their behavior in the batch gate. Release
runs retain the finer measurement. Each test file stays below about
400 lines.

The local motion lib baseline took 207.11 seconds. Fixture changes alone
reduced it to 191.12 seconds, a reduction of about 7.7 percent. This was
not enough to address the slow target. Add the target split rather than
rely on smaller fixtures alone.

**Considered and dropped.** Moving these tests to the heavy lane would
remove their checks from the batch gate. The proposed light tier in
PR #2787 has not merged. Moving all seven reported slow tests would need
access to private helpers. Move the public shape tests instead. Keep the
private tests in the unit module without exposing more production APIs.

The smaller 38 x 33 mm D10 rectangle failed the existing rest-area
assertion: 31.03 mm2 exceeded 21.50 mm2 plus the 8.27 mm2 tolerance.
Enlarge the fixture to 44 x 36 mm and keep that assertion.

Smaller D10 island fixtures failed the existing checks. A 36 x 36 mm
outer boundary with a 6 x 6 mm hole failed the rest comparison.
A 54 x 36 mm outer boundary with a 10 x 10 mm hole measured about
128 degrees of engagement at `D / 60` and failed the engagement check.
Keep the 48 x 40 mm outer boundary and the 12 x 12 mm hole. Do not
relax either assertion.

The 30 x 30 mm and 45 x 45 mm triangles failed the existing rest
comparison. Keep the original 60 x 60 mm triangle. The neck fixture with
a 24 mm wide lobe also failed the rest comparison. Keep its original
30 x 30 mm lobe and shorten only the narrow end.

**Cost to change later.** Restore or enlarge the fixtures if a defect
needs a larger case. Change the execution budget or debug cell size only
with measured evidence. A different target split needs only test moves
and helper imports. Keep the assertions and test count when changing
the fixtures or target layout.

## PR #3032 - Refresh the reached Linux bore pin

**What was decided.** Pin the Linux x86_64 bore path to 3158 moves,
3130 planar feeds and 1141 arcs. Require the imported mesh to contain
6228 facets. Require the four cutting levels at Z 0, 5, 10 and 15.
Add a quick test that rejects the old tuple and adjacent count tuples.
Keep the existing verification, fallback and planning-budget checks.

**Why.** The review found a stale baseline in the reached release heavy
lane. PR #2904 (`bac4a96c7`) replaced the STEP importer. Decision #917
records that `Milling-test.step` changed from 952 truck facets to 6228
solidcore facets, with measured deviation within the requested tolerance.
The changed mesh affects the cutting regions and their arc fits.
The review measured the new tuple on both this PR and upstream main.
The mesh and cutting-level assertions bind the count to that input and
require every intended level to remain present.

**Considered and dropped.** Do not widen the count range, ignore the
failure, or move the test out of its lane. Do not change production code
to recreate the old truck-mesh count. Keep the safety assertions and
measure the corrected pin in the release heavy lane.

**Cost to change later.** A later mesh or planner change must explain
and measure a new tuple. Keep the mesh, cutting-level and safety checks
when the count changes.

## #2991 - The first-traverse refusal of a 3+2 operation names the heights that the user set

**What was decided.**
- `Warning::FirstTraverseLow` gets the field `tilted: bool`, with
  `#[serde(default)]`. A cache saved before this change loads, and its
  verdict reads as upright, with the text that it had.
- The law (`camcraft_sim::verify::first_traverse_low`) does not change. It
  gives the two heights in the frame of the path and `tilted: false`.
- The operation layer (`operation::first_traverse::judge`) puts a 3+2
  verdict into the frame in which the user sets the heights. Generate
  shifts each height by `h - origin.z` into the frame
  (`operation/generate.rs`), so `in_user_frame` adds `origin.z` to the two
  heights. A frame that is not upright (`TiltedFrame::is_upright`) sets
  `tilted`. In the guide example (`Indexed Face1`, B 20 deg, origin Z 20),
  the verdict now gives the clearance height 30 (the typed value) and the
  corner 31.114, not 10 and 11.114.
- The text of a tilted verdict says that the two heights are measured along
  the tilted tool axis, and it names the raise (`top - height`, the same in
  each frame). It has no `Z` value and no `X/Y`: "the first rapid (move 0)
  comes from an unknown position at the clearance height 30.000 mm, under
  the stock top at 31.114 mm (both measured along the tilted tool axis) -
  raise the clearance height by at least 1.114 mm".
- The text of an upright verdict does not change.
- The posed law (#3084, #3100) reads a 3+2 plane along the frame's axis
  from its origin, so its verdict is local too. It takes the same shift
  and `tilted` before it replaces the lower first-traverse verdicts. The
  tops then compare in one frame, and one verdict names the highest top.
  `FirstTraverseUnderTable` stays as it is (#3138).
- The troubleshooting page gets an entry for the new text. The indexed
  guide page says what the warning gives after a regenerate.

**Why.**
- The refusal was correct, but it named the local height (10), and the user
  typed 30 (the issue). A Fixed height is typed in the frame of the setup,
  and `h - origin.z` gives the local value. Thus `local + origin.z` is the
  typed value. For a height that refers to the model or the stock, the
  resolved value is `z_local + origin.z` (#2389, `fold_height`), and the
  same shift gives the resolved height. The raise is correct in the two
  cases.
- The conversion is in `app`, which knows the frame. The sim law stays one
  function in one frame.

**Considered and dropped.**
- Keep the local heights in the warning and add `origin.z` as a second
  field, for the text to add: two new fields in place of one, and the
  stored heights do not match the text.
- Change the upright text too (no `Z`, a raise): the upright text is
  correct, and many tests and the troubleshooting heading quote it. That
  is out of the scope of this issue.
- A change of the op stamp salt (v4 to v5), so that each saved cache reads
  Stale and is generated again with the new text: each stamp moves, and
  the pinned stamps of `deburr_cache_stamp` and `wire_stamp` and the stamps
  of the example projects change for a text change. The verdict and the
  held post are the same in an old cache. Only its text is the old text
  until the operation is generated again.
- Regenerate `examples/guide-multiaxis.camproj`: the cache diff (stamps,
  rounding) is large for a text change. The guide page says "after a
  regenerate".

**Cost to change later.** Low. One field with a default, one map in
`operation/first_traverse.rs`, and one text arm in `verify/types.rs`.

## #2996 - Widen verdicts only for models limited by the file tolerance

The maintainer decided on 2026-11-20 to accept a true-surface bound up to
0.030 mm for a model made coarse by the file's stated tolerance. The
program header must state that bound. A model made coarse by the facet
budget keeps the strict law of #864.

### The rule

A model's chord error `c` bounds the deviation of its kept mesh from the
true surface. The importer promises `PROMISED_CHORD` = 0.005 mm. The
excess is `e = c - 0.005`. Each gouge law holds a tolerance `t` and judges
against the mesh at `t'`.

The persisted `file_tolerance` record permits widening only when the file
tolerance required the coarse mesh and the facet budget did not coarsen
it further. Missing records, budget coarsening and mixed causes keep the
strict law. A selection can widen only when every reduced source has the
permitted cause. Import, project save/load, copies and undo preserve the
record. Update undo restores each copy's own record, including a cause
that differs from the source. This prevents one eligible part from
widening another part.

For an eligible model:

| Chord `c` | Mesh tolerance `t'` | True-surface bound for `t = DEV_TOL` |
|---|---|---|
| up to 0.005 mm | `t` | at most 0.015 mm |
| 0.005 to 0.010 mm | `t - e` (#864) | 0.015 mm |
| over 0.010 to 0.020 mm (`WIDE_CHORD_LIMIT`) | `min(t - 0.005, 0.005)` | `c + 0.005`, at most 0.025 mm |
| over 0.020 mm | `t - e` (#864) | no allowance at `DEV_TOL`: refused by name |

An ineligible model uses `t - e` at every reduced chord. At `c = 0.012`
mm, `DEV_TOL = 0.010` mm gives a mesh tolerance of 0.003 mm. At or above
`c = 0.015` mm, that law has no tolerance left and refuses the operation.
Missing cause records, budget models and chords up to 0.010 mm keep their
old law.

The eligible widened mesh allowance is capped at `PROMISED_CHORD` =
0.005 mm even when the base law has a larger tolerance. For a plasma law
with `t = 0.025` mm and `c = 0.012` mm, an eligible file-tolerance model
uses a mesh allowance of 0.005 mm and a true-surface bound of 0.017 mm.
A budget model at the same chord keeps its old mesh allowance of
0.018 mm. This cap makes the stated widened bound valid for every
eligible gouge law.

- The mesh tolerance and the true-surface bound are different quantities.
  At `c = 0.019` mm, an eligible model has a mesh tolerance of 0.005 mm
  and a true-surface bound of 0.024 mm. The header and model note state
  0.024 mm, rather than the chord or the mesh tolerance.
- `t'` never exceeds `t`. A law whose own tolerance is 0.005 mm or less
  is still refused by name in the widened range.
- `WIDE_CHORD_LIMIT` is a constant in `camcraft_sim::verify`. No file,
  facet budget or vouch can raise it.
- `verify::excess_floor` keeps the strict default. The explicit
  `verify::excess_floor_for` selects the widened arithmetic from the
  cause record. `verify::strict_floor` remains strict.

### Safety, for each direction

- **A cut into the part.** On a convex wall, a facet can stand inside
  the true surface by `c`. The mesh allowance adds `t'`, so the stated
  true-surface bound is `c + t'`. A deeper gouge is convicted and blocks
  the post. Pins:
  `a_real_gouge_deeper_than_the_verdict_tolerance_still_blocks_a_widened_model`,
  `a_cut_deeper_than_the_widened_tolerance_into_a_convex_wall_is_still_convicted`.
- **Material left on the part.** On a concave wall, a facet can stand in
  the air by `c`. A false gouge can block the post. The rule keeps that
  conservative result.

### Each reader of the verdict tolerance

- **Gouge laws** use the widened mesh allowance only for eligible source
  models. Other source models use #864's strict allowance.
- **Laws that also guard a body other than the cutting edge** keep
  `verify::strict_floor` and `fidelity_law::tightened_strict`. These are
  the turning meridian margin, lathe axial-hole tolerance,
  `revolve::gouge_tol_on`, rotary field allowances and probe stylus slack.
  The cutting-edge laws in `VerifyContext` can use the eligible widened
  allowance. The program gate still uses the strict law for turning,
  rotary and probe operations. These operations are refused when the
  excess uses their floor.
- **Collision bands** grow by the whole excess, including the widened
  range. This applies to the reach law, `rapids_radial`, `cross_stock`,
  `drill_reach` and `drill_station`. Their growth does not come from the
  smaller deduction made by the widened mesh law.
- **`stock_top`** grows by `model_excess` directly.
- **Stock simulation and the program gate** use the same cause record
  and tolerance law as the operation. The gate refuses an operation
  when the selected law has no positive allowance.
- **Keep law and rest material** do not read the excess.
- **Fixtures** are judged by a box grown by the chord.

### What the user sees

- Each widened model adds a program header comment. For `c = 0.019` mm,
  it states a true-surface bound of 0.024 mm. It does not state that the
  model was checked to its chord alone. Bound display rounds upward to
  0.001 mm or 0.00001 inch, rather than to the nearest value. For
  `c = 0.0192` mm, the numerical bound is 0.0242 mm and the displayed
  bound is 0.025 mm. This formatting does not change `surface_bound`.
- The engine emits the note after `onOpen` through `onComment`. Each
  shipped dialect uses its own valid comment delimiters and preserves
  the complete bound. A custom post may omit the note, as the maintainer
  permitted.
- The model page and MCP facts state the same true-surface bound. The
  import consequence describes the permission only for the eligible
  file-tolerance cause.

### What the user loses

For an eligible widened model, the checks can miss a true-surface gouge
up to `c + 0.005` mm, at most 0.025 mm. This stays below the accepted
0.030 mm bound. The full-fidelity bound is at most 0.015 mm. Models
coarsened by the budget lose no protection from #864.

### Considered and dropped

- **Widen all coarse models from the chord alone.** Dropped. The
  maintainer permits only the file-tolerance cause. Old records cannot
  establish that cause and therefore keep the strict law.
- **Report the chord as the check bound.** Dropped. It excludes the
  additional mesh allowance and understates the possible real gouge.
- **Round the displayed bound to the nearest unit.** Dropped. That can
  display a value below the numerical bound. Round upward instead.
- **Spend the full accepted 0.030 mm bound.** Dropped. Keeping the
  existing 0.005 mm mesh allowance gives a smaller bound, at most
  0.025 mm. The same cap also protects laws with larger base tolerances.
- **Widen only where #864 has no allowance left.** Dropped. A coarser
  model could then receive a looser verdict than a finer model.
- **Use `max(t, c)` as each law's tolerance.** Dropped. It can loosen a
  finish tolerance beyond the user's request.
- **Use `VouchModelFidelity`.** Dropped. The chord is a measured value.
- **Widen every body guard.** Dropped. Turning, rotary and probe guards
  must still protect the shank, holder, bar and stylus.

### Cost to change later

The limit and widened arithmetic stay in the simulation crate. A change
to eligible causes must update import, persistence, copies and undo, with
their lifecycle pins. A numerical change must also update the separate
mesh-allowance and true-surface-bound pins and the warning text.

## #3000 - Rotary Contour rings about a horizontal axis

**What was decided.** For a fitted axis with `abs(axis.dir.z) < 0.0175`,
Rotary Contour reads top and bottom as axial ball-center stations.
It reads clearance and retract as tool-tip radii about the fitted axis.
These values do not depend on the axis line's world Z position.
Other axis stances keep their existing world-height conversion.

The generator reuses the waterline contact law and the radial link builder.
A coordinate permutation preserves each ball center between their planning
frames. Arcs become chords before this conversion. The existing pose law
then places the tool tip under that same ball center.
The generator refuses unsafe clearance and retract radii by name.
It also refuses inverted or non-finite station bounds by name.
This change adds no dependencies.

**Why.** A horizontal axis has no usable world-Z divisor for axial stations.
Explicit station bounds permit complete rings about X.
Radial clearance and retract moves let the tool leave each ring safely.
Reusing the existing contact and link laws limits the new geometry code.
Keeping the other stances unchanged preserves their established height contract.

**Considered and dropped.** Removing the stance guard alone retains division
by zero and does not provide safe links. A global conversion of rotary heights
to radii belongs to #2774, which has separate live work.
Changing standing-contour semantics would extend this fix beyond its defect.
A new ring-generation algorithm would duplicate the existing waterline law.

**Cost to change later.** A common rotary height contract will need coordinated
parameter, UI, and compatibility changes. The station and clearance pins must
change with that contract. The ball-center conversion and radial link reuse
can remain if their geometric conventions remain the same.

**Refusals that this change removes on purpose.** The old horizontal-stance
refusal ("a laid bar is finished with passes along it: Rotary Parallel") was
not a safety law. It said only that the height law had no world-Z divisor.
This change gives the laid stance its own station law, so two app tests that
pinned the old refusal now pin the new result:

- `operations::the_rotary_twins_refuse_each_other_stances_by_name` becomes
  `a_standing_bar_refuses_rotary_parallel_by_name`. The standing-bar refusal
  of Rotary Parallel stays, with its name check. The laid twin moves to
  `a_laid_bar_cuts_rotary_contour_rings_about_x`. That test requires status
  Ok, zero blocking warnings, radial poses about X, ball centers inside the
  axial station window, rings at more than three stations, and the
  column-verdict refusal of a rotary program.
- `setup_align_multiaxis::turned_rotary_contour_cuts_posts_and_fits_axis_like_the_baked_part`
  expected a refusal for the as-modelled stance (the bar lies flat along Y: `unturn_xz` maps the bar axis z to y). That
  stance now cuts. The test requires a fitted axis along Y, radial poses about
  Y on each posed move, and a path that differs from the turned path. The
  turned and baked cases keep their equal-path and equal-post checks.

Dropped: keep the refusal for these two fixtures only. That would make the
generator depend on the caller, and #3000 asks for exactly this stance.
Dropped: change the tests to "differs or refuses". That accepts a refusal,
so it is weaker than the old assert.

## #3001 - Post explicit Side Burn moves through the machine dialect

**Decided:** Add the optional `edm.codes.side` template to the shipped
sinker post and the machine editor's code list. Require `{x}`, `{y}`,
`{z}`, and `{f}` in the template. Fill them with the absolute endpoint
in the work offset and the feed, in the document's units. Keep all EDM
codes in the machine file. Add no production code for a real control.

**Why:** The generated Side Burn already states its downward plunge,
lateral feed, return feed, and rapid retract as explicit CL moves.
Post the plunge with `depth`. Post each lateral feed with `side`.
Preserve the direction and amount that the generator states. Accept only
feeds along one X or Y axis at constant Z. Refuse missing dialect data,
incomplete coordinates, invalid feed, and unsupported moves by name.
The existing straight burn keeps its current depth code and needs no
`side` entry. The tests use an invented dialect. No real EDM control was
exercised.

**Dropped:** Do not choose an implicit lateral code or reuse `depth` for
a lateral feed. Either choice can omit the required movement. Do not
replace explicit moves with a control orbit. Do not add general XYZ or
diagonal servo feeds; the generated Side Burn does not need them.

**Cost to change later:** A real control needs verified machine data from
its public manual and inspection of its NC output. Additional motion
types need a separate safety rule and pinning tests. Existing machine
files remain valid and refuse Side Burn until they state `side`.

### Bore fixture and editor coverage

**Decided:** Refresh the Linux bore path pin for the current imported
6,228-facet fixture. Pin the mesh size and exact cutting levels. Keep
the verification, fallback, and time-budget checks. Pin `Code side` by
its literal label in the existing machine editor test.

**Why:** PR #2904 replaced the bore fixture. Its old Linux path counts
describe the previous mesh. The explicit UI label assertion does not
depend on the production code-role list.

**Dropped:** Do not change the production planner to recover old fixture
counts. Do not remove the exact path pin or weaken the safety checks.

### Aligned-setup sinker test: the refusal names the missing code

**Decided:** Change the expected refusal text of
`sinker_electrode_burn_matches_baked_and_side_burn_stays_refused`
(`crates/app/tests/setup_align_non_mill.rs`). The fixture dialect
`SINKER EDM SYNTHETIC DIALECT (FIXTURE)` states no `edm.codes.side`.
The post still refuses its Side Burn and writes no file. The refusal now
names the missing code: "states no edm.codes.side". The test also
asserts that the refusal does not name `edm.codes.depth`, so the plain
burn SB1 in the same program still posts.

**Why:** The old text "a Sinker Side Burn moves the electrode sideways"
described a post that wrote no lateral move at all. This PR replaces
that refusal with one that names the machine data to add. The test's
meaning stays: a machine without a lateral servo template refuses the
Side Burn by name. The straight burn half of the test (the aligned and
baked programs are equal) is unchanged and passes.

**Dropped:** Do not add `edm.codes.side` to the fixture dialect. That
would make the test post a Side Burn and drop the pin that a dialect
without the template refuses it. Do not weaken the assert to "any
refusal".

## #3002 - Scale the post output budget

**Chosen:** Set the output line budget to `max(100_000, 16 * records + 1_024)`.
Use saturating arithmetic and cap the budget at `u32::MAX` so the JavaScript counter remains exact.
Apply one budget to the complete post run, across all hooks and operations.
Initialize it before the user script loads and give it the first operation name.
Update the operation name from the current properties as the engine processes the stream.
Report the limit, the attempted line count, and the operation when output exceeds the budget.

Keep the emitter count private to the host closure.
Keep the refusal latched in Rust so a script cannot hide an exceeded budget by catching the exception.
Check the output buffer separately so direct buffer writes also cause a refusal.
Move the existing output pull helper to `js_host` to keep `js.rs` below 400 lines.
This move does not change the output format.

**Why:** The fixed 100,000-line limit refuses valid Tormach programs whose operations contain more than 100,000 moves.
The input record count gives larger programs a larger finite budget.
The minimum preserves the existing allowance for small programs.
The additional allowance covers headers, tool changes, and records that emit several lines.
The diagnostics identify the operation and the exhausted allowance.

**Dropped:** Unbounded output removes the guard against a runaway script.
A much larger fixed limit still has no relation to the input and permits excessive output for small programs.
Posting each operation separately does not help an operation that exceeds the old limit by itself.
Splitting toolpaths or changing their cutting parameters changes the user's machining plan to satisfy a post implementation limit.
